evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-knowledge-wiki — DeepSeek Harness 知识库插件

把 Word / PPT / Excel / PDF（文字版与扫描版）等资料整理成**适合大模型阅读、学习的形式**，
存放在**固定、可命名、可导出、可持续修订**的知识库中；deepseek 通过一组 `kb_*` 工具
随时调用知识库内容进行问答、推理、整理、课件与文档制作等工作。

## 能力

| 工具 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `kb_import` | 导入文件或目录（.docx / .doc 自动转换 / .pptx / .xlsx / .xlsm / .pdf / .md / .txt / .epub / .mobi / .azw3，扫描版 PDF 自动逐页 OCR 中文，自动识别文字层损坏页并只对问题页 OCR，文字层双栏页自动重排；Word OMML 公式转 LaTeX；Excel 按工作表转 Markdown 表格；.txt 自动识别 UTF-8/UTF-16/GBK；MOBI/AZW3 自动经 Calibre 转 EPUB）。旧版 .doc/.ppt 与 MOBI/AZW3 一律在后台任务中转换；正在导入中的同名文档自动跳过。**导入前自动查重**：同库重合跳过、跨库重合默认跳过并报告；同库同标准号不同年份/阶段（多版本）默认暂停并提示，加 `allowSameNumber: true` 确认后仍可入库（见下文）；标准/书籍正文/封面优先，其他资料只用文件名；扫描页 OCR 前默认做水印净化（`watermark=auto/off/strong`）；`path` 是 kbpack 包（.zip）时自动路由到 `kb_import_package` |
| `kb_import_package` | 导入 kbpack 知识库包（`kb_export format=zip` 产出的 `.zip`，带 `manifest.json`）：安全校验（坏包/路径穿越/符号链接/版本过高拒绝）、同 id 相同内容幂等跳过、同 id 不同内容另存新 id、同标准号不同 id 走导入查重；同名库**不静默写入**，返回 `merge` / `rename` / `replace` 三选一（replace 需 `confirm:"replace"`），`dryRun=true` 只预演；包内 `*Source=manual` 字段不覆盖目标库人工值 |
| `kb_reparse` | 从库内 `sources/` 重新解析文档（无需重新上传），用于 OCR/解析器升级后刷新旧管线产物；`doc` 单个、`all=true` 批量，支持 `forceOcr`、`forceOcrPages`/`skipOcrPages`、后台任务 |
| `kb_list` | 列出知识库 / 知识库内文档与状态（旧管线/已修订/文字层损坏/OCR 低置信会标注），每条带一行摘要与标签；省略 `kb` 时只列本会话范围内的库；默认最多 50 条，支持 `limit/offset/query/status/kind` 分页过滤（`kind=note` 只看笔记、`kind=source` 只看资料）；本库有维护规范时会提示 |
| `kb_query` | 全文检索（纯文本优先 FTS5/BM25 条款索引，正则/索引不可用时回退 ripgrep；中文短语直接搜；标准号自动兼容 GBT=GB/T=GB_T=GB∕T 与年份分隔符变体）；按标题/标题行/命中密度/更新时间排序，每文档默认 5 条；`kb="*"` 跨库检索；限定模式下省略 `kb` 检索范围内全部库；命中项带 part、页码、条款与笔记类型；返回结构化 `sources`（含深链）供界面引用 |
| `kb_read` | 按分块精读、读大纲、读整篇；大纲条目带页码/部分，读取时返回页码范围与结构化 `sources`；支持虚拟页 `doc="schema"`（维护规范）、`doc="index"`（内容索引）、`doc="log"`（操作日志），按 part 分页读取 |
| `kb_view` | 查看原始页面图片（PDF 按页渲染；Word/PPT/EPUB/MOBI 提取内嵌图）——公式、原理图、电路图专用 |
| `kb_edit` | 精确替换修订（持续修改完善）；`doc="schema"` 可修订该库维护规范（index/log 自动维护，不能编辑） |
| `kb_describe` | 给文档写一行摘要与标签（编目）：摘要会显示在 `kb_list` 与 `index.md`，并作为摘要行进入 FTS 索引（只在摘要里的词也能被 `kb_query` 命中），重解析/重导入不会覆盖模型写的摘要；存量文档可 `all=true` + `auto=true` 批量回填缺失摘要（抽取式，不递增版本号，`limit` 分批） |
| `kb_retitle` | 修正标题：单篇传 `doc`（默认按 `cleanTitle` 去掉站点域名、`GB_T`、序号、span 残留等噪声），批量传 `all=true`（默认 `dryRun=true` 只预览，确认后 `dryRun=false` 应用）；加 `standardPrefix=true` 把有标准号的资料统一成「标准号 + 名称」；会重建合并版首行标题、保留历史、版本+1 |
| `kb_trust` | 标注来源可信度：`high`（已发布现行标准、正式教材）/ `medium`（企业文件、培训资料、报批稿）/ `low`（草案、征求意见稿、已废止标准）/ `unknown`（清除）；支持单篇、`docs` 列表、`all=true` + `query`/`stage` 过滤（批量默认 dryRun）。检索会优先高可信、标注低可信并提醒用户 |
| `kb_lint` | 机械体检：导入失败、旧管线、文字层损坏/OCR 低置信、内容重复、同标准号同期同阶段重复、同号多版本、正文完整性/文件名与封面不一致、未编目、笔记无来源、续/修订版提示、无入链笔记、临时/锁文件（`~$*`、`.~lock.*`、`Thumbs.db`/`desktop.ini`/`.DS_Store`）、缺 schema；输出分组问题与建议动作（`kb_reparse`/`kb_describe`/`kb_remove`/`kb_edit`）；限定模式下省略 `kb` 逐库体检 |
| `kb_edit_batch` | 批量精确修订（事务语义）：一次提交 1–50 条 `{doc, old_string, new_string, replaceAll?}`，**先全部校验再写入**；任一条失败整批不改并回滚已写分块；`dryRun=true` 只校验。适合“一次改 10–15 页”的跨文档维护；同一文档一批只允许一条编辑 |
| `kb_snapshot` | 库级快照：把 `kb.json`、`schema/index/log`、派生 `markdown/`（可选 `sources/`）打包到知识库 `snapshots/`，用于批量编辑/重解析前留档；`list=true` 列出已有快照 |
| `kb_snapshot_restore` | 从快照恢复：`list=true` 列快照，`snapshot`/`latest` 选择；默认 `dryRun=true` 只预演新增/移除/变更篇数，`dryRun=false` 才写入；恢复前自动留 `before-restore` 快照，`prune=true` 时快照外文档的 markdown/sources 移到 `trash-restore/`；重建索引与 FTS 并写 log |
| `kb_add_note` | 写入编译页/笔记（单篇上限 2MB）：`kind=summary/entity/concept/topic/note`、`tags`、`sources`（docId#页码 或 [[标题]]）；**同一标题再次调用=更新同一篇**（版本+1、保留历史），不要用「续」「修订版」另起新页 |
| `kb_remove` | 删除文档（默认软删除，可用 `kb_restore` 恢复；`soft=false` 永久删除）或整个知识库（删整库需显式 `kb` + `removeKb=true` 且 `confirm` 逐字等于知识库名称） |
| `kb_restore` | 恢复软删除文档（不带 `version`）或恢复历史版本（`version=N`，来自 `kb_history`） |
| `kb_history` | 列出文档保存过的历史版本（覆盖导入/重解析/编辑前的快照，最多 10 个） |
| `kb_export` | 导出 md（单文件）/ jsonl（分块，RAG 用；`chunkSize`/`chunkOverlap` 可切 RAG 小块）/ zip（完整包，内置 JSZip 打包、不依赖系统命令；带 `manifest.json` = kbpack/v1，可被 `kb_import_package` 还原；`docIds` 可只导出选中资料）/ **vault**（Obsidian Vault：`index.md` + `wiki/` 笔记与资料页 + `[[双链]]`，`includeSources=true` 时带 `raw/`） |
| `kb_rename` | 重命名知识库（`kb` 必填，须在本会话范围内） |

大文件（如整本扫描书）导入自动转为**后台任务**，与内置 `job_list` / `job_output` 联动查看进度；
取消后台任务会在 `job_output` 中显示为 cancelled。后台任务会写逐文件统计：
**只要有文件失败，任务状态就是 `failed`（详情写明“部分失败：成功 X，失败 Y”）**，不再把部分失败显示成完成。
长任务每 60 秒刷新一次 `heartbeatAt`（不改文档 `updatedAt`）；进程崩溃后，残留的 `.lock`
带 owner PID，下一个操作可在 PID 消失且锁超过 60 秒时快速回收，不必等满 30 分钟。

**旧版 .doc 自动转换**：Windows 用本机 Microsoft Word（COM 自动化，无对话框、禁宏）；
macOS 用自带 `textutil`；Linux 可用 LibreOffice。未装任何转换工具时会给出明确提示。

## 知识库存储结构（默认 `~/.dsh/knowledge/<知识库名>/`）

```
kb.json                    清单：文档列表（id/标题/类型/页数/大纲/版本/状态/
                           sha256/解析管线版本/contentSource/OCR 元数据/
                           summary·tags·笔记 kind/sources/linksOut）
schema.md                  维护规范（每库可定制；建库导入时写入模板）
index.md                   内容索引（清单自动渲染：笔记在前、资料在后，每条一行摘要）
log.md                     操作流水（只追加：ingest/edit/note/describe/remove/restore…）
sources/<docId><ext>       原始文件（逐字节保留）
markdown/<docId>/<docId>.md   合并版（整篇通读）
markdown/<docId>/parts/NNNN.md 分块版（检索、精读、RAG）
markdown/<docId>/parts/index.json 分块索引（合并版行号 → part/页码）
markdown/<docId>/pages.json   逐页质量（文字层/OCR、损坏标记、置信度）
exports/                   导出产物
```

- **知识库名称**：`kb_import` 的 `kb` 参数决定（可含中文），不存在即创建。
- **持续修改**：同名文件且内容未变 = **跳过不重跑**（返回 `skippedUnchanged`）；内容变化
  或 `forceReparse`/`kb_reparse` 时原位更新（版本号 +1）。`kb_edit` 精确替换并标记
  `edited=true`；`kb_add_note` 写编译页（同标题再次调用=更新该笔记）。清单会记录每个文档的 `sourcePath`：**同一路径**重复导入是原位更新，
  不同目录下的同名文件（如 `A/通知.pdf` 与 `B/通知.pdf`）会另建文档，不会互相覆盖。
  旧版本清单没有 `sourcePath` 的条目无法追溯来源，首次重导仍按原位更新，并在导入结果的
  warnings 里提示一次；担心覆盖时请先备份或导入到新库，重导一次后就会记录来源路径。
- **导出**：md 适合直接上传对话类产品（目录带摘要，笔记带 YAML frontmatter）；jsonl 适合 RAG 管道；
  zip 是完整可迁移包（含 README、`index.md`/`schema.md`/`log.md` 与全部 markdown，
  `includeSources=true` 时含原始文件）。
  zip 用 `generateNodeStream` **流式写盘**，不会把整包（含原始文件）先读进内存；
  导出清单剥离本机 `sourcePath`，失败条目整条略过。

## 知识库工作台（0.20.4）

插件在 web profile 下提供 `/kb/` 工作台（可通过配置 `uiEnabled: false` 关闭）：

- 总览：库卡片、简介、文档/笔记/页数/字数、类型与可信度分布；
- 新建知识库、编辑简介/标签、重命名、归档（含非空库，移动到 `.trash/`）；
- 回收站：列出归档库，支持恢复（原名冲突时可改名恢复）与彻底删除（需逐字输入库名确认，删除后磁盘文件不可恢复）；
- 库详情：概览 / 资料 / 笔记 / 日志 / 设置 / 标准更新；
- API：`GET /kb/api/status|kbs|kbs/:name|kbs/:name/docs|...`。

打开方式：在浏览器访问 `http://127.0.0.1:<dsh-web-port>/kb/`（端口见 `dsh web` 启动行）。

工作台支持直接在浏览器里上传资料：选文件 / 选目录 / 拖拽文件 → 逐个上传（并发 2）→ 后台导入；
目标库可在上传前切换；导入标题自动按 `cleanTitle` 去掉站点域名、`GB_T`/序号等噪声；逐文件进度与报告可见，
失败可重试。扫描件可选 OCR 精度（best 更准 / fast 更快）与「强制 OCR」（文字层损坏时）。批次临时目录在
导入成功后删除、失败保留 24 小时供排查（过期批次在新建批次时清扫）。单文件与单批次上限见配置
`uiMaxUploadBytes` / `uiMaxBatchFiles`。

- 上传/导入会自动跳过 Office 所有者文件（`~$…`）、LibreOffice 锁文件（`.~lock.…`）与
  `Thumbs.db` / `desktop.ini` / `.DS_Store` 等系统垃圾文件，并在上传面板与导入结果里报告
  「已跳过 N 个临时/锁文件」；普通 `.tmp` 文件不跳过。

概览页/库详情页「导入知识库包」：选择 `.zip` 上传后先预检（同名库返回 merge/rename/replace 三选一），
确认后后台导入；「导出知识库」支持正文包 / 完整包 / Markdown，后台生成后在弹窗内下载。

「标准更新」面板（库详情 tab）：读取 `.std-check.json` 的上次检查时间、缓存有效期（TTL 7 天）
与待下载数（有新版 / 草案转正 / 可补下载）；支持仅检查 / 检查并下载 / 补下载 / 强制全查 / 本轮上限，运行中可取消（当前正在处理的标准完成后停止，之后不再发起新的下载）；新增「按标准号补下载」：输入编号先检索并校验站点确认页（防串档）与金币，确认后再下载并导入；
下载前必须勾选金币确认（每个标准约 6 金币，VIP 免金币）；`bzCookie` 只在状态里显示“已配置 / 未配置”，
不会回传给浏览器。

当前版本仍不支持合并知识库；后续版本再加入。

### 实现偏差 / 已知限制（0.20.4–0.22.0）

- 拖拽只接收**文件**，不做拖拽文件夹递归；整理整个目录请用「选择目录」。
- 资料列表沿用按标题排序，不支持按更新时间排序；导入完成在弹窗内直接给出逐文件结果。
- 失败批次仅用于排查：没有删除或重试**失败批次**的 API（`DELETE` 只接受未开始导入的 open 批次），
  目录保留至清扫；重试是客户端用本地失败文件重新上传。
- 批次 24 小时过期由「创建批次」触发清扫（create-triggered），不是后台定时任务。
- `refreshKbIndex` 仍留在 `lib/import-job.js` 的导入收尾里，尚未拆成独立模块。
- UI 没有真实浏览器 DOM 测试：资料工具栏（搜索防抖/输入法/跳页/清除/焦点）用 fake DOM 单测
  （`test/ui-docs-controls.test.mjs`），胶囊用 `node:vm` 跑 `lib/client.js`；样式、真实焦点顺序与
  布局仍需手工验收，另有 `scripts/check-ui.mjs` 的语法门禁。
- 范围只约束 `kb_*` 工具：工作台 HTTP API 与 UI 不受范围影响（范围不是权限边界）。
- `kb_edit_batch` / `kb_add_note` 为单库策略：范围有多库时必须显式 `kb`，不做跨库事务。
- 切换范围会改写一次 system prompt 前缀（同一范围下前缀稳定）；范围变更在下一轮模型步生效。
- `restoreKb` / `removeKbDir` 未做范围同步；失效库名由读取时清理（prune）兜底。
- 胶囊只注册在 `conversation.input.left`；`conversation.session.header.utilities` 未接入。

## 0.25.0 回收站增强与 CI

回收站的已删除资料支持跨库批量彻底删除、搜索与排序，并可按天自动过期清理；仓库新增 GitHub Actions，
跑单元/构建门禁与真实浏览器 E2E。

### 跨库批量彻底删除

- 「已删除资料」多选不再限制同一个库：勾选来自不同库的条目后仍可点 **彻底删除所选**。确认弹窗要求逐字输入
  **`彻底删除 N 篇`**（N 为去重后的篇数）；有重复条目时按勾选数输入也接受。服务端做同样校验，不一致回
  `400 CONFIRM_REQUIRED`。
- 行内单篇彻底删除仍走本库接口，逐字输入 **库名** 确认；资料页「清空本库已删除资料」同样输入库名。本库单篇/清空
  与跨库批量一样在清单锁内复验已删除状态（`requireDeleted`）。
- 删除前对**全部条目做只读预检**：库不存在/已归档（原目录不在活跃库中）、资料不存在或不在回收站（例如在用资料）都会
  **整批拒绝**（`409 KB_NOT_FOUND` / `409 DOC_NOT_DELETED`，`details` 带首个问题条目），合法条目也不会被提前删掉。
- 逐篇删除都在清单锁内**复验仍在回收站**：预检后到真正删除前被恢复（或重新进入导入）的条目拒绝删除，按
  「彻底删除失败：文档已不在回收站」计入 `failed` 并继续；不会因为并发恢复回 500。
- 预检通过后逐篇 `removeDoc(..., { requireDeleted: true })`；单篇失败不中断其余条目，返回 `{purged, failed, byKb}`，失败项只带库、标题与固定文案
  「彻底删除失败」，不跨 API 回传本机路径。每篇写所属库日志 `remove`（detail「彻底删除（跨库批量）」），
  每个受影响库刷新一次 `index.md`；日志/索引是附属写入，失败不会回滚已完成的永久删除。
- 单次最多 **500 篇**；`items` 为空、缺 `kb`/`id`、超过上限都是 `400 INVALID_ARGS`。请求仍要求工作台写头与同源。
- HTTP：`POST /kb/api/trash/docs/purge`，body `{items:[{kb,id}], confirm}`。

### 搜索与排序

- 「已删除资料」工具条新增搜索：对**库名、标题、类型、来源文件**做大小写不敏感子串匹配；输入 **300ms 防抖**，
  `Enter` 立即搜索；输入法组合期间不发中间请求，`compositionend` 后立即应用并恢复焦点。
- 排序下拉：**删除时间（新→旧）**（默认）/ **删除时间（旧→新）** / **标题 A→Z** / **标题 Z→A** /
  **库名 A→Z** / **库名 Z→A**。切换排序立即请求并清空当前选择；未知/非法 `sort` 回落默认值，响应回显解析后的 `sort`。
- 过滤和排序在截断前对全量已删除资料执行：`total` 是命中总数，列表最多 **500** 篇，超出时显示「仅显示前 500 篇」。
- 搜索命中 0 篇显示「没有匹配的已删除资料」并提供 **清除搜索**；回收站本来为空则显示「没有已删除的资料」。
- 排序稳定性：删除时间相同或标题/库名相同时按「库名 + id」兜底；`deletedAt` 缺失/非法的行始终排在最后。
- HTTP：`GET /kb/api/trash/docs?query=&sort=`，响应额外返回归一化后的 `query` 与 `sort`。

### 自动过期清理

- 新配置 `trashRetentionDays`：默认 `0`（关闭），允许 **0–3650** 天。配置为 N 后，**工作台启动时**与
  **访问回收站时**（同一 `kbRoot` 每小时最多扫描一次，进程内节流）永久删除 `deletedAt` 超过 N 天的普通
  软删除资料。
- **跳过跨库移动留下的源库墓碑**（带 `movedTo` 的行）：撤销移动还要依赖它，即使过期也不自动清理，只能手动处理。
- 只扫描活跃（非归档、非合并）库；`deletedAt` 缺失或**不是 ISO 日期时间**（`YYYY-MM-DDTHH...`）的行无法判断年龄，
  跳过并计入 `skipped`；单篇删除失败（含锁内复验时已被恢复/重新导入）也计入 `skipped` 并继续处理其余条目。
- **单轮最多清理 500 篇**：达到上限即停止，返回 `capped=true`（表示可能还有未处理条目）；`byKb` 只统计实际删除的条目。
- 删除调用同样传 `requireDeleted: true`，锁内复验已删除状态；重新导入已软删除资料时 `markImporting` 会清除
  `deletedAt`/`deletedFromStatus`，导入期间不会被回收站列表、自动清理或批量彻底删除选中。
- 每篇写日志 `remove`（detail「自动清理（超过 N 天）」），有变动的库刷新一次 `index.md`；清理失败不影响工作台启动与
  回收站列举。目前只有配置入口，没有 UI 开关，也不是后台定时任务。

### CI / E2E

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 两个 job：
  - `unit`（ubuntu-latest）：`npm ci` → `npm run typecheck` → `npm test`。
  - `e2e`（macos-14，手动）：安装 `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.2` → 用临时 `DSH_HOME` 首次启动 `dsh web` 生成 profile →
    用 `install-to-machine.sh` 注册本仓库 → 安装 Playwright WebKit → 跑 `npm run test:e2e`；失败时上传
    `test/e2e/.artifacts`（目录以 `.` 开头，workflow 用 `include-hidden-files: true` 才会收集）。
  - `e2e-windows`（自托管 Windows，手动 `run_e2e_windows=true`）：`dsh.cmd` + Chromium，
    跑同一套件；需 runner 有可用 profile。
- 全新 CI profile 没有历史会话/模型凭据：胶囊用例自动 **skip** 并说明原因；工作台/回收站/搜索排序/移动/重试/预览用例
  照常执行，其余失败仍会让 job 红。
- 本地有真实 profile 与凭据时跑完整套件（当前 12 项；来源面板在 CLI 0.1.x 会 skip）；CI 为核心用例通过 + 胶囊/来源面板按宿主 skip（Office 可选预览在无转换引擎时也会 skip）。
- E2E 宿主兼容两种 profile 布局：优先 profile 自带 `node_modules`，否则使用 `profiles/node_modules` 共享目录；
  全新 CI profile 缺 `pnpm-lock.yaml` / `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 时跳过，不再启动失败。

### 已知限制（0.25.0）

- 自动清理对跨库移动墓碑不生效（`movedTo` 还要用于撤销移动），需要手动彻底删除；撤销移动后墓碑消失，才会进入普通清理范围。
- 跨库批量彻底删除仍逐篇调用 `removeDoc`，不是多库事务；单篇失败保留在 `failed` 里，需要人工重试。
- E2E 胶囊用例在全新 profile（无历史会话/模型凭据）自动 skip，CI 不覆盖胶囊交互。
- Chromium 下载在部分网络/CDN 不可用；E2E 套件优先 WebKit，只装 WebKit 也能跑。

## 0.33.0 知识库搬运闭环（kbpack）+ 快照恢复 + 水印净化

- **kbpack 导出**：`kb_export(format="zip")` 新增 `manifest.json`（`format=kbpack/v1`、`kbName`、

  符号链接/包格式版本过高拒绝；同 id 相同内容幂等跳过；同 id 不同内容另存新 docId；同标准号不同 id
  走现有 dedup；同 id 覆盖用 `replace` + `confirm:"replace"`，旧版进 history；包内 `title/summary/trust/standard`
  的 `*Source=manual` 不覆盖目标库人工值；导入后一次清单写入、重建索引/FTS、log 记 `import-package`。
- **同名库由用户选**：目标库已存在且未给 `mode` 时不写入，返回 `merge` / `rename`（自动加「(导入)」后缀）/
  `replace` 三选一；`dryRun=true` 只预演。
- **大包支持**：>256 MB 的包自动切换**流式 ZIP 解压**（不整包进内存）；真实「标准」库
  带 sources 的 **4.76 GB** 包实测 7.2 秒导入 913 篇 + 906 份原件（RSS 峰值约 218 MB）。
  单包上限 8 GB；正文包（913 篇约 58 MB）仍是最快迁移方式。
- **快照恢复**：新工具 `kb_snapshot_restore`，默认 dry-run；校验 zip/库名/schemaVersion；恢复前自动留
  `before-restore` 快照；`prune=true` 时快照外文档的 markdown/sources 移入 `trash-restore/`；log/schema/history
  不随快照回滚；恢复后重建索引与 FTS。
- **人工可信度可编辑**：资料列表每行可直接下拉改可信度（高/中/低/未标注），资料弹窗顶部也有同一选择；
  `PATCH metadata` 支持 `trust`，落盘 `trustSource=manual` 且不递增正文版本号；`kb_trust` 单篇/批量行为不变。
- **OCR 前水印净化**：扫描页渲染后按亮度直方图 + 深色核心邻域判定浅灰水印并置白，默认 `watermark=auto`
  （`off`/`strong` 可调）；只改 OCR 用的内存图，不写回原件；`kb_import`/`kb_reparse`/`kb_import_package`
  均可传 `watermark`。配套 `scripts/watermark-ab.mjs` 用真实文字层页做真值、叠加合成水印比较 CER：
  6 页平均 CER 干净 0.1221 → 加水印 0.1901 → 净化后 0.1490（报告 `docs/reports/2026-10-31-watermark-ab.md`）。

- **标题统一规则补强**：NB / DL / IEC/TS 等编号也能正确剥离，避免
  「NB 41004-2014 NB 41004-2014-征求意见稿」这类重复前缀；真实「标准」库只读预览从 369 篇降到 358 篇。
- **真实「标准」库预览（只读，未应用）**：911 篇中 **358 篇**标题会被统一成「编号 + 名称」。

## 0.31.3 标题统一、标准号搜索与扫描件摘要清洗

- **标准类资料标题统一成「标准号 + 名称」**：导入时自动补规范编号（如
  `GB/T 20001.10-2014 标准编写规则 第10部分：产品标准`，编号不含“（发布稿）”等阶段）；
  已有资料可用 `kb_retitle(all=true, standardPrefix=true)` 先预览、再 `dryRun=false` 应用。
  无标准号的资料标题不变。
- **资料列表搜索新增「标准号」**：搜索框现在匹配 名称 / 摘要 / 标准号 / 标签
  （例如直接搜 `GB/T 20001.10`）；仍是纯文本包含匹配，不做标准号归一。
- **扫描件自动摘要清洗**：摘要生成时跳过 OCR 页眉（ICS/CCS/标准号行）与乱码行
  （如 `ICS 01.120 ng oe a 00 ye aa …`），取第一段可读正文。已有摘要需
  `kb_reparse` 重解析或 `kb_describe` 覆盖后才会更新。
- **工作台「检索设置」入口移到侧栏**：内嵌模式顶栏会被隐藏，现在侧栏底部「检索设置」
  始终可见；顶栏按钮保留给独立页面。
- **修复一键准备下载模型 404**：HuggingFace 的 `model.onnx` 在 `onnx/` 子目录，0.31.2 的
  下载 URL 少了这一段；0.31.3 已修正（HuggingFace 失败自动换 hf-mirror）。
- **真机演练（0.31.3）**：`npm i` 安装可选依赖 5.9s / 297MB；从 hf-mirror 实际下载模型
  3 个文件 / 91MB；用下载后的模型嵌入 Q01 与 0.30 fastembed 向量余弦 **0.999999**。

## 0.31.2 工作台「检索设置」：语义开关与一键准备

**不用改 YAML 了**：工作台右上角新增「设置」按钮：

- 勾选「启用语义检索」**立即生效**（写入 `<kbRoot>/.semantic.json`，0600，覆盖配置里的
  `semanticSearch` 默认值），不加载模型；取消勾选后检索路径完全回到 0.30。
- 面板显示三行状态：**运行组件**（可选依赖是否可解析）、**模型**（3 个文件是否齐全）、
  **索引**（就绪篇数 / 缺失原因）。
- 未准备时出现「**一键准备（约 390MB）**」：勾选同意后后台执行
  ① `npm i --no-save --save-peer onnxruntime-node@^1.31.1 @huggingface/tokenizers@^0.2.0`（插件目录）；
  ② 下载 `model.onnx` / `tokenizer.json` / `tokenizer_config.json` 到
  `~/.dsh/tools/models/bge-small-zh-v1.5`（HuggingFace 失败自动回退 hf-mirror；
  可用 `SEMANTIC_MODEL_BASE_URL` 指定镜像或代理地址）。进度显示在面板里，完成后开开关即用。
- 终端入口仍保留：`npm run semantic:setup`（= 装依赖 + 下模型，已就绪时直接返回）。
- API：`GET/PUT /kb/api/semantic`、`POST /kb/api/semantic/prepare`（必须 `{confirm:true}`）。

**已知限制（0.31.2）**：自动准备需要 `npm` 在 PATH、约 390MB 磁盘与可用网络；准备任务不可中途取消
（完成后可关开关）；插件升级或 `npm install` 可能清掉可选依赖，重新打开面板点一次「一键准备」即可。

## 0.31.1 知识库路径自检与真实延迟复测

- **指定知识库目录更宽容**：`kbRoot` 现在支持 `~`、`~/`、Windows 的 `~\`、`$HOME`、`${HOME}`、
  `%USERPROFILE%`；启动时统一转成**绝对路径**（相对路径按启动目录落盘，避免运行中 cwd 变化换库）。
- **启动自检**：建目录 + 可写检查失败时不再静默——`GET /kb/api/status` 新增
  `kbRootOk` / `kbRootError`，插件日志也会记录原因；自检失败不阻塞其它功能加载。
- **真实嵌入延迟复测**：80 题真实模型 + 生产检索路径，开启语义后 **p95 58.2ms**（含查询嵌入 2.83ms、
  融合与两阶段页码 2.11ms），p50 42.4ms，远低于 120ms 门槛。方法见
  `docs/specs/2026-10-31-semantic-regression.md` 的 0.31.1 段。
- 行为无回退：语义层仍默认关闭；不装可选依赖/模型的用户不受影响。

## 0.31.0 可选语义层（默认关闭）

**做了什么**：把 0.30 评测里胜出的「文档级语义 RRF」做成可选层，接入 `kb_query` 与工作台
`/kb/api/search`：

- 排序 = B 的 boost 文档序 + 文档向量余弦序做 RRF（k=20）；**词面强命中**（标题命中 + 条款命中
  ≥2 个不同查询词 + `trust != low`）时把 B 的 top-1 锁回第一位——只影响排序，不改变召回集合；
- **两阶段页码**：dense 独有文档在文档内按查询词命中条款定位 `page/clause`；确实找不到时
  `page=null` 并在 `note` 里标注「N 篇语义命中未定位到页码」，不伪造页码；
- 索引 `<kb>/.index/doc-vectors.f32` + `doc-vectors.meta.json`（911 篇约 1.9MB），按 manifest 增量刷新；
  >100 篇首次启用走**后台进程**建索引（当次检索回退 B 并在 note 里说明）；
- `/kb/api/status` 暴露 `semantic: {enabled,indexReady,model,dim,docs,reason}`；工作台状态行在
  `engine=hybrid` 时显示「语义」；
- **语义画像可选 `summary` / `window`**：工作台「检索设置」→「语义画像」下拉即可切换，
  也可在 profile 配置 `semanticProfile`。默认 `window`：把全文按页切成 8 个窗口、分别嵌入后取质心
  （仍是一条向量/文档）；`summary` 是 600 字快画像（标准号+标题+标签+摘要+首条款）。
  80 题纯 dense 审计：当前 600 字 Recall@10 54.2%，窗口质心 65.0%、多窗口 max 71.7%；
  质心 MRR 从 0.282 提到 0.440，索引仍 1.9MB，但建索引约 8 倍时间。
  生产口径回归（B vs 语义）：window + pageGuard=8 的 Doc Recall 93.3%→96.7%、
  Page Recall 81.7%→83.3%、Page MRR 0.576→0.578；只调整 top-10 顺序，不增加返回 Token。
  summary 全面更差，不作为默认；语义默认仍关闭。
- **默认 `semanticSearch=off`**：关闭时行为与 0.30 完全一致（golden 对比测试逐字段校验），
  不加载模型、不读写向量索引。

**如何开启**

0.31.2 起：工作台右上角「设置」→ 勾选「启用语义检索」；未准备时先点「一键准备（约 390MB）」。
也可以手动三步：

1. 在插件目录装可选依赖（见下「打包策略」）；模型放 `~/.dsh/tools/models/bge-small-zh-v1.5/`；

# TeamHarness DeepSeek Harness adapter This adapter lets a stock DeepSeek Harness release load Controller-projected TeamHarness context and role-specific Skills, connect to the existing TeamHarness MCP server, and resume a caller-supplied DSH session without changing DSH itself. The managed Matrix bridge supplies one stable session ID per room and a deterministic message ID per Matrix event. This adapter is installed directly into the managed Worker's dedicated headless DSH profile. The runtime is experimental while it remains pinned to a DeepSeek Harness release candidate; the Controller-facing `deepseek-harness` runtime name and persisted state format are stable within AgentTeams. The smoke run is pinned to DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.1.1-rc.2` at commit `b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e`. Build that checkout first, then run: ```powershell pwsh -File plugins/teamharness/adapters/deepseek-harness/smoke.ps1 -DshRoot ../deepseek-harness-rc2 ``` The script uses a temporary `DSH_HOME`, installs this directory as a DSH bundle, boots both Worker and standalone compositions, verifies the prompt/Skill/MCP path, removes the bundle, and deletes the temporary home after a successful run. Additional live checks are documented in `deepseek-harness/README.md`. They cover a real model turn, Matrix text and file delivery, MinIO-backed session recovery, Controller-driven Pod replacement, and a real Team Leader/Worker scenario.

**AgentTeams is an open-source collaborative multi-agent runtime platform. It enables multiple Agents to collaborate in a controlled and auditable room, with full human visibility and intervention capabilities throughout the process.** Built on a **Manager-Workers architecture**, AgentTeams features a Manager that centrally orchestrates multiple Workers, focusing on collaboration scenarios between humans and Agents, as well as among Agents within enterprise environments. AgentTeams does not compete with other Agent runtimes. Instead of implementing Agent logic itself, it orchestrates and manages multiple Agent containers (including the Manager and numerous Workers). ## Key Features - 🧬 **Manager-Workers Architecture**: Eliminates the need for human oversight of individual Worker Claws by enabling Agents to manage other Agents. - 🤝 **Multi-Runtime Collaboration**: OpenClaw, QwenPaw, Hermes, and experimental DeepSeek Harness Workers coexist in the same IM room. Use the runtime that best fits each role while keeping collaboration visible in Matrix. - 📦 **MinIO Shared File System**: Introduces a shared file system for inter-Agent information exchange, significantly reducing token consumption in multi-Agent collaboration scenarios. - 🔐 **Higress AI Gateway**: Centralizes traffic management and mitigates credential-related risks, alleviating user concerns about security vulnerabilities in the native Lobster framework. - ☎️ **Element IM Client + Tuwunel IM Server (both Matrix protocol-based)**: Eliminating DingTalk/Lark integration overhead and enterprise approval workflows. Enables rapid user onboarding to experience the "delight" of model services within an IM environment, while maintaining compatibility with native OpenClaw IM integration. - 🧬 **Integrate** [AgentLoop](https://www.aliyun.com/product/agentloop?spm=at.readme.0.0.0) ：Provides capabilities such as full-stack Agent observability and auditing, Agent evaluation and experimentation, and Agent asset management and continuous optimization. ## News - **2026-10-16**: [Release Notes](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/releases/tag/v1.2.5) — AgentTeams v1.2.5: strengthens coding-tool delegation, Worker configuration management, and in-place QwenPaw runtime upgrades; ships with Dashboard v1.3.1 by default; and fixes multiple issues in MCP registration, Matrix message collaboration, and Worker recovery. - **2026-09-20**: [Release Notes](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/releases/tag/v1.2.4) — AgentTeams v1.2.4: adds TeamHarness task state history, progress tracking, and completion notifications; upgrades to QwenPaw 2.2.1 and Dashboard v1.2.4.9; expands team permissions, auditing, and skill management; introduces the experimental DeepSeek Harness Worker; and improves Worker state persistence and installation reliability. - **2026-08-22**: [Release Notes](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/releases/tag/v1.2.3) — AgentTeams v1.2.3: makes long-running Project workflows visible and controllable through new Controller APIs, `agt` commands, and Dashboard v1.2.4; adds audited human interventions, Project history, and QwenPaw Worker checkpoints; promotes QwenPaw as the recommended local Manager and Worker runtime; and improves Skill recovery, Windows AppService startup, and runtime reliability. - **2026-08-08**: [Release Notes](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/releases/tag/v1.2.2) — AgentTeams v1.2.2: adds Manager-to-Worker custom Skill delivery with validation, storage upload, `Worker.spec.skills` assignment, and QwenPaw hot refresh and enablement without a restart; hardens Manager and Worker Skill loading; and ensures Team Leaders and Workers explicitly join Team Rooms after invitation. - **2026-08-06**: [Release Notes](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/releases/tag/v1.2.1) — AgentTeams v1.2.1: unifies the Manager and Worker runtime stack on QwenPaw 2.0.1, publishes the QwenPaw Worker multi-architecture image, strengthens atomic Matrix and TeamHarness task assignment and CoPaw-to-QwenPaw state migration, adds custom model vision and reasoning capability overrides, and improves Worker lifecycle and runtime management reliability. - **2026-07-30**: [Release Notes](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/releases/tag/v1.2.0) — AgentTeams v1.2.0 (stable): establishes AgentTeams naming and the final Team/Worker resource contracts end to end; adds the plugin platform, TeamHarness and WorkerFlow integrations, Matrix AppService and Human SSO, model-provider routing and LLM preflight, plus richer controller observability. Beta installation requires explicit opt-in, while the stable default remains v1.1.2. - **2026-05-27**: [Release Notes](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/releases/tag/v1.1.2) — AgentTeams v1.1.2: QwenPaw-first installer with keep-all upgrade flow, Team human coordinators and refreshed Team Leader coordination tools, Nacos remote skills with `sts-agentteams` / `ai-registry` STS scope, Worker CR-name decoupled from runtime name, controller reconcile metrics and graceful shutdown. - **2026-05-07**: [Release Notes](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/releases/tag/v1.1.1) | [Changelog](changelog/v1.1.1.md) — AgentTeams v1.1.1: declarative MCP on Worker/Manager/Team CRDs (breaking) and on Team Leader, custom `spec.env` for CRs, Token Plan + Qwen Cloud international + `qwen3.6-plus`, namespace-scoped controller RBAC, optional `SOUL.md` in Worker packages. - **2026-04-24**: [English](blog/agentteams-1.1.0-release.md) | [中文](blog/zh-cn/agentteams-1.1.0-release.md) — AgentTeams v1.1.0: Kubernetes-native control plane, Hermes autonomous coding agent runtime, 1.7 GB image shrink, agt CLI replaces shell scripts. - **2026-04-14**: [English](blog/agentteams-k8s-native-multi-agent-collaboration.md) | [中文](blog/zh-cn/agentteams-k8s-native-multi-agent-collaboration.zh-CN.md) — Deep dive: AgentTeams as a Kubernetes-native multi-agent collaboration orchestration system. - **2026-04-03**: [English](docs/usage/resource-management.md) | [中文](docs/zh-cn/usage/resource-management.md) — AgentTeams 1.0.9: Kubernetes-style declarative resource management (YAML for Worker, Team, Human); Worker Template Marketplace; Manager QwenPaw runtime; Nacos Skills Registry and more. - **2026-03-14**: [English](blog/agentteams-1.0.6-release.md) | [中文](blog/zh-cn/agentteams-1.0.6-release.md) — AgentTeams 1.0.6: enterprise-grade MCP Server management, zero credential exposure. - **2026-03-10**: [English](blog/agentteams-1.0.4-release.md) | [中文](blog/zh-cn/agentteams-1.0.4-release.md) — AgentTeams 1.0.4: QwenPaw (formerly CoPaw) Worker support, 80% less memory. - **2026-03-04**: [English](blog/agentteams-announcement.md) | [中文](blog/zh-cn/agentteams-announcement.md) — AgentTeams open sourced under its former name. ## Why AgentTeams - **Enterprise-Grade Security**: Worker Agents operate with consumer tokens only. Real credentials (API keys, GitHub PATs) stay in the gateway — Workers can't see them, and neither can attackers. - **Fully Private**: Matrix is a decentralized, open protocol. Host it yourself, federate with others if you want. No vendor lock-in, no data harvesting. - **Human-in-the-Loop by Default**: Every Matrix room includes you, the Manager, and the relevant Workers. Watch everything. Jump in anytime. No black boxes. - **Zero Configuration IM**: Built-in Matrix server means no bot applications, no API approvals, no waiting. Just open Element Web and start chatting. - **One Command Setup**: `curl | bash` and you're done — AI gateway, Matrix server, file storage, web client, and Manager Agent. - **Skills Ecosystem**: Workers pull from [skills.sh](https://skills.sh) (80,000+ community skills) on demand. Safe because Workers can't access real credentials. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites**: Docker Desktop (Windows/macOS) or Docker Engine (Linux). **Resources**: 2 CPU cores + 4 GB RAM minimum. For multiple Workers, 4 cores + 8 GB recommended. ### Install **macOS / Linux:** ```bash bash <(curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/main/install/agentteams-install.sh) ``` **Windows (PowerShell 7+ recommended):** ```powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force; $wc=New-Object Net.WebClient; $wc.Encoding=[Text.Encoding]::UTF8; iex $wc.DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/main/install/agentteams-install.ps1') ``` The installer walks you through: 1. Choose your LLM provider (OpenAI-compatible APIs supported) 2. Enter your API key 3. Select network mode (local-only or external access) 4. Wait for setup to complete ### Access Open http://127.0.0.1:18088 in your browser and log in to Element Web. The Manager will greet you and explain how to create your first Worker. **Mobile**: Use any Matrix client (Element, FluffyChat) and connect to your server address. **That's it.** No bot applications. No external services. Your AI team runs entirely on your machine. ## Upgrade ```bash # Upgrade to latest (preserves all data) bash <(curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/main/install/agentteams-install.sh) # Upgrade to specific version AGENTTEAMS_VERSION=v1.2.5 bash <(curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/main/install/agentteams-install.sh) ``` ## Uninstall **macOS / Linux:** ```bash bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/main/install/agentteams-install.sh) uninstall ``` **Windows (PowerShell):** ```powershell Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force; $wc=New-Object Net.WebClient; $wc.Encoding=[Text.Encoding]::UTF8; $s=$wc.DownloadString('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/agentscope-ai/AgentTeams/main/install/agentteams-install.ps1'); & ([scriptblock]::Create($s)) uninstall ``` This removes all AgentTeams containers (Manager, Workers, docker-proxy), Docker volume, network, env file, workspace directory, and install log. ## Install on Kubernetes (Helm) For shared / production deployments you can install AgentTeams on any Kubernetes cluster via the official Helm chart. The default profile bundles the Higress AI gateway, Tuwunel (Matrix), MinIO and the AgentTeams controller — no external dependencies required. The commands below provide a quick installation path. See the [Kubernetes Deployment Guide](docs/usage/deployment/kubernetes.md) for cluster planning, values files, model services, runtimes, persistence, Ingress, and operations. **Prerequisites** - Kubernetes 1.24+ (kind / minikube / k3s / managed K8s — all work) - Helm 3.7+ - A default StorageClass (for the Tuwunel + MinIO PVCs) **Install (OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible)** ```bash helm repo add higress.io https://higress.io/helm-charts helm repo update helm install agentteams higress.io/agentteams \ -n agentteams-system --create-namespace \ --render-subchart-notes \ --set credentials.llmApiKey= \ --set credentials.adminPassword= \ --set gateway.publicURL=http://localhost:18080 ``` For non-OpenAI providers that expose an OpenAI-compatible API, also set `llmBaseUrl`: ```bash helm install agentteams higress.io/agentteams \ -n agentteams-system --create-namespace \ --render-subchart-notes \ --set credentials.llmApiKey= \ --set credentials.llmBaseUrl=https://your-provider.example.com/v1 \ --set credentials.defaultModel=your-model-name \ --set credentials.adminPassword= \ --set gateway.publicURL=http://localhost:18080 ```
Using Qwen (通义千问) instead ```bash helm install agentteams higress.io/agentteams \ -n agentteams-system --create-namespace \ --render-subchart-notes \ --set credentials.llmApiKey= \ --set credentials.llmProvider=qwen \ --set credentials.defaultModel=qwen3.5-plus \ --set credentials.adminPassword= \ --set gateway.publicURL=http://localhost:18080 ```
| Value | Required | Description | |---|---|---| | `credentials.llmApiKey` | yes | API key for your LLM provider | | `gateway.publicURL` | yes | Public URL where users will reach Element Web (e.g. `http://localhost:18080` for port-forward, or `https://agentteams.example.com` for an Ingress) | | `credentials.adminPassword` | recommended | Matrix admin password; auto-generated if left empty (you'll have to read it back from the Secret) | | `credentials.llmProvider` | no | LLM provider name, defaults to `openai-compat` | | `credentials.defaultModel` | no | Default model, defaults to `gpt-5.4` | | `credentials.llmBaseUrl` | no | OpenAI-compatible base URL (e.g. `https://api.deepseek.com/v1`). Leave empty for official OpenAI API | | `preflight.llm.enabled` | no | Run an install/upgrade hook that validates the LLM API key, base URL, and model before the controller starts. Defaults to `true` | | `preflight.llm.strict` | no | Fail the Helm install/upgrade when the LLM preflight fails. Defaults to `true`; set to `false` to emit a warning and continue | | `preflight.llm.timeoutSeconds` | no | Per-request timeout for the LLM preflight HTTP probe. Defaults to `30` | | `preflight.llm.retries` | no | Retry count for transient LLM preflight failures such as rate limits and provider 5xx responses. Defaults to `2` | | `preflight.llm.activeDeadlineSeconds` | no | Kubernetes Job active deadline for the preflight hook. Defaults to `120` | | `preflight.llm.resources` | no | Optional Kubernetes resource requests/limits for the preflight hook container | | `manager.runtime` | no | Manager runtime: OpenClaw uses `openclaw` (default); CoPaw uses `qwenpaw` in the current chart, with `copaw` retained as a compatibility alias. Managers do not support Hermes or DeepSeek Harness | | `worker.defaultRuntime` | no | The chart provides default image values for `openclaw` (default), `copaw`, `hermes`, experimental `deepseek-harness`, and `openhuman`; the current CRD rejects an explicit `spec.runtime: openhuman`, and QwenPaw Workers require an explicit `spec.image` | Helm installs run an LLM preflight hook by default. The hook sends a minimal OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` request using `credentials.llmApiKey`, `credentials.llmBaseUrl`, and `credentials.defaultModel`; invalid keys, unreachable base URLs, unsupported models, quota errors, and provider outages fail the install before the controller starts. To bypass this check for restricted or offline clusters: ```bash helm install agentteams higress.io/agentteams \ -n agentteams-system --create-namespace \ --set credentials.llmApiKey= \ --set credentials.adminPassword= \ --set gateway.publicURL=http://localhost:18080 \ --set preflight.llm.enabled=false ```
Using alternative runtimes (CoPaw Manager + Hermes Workers) ```bash helm install agentteams higress.io/agentteams \ -n agentteams-system --create-namespace --devel \ --set manager.runtime=qwenpaw \ --set manager.image.repository=higress-registry.cn-hangzhou.cr.aliyuncs.com/agentteams/agentteams-manager-qwenpaw \ --set worker.defaultRuntime=hermes \ --set credentials.llmApiKey= \ --set credentials.llmBaseUrl=https://your-provider.example.com/v1 \ --set credentials.defaultModel=your-model-name \ --set credentials.adminPassword= \ --set gateway.publicURL=http://localhost:18080 ``` When selecting the CoPaw Manager, set both `manager.runtime=qwenpaw` and the `agentteams-manager-qwenpaw` image. Configure Worker default images through `worker.defaultImage.`.
**Multi-Region Image Registry** Images point to the China region by default. When deploying outside China, use a nearby registry for faster pulls: | Region | Registry | |---|---| | China (default) | `higress-registry.cn-hangzhou.cr.aliyuncs.com/higress` | | North America | `higress-registry.us-west-1.cr.aliyuncs.com/higress` | | Southeast Asia | `higress-registry.ap-southeast-7.cr.aliyuncs.com/higress` | `global.imageRegistry` affects only subcharts that consume that global value. The Controller, Manager, Workers, Tuwunel, MinIO, and Element Web use their own complete `image.repository` values. Override every relevant image in a values file when switching regions or using a private registry. See the [Kubernetes Deployment Guide](docs/usage/deployment/kubernetes.md) and [`helm/agentteams/values.yaml`](helm/agentteams/values.yaml) for the complete configuration. **Access** For a temporary local admin session, forward the Higress Gateway: ```bash kubectl port-forward -n agentteams-system svc/higress-gateway 18080:80 ``` Then open http://localhost:18080 and log in to Element Web. The port-forward ends when the command exits and is not suitable for shared access. For company or Internet access, expose only `svc/higress-gateway` through an HTTPS Ingress or LoadBalancer. `gateway.publicURL` is written into the Element Web configuration as its Matrix homeserver URL, so it must exactly match the public origin that users open (for example, `https://agentteams.example.com`). 1. Point the public DNS name at your Ingress controller or load balancer. 2. Provision a TLS certificate Secret in `agentteams-system`. 3. Set the same origin on the Helm release: ```bash helm upgrade agentteams higress.io/agentteams \ -n agentteams-system --reuse-values \ --set gateway.publicURL=https://agentteams.example.com ``` 4. Route that host to the Higress Gateway. This generic example assumes an NGINX IngressClass and an existing `agentteams-tls` Secret; replace both to match your cluster: ```yaml apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1 kind: Ingress metadata: name: agentteams namespace: agentteams-system spec: ingressClassName: nginx tls: - hosts: - agentteams.example.com secretName: agentteams-tls rules: - host: agentteams.example.com http: paths: - path: / pathType: Prefix backend: service: name: higress-gateway port: number: 80 ``` Verify both the web entry point and Matrix routing after DNS and TLS are ready: ```bash curl -fsSI https://agentteams.example.com/ curl -fsS https://agentteams.example.com/_matrix/client/versions ``` Keep the controller API, Tuwunel, MinIO, and the Higress Console private unless you apply separate authentication and network policy. Use HTTPS for shared access because Matrix login credentials and access tokens pass through this endpoint. A `LoadBalancer` Service can replace the Ingress, but the DNS, TLS, and `gateway.publicURL` requirements remain the same. **Upgrade** ```bash helm repo update helm upgrade agentteams higress.io/agentteams -n agentteams-system --reuse-values ``` **Uninstall** ```bash helm uninstall agentteams -n agentteams-system kubectl delete namespace agentteams-system ``` For the Kubernetes-native architecture (CRDs, controller, declarative `Worker` / `Team` / `Human` resources), see [docs/design/k8s-native-orchestration.md](docs/design/k8s-native-orchestration.md). ## How It Works ### Manager as Your AI Chief of Staff ``` You: Create a Worker named alice for frontend development Manager: Done. Worker alice is ready. Room: Worker: Alice Tell alice what to build. You: @alice implement a login page with React Alice: On it... [a few minutes later] Done. PR submitted: https://github.com/xxx/pull/1 ```

    

① Manager creates a Worker and assigns tasks                    ② You can also direct Workers directly in the room

### Security Model ``` Worker (consumer token only) → Higress AI Gateway (holds real API keys, GitHub PAT) → LLM API / GitHub API / MCP Servers ``` Workers see only their consumer token. The gateway handles all real credentials. The Manager knows what Workers are doing but never touches the actual keys. ### Human in the Loop Every Matrix Room includes you, the Manager, and relevant Workers: ``` You: @bob wait, change the password rule to minimum 8 chars Bob: Got it, updated. Alice: Frontend validation updated too. ``` No hidden agent-to-agent calls. Everything is visible and intervenable. ## Multi-Runtime Collaboration AgentTeams provides multiple Worker runtime families that can **coexist in the same IM room**, collaborating on tasks together: - **OpenClaw** (Node.js) — General-purpose agent with rich skills ecosystem, ideal for task orchestration and tool calling - **QwenPaw** (Python) — Lightweight runtime, suited for browser automation and quick tasks - **Hermes** ([hermes-agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)) — Autonomous coding agent with terminal sandbox, self-improving skills, and persistent memory - **DeepSeek Harness** (experimental) — Headless coding agent with room-scoped session continuation, Matrix file exchange, and restart recovery; currently pinned to a tested DSH release candidate The `copaw` value remains available for compatibility with existing CoPaw Workers; the current CRD accepts both `copaw` and `qwenpaw`. Each runtime excels at different tasks. A common pattern is to use deterministic agents (OpenClaw/QwenPaw) as Leaders to decompose and assign work, and Hermes Workers for autonomous code execution. All runtimes communicate through Matrix rooms—fully visible and fully intervenable. ```bash # Switch any worker's runtime in place agt update worker --runtime hermes ``` ## Architecture ``` ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ agentteams-controller │ │ Higress │ Tuwunel │ MinIO │ Element Web │ └──────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘ │ Matrix + HTTP Files ┌──────────────────┴──────────┐ │ agentteams-manager-agent │ │ Manager (OpenClaw/ │ │ QwenPaw) │ └──────────────────┬──────────┘ │ ┌──────────────────┼────────────────────────────┐ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ Worker Alice Worker Bob Worker Charlie (OpenClaw) (QwenPaw) (Hermes) ``` | Component | Role | |-----------|------| | agentteams-controller | Kubernetes-native control plane, reconciles Worker/Team/Manager CRs | | Higress AI Gateway | LLM proxy, MCP Server hosting, credential management | | Tuwunel (Matrix) | Self-hosted IM server for all Agent + Human communication | | Element Web | Browser client, zero setup | | MinIO | Centralized file storage, Workers are stateless | ## AgentTeams vs OpenClaw Native | | OpenClaw Native | AgentTeams | |---|---|---| | Deployment | Single process | Distributed containers | | Agent creation | Manual config + restart | Conversational | | Credentials | Each agent holds real keys | Workers only hold consumer tokens | | Human visibility | Optional | Built-in evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-capability-router

> 状态：v0.3.0。v0.2.0 的检查点已在 DSH Desktop 0.2.1 上做过 A/B 对照（[DESIGN.md](./DESIGN.md) 第十节）；v0.3.0 加了专家包、规则匹配、角色注入与技能目录收窄。
> 设计取舍、宿主 API 实测记录、踩过的坑都在 [DESIGN.md](./DESIGN.md)。

本机自研的 DSH 插件。解决两个问题：**agent 拿到一句含糊的需求就直接开干**，以及**技能装多了挑不准**。

## 仓库结构

```text
lib/index.js           插件本体：挂载、两处注入、自检技能
lib/experts.js         专家包发现与校验（内层覆盖外层）
lib/router.js          规则匹配器：一句话判给哪个专家
lib/narrow.js          技能目录收窄（冒名接管，仍可按名加载）
lib/yaml.js            YAML 子集解析器（为了零依赖手写的）
experts/<id>/          专家包：expert.yml + role.md，首批 5 个
test/smoke.mjs         假 ctx 跑 apply，九场景
test/experts.mjs       解析器与扫描器，九场景
test/router.mjs        匹配打分与三种结论，九场景
test/narrow.mjs        收窄语义（含仍可按名加载），八场景
test/route.mjs         集成：一句话进来后模型看到什么变了
tools/match.mjs        匹配器验收集（a 回归 / b 口语 / c 探针）
tools/dump-session.mjs 把 DSH 的多帧 zstd 会话日志 dump 成可读 JSONL
DESIGN.md              设计文档：为什么这么做、宿主 API 实测、坑
README.md              本文件
```

`tools/dump-session.mjs` 解决一个很具体的问题：`~/.dsh/sessions/<slug>/session-<id>/session.v4.jsonl.zstd` 是**多帧 zstd 串联**，`zlib.zstdDecompressSync` 只解第一帧（通常几百字节）。这个工具按帧头 magic 切片逐帧解压再拼接，并给出事件与工具调用统计：

```bash
node tools/dump-session.mjs ~/.dsh/sessions/<slug>/session-<id> --stats
node tools/dump-session.mjs ~/.dsh/sessions/<slug>/session-<id> --out dump.jsonl
```


## 两个注入通道

同一份协议，用两种方式送到模型面前，区别在**距离**。

| | 长期原则段 | 当轮检查点 |
|---|---|---|
| 机制 | `ctx.systemPrompt.section()` | `ctx.on("agent/pre-step")` |
| 位置 | 系统提示后半段 | 紧跟用户那句话 |
| 距离 | 中间隔着几十 KB 项目规则 | 零距离 |
| 频率 | 常驻 | 每条用户消息一次 |
| 作用 | 背景设定 | 触发动作 |

只有后者会真正改变行为。前者存在的意义是：模型在长对话里回头翻上下文时，还能找到依据。

检查点的做法是在 `agent/pre-step` 里往 `decision.messages` 末尾追加一条 user 消息：

```js
{
  role: "user",
  id: randomUUID(),
  content: [{ type: "text", text: HINT_TEXT }],
  source: { kind: "capability-router-hint", form: "notice", forPrompt: <该用户消息的 id> }
}
```

`forPrompt` 用来去重——同一条用户消息只注入一次，工具调用来回多少步都不重复。识别"真人说的话"靠 `source.kind === "user"`，因为 `agent-instructions`、`runtime-context`、`skill-catalog`、`time-context` 也都是 user 角色。

## 检查点写了什么

```text
【能力路由 · 当轮检查】

先归类用户这句话，再决定动作：

- 提问（要答案）：直接答。不要顺手改代码，不要先跑一堆命令验证。
- 命令（要动作）：有一个会改变实现方向的黑洞就问，一次只问一个，附上推荐答案；没有就开工。
- 报告（是继续）：接着做，别重新评估已经定下的事。

开工前扫一眼技能目录：对口就加载完整指令再动手；不对口就说「我手上没有对应能力」并说缺什么。
```

## 专家包

一个目录就是一个专家：`expert.yml` 说它是谁、什么话该找它，`role.md` 是命中后注入的角色提示词。

```text
<包内>/experts/<id>/                          随插件发布，改它要动源码
<DSH_HOME>/capability-router/experts/<id>/    用户自建或覆盖，同名 id 以内层为准
  expert.yml
  role.md
  skills/        可选，专家自带的技能
```

```yaml
name: 前端工程师
description: 界面、交互、样式、浏览器行为
triggers: [界面, 样式, 前端, 组件, 布局, 交互, 渲染, 动画, 响应式, 页面, CSS, HTML, React, Vue, 浏览器]
skills: [frontend-design, playwright, canvas-design, theme-factory, prototype]
tools: []          # 空 = 用全部
```

`expert.yml` 用的是 YAML 子集：扁平 key、标量、一维列表（`[a, b]` 或缩进 `- a`），不支持多行块和嵌套——要长文本写进 `role.md`。

自带五个：

| id | 名字 | 覆盖什么 |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend` | 前端工程师 | 界面、样式、交互、浏览器行为 |
| `backend` | 后端工程师 | 接口、数据模型、并发、服务边界 |
| `docs` | 文档与写作 | 文档、方案、汇报、对外文字 |
| `debug` | 排障工程师 | 报错、崩溃、不生效、性能 |
| `data` | 数据与办公 | 表格、报表、演示文稿、PDF |

`name`、`description`、`triggers` 任一为空，这个专家会被判无效并进告警；缺 `role.md` 只告警（命中后只注入技能集）。内层同名包坏了不会退回旧版本，那个 id 直接消失——少一个专家比用错一个专家好。

**当前版本只做到「读得出、列得全」**：扫描结果出现在 `capability-router` 自检技能里，匹配与收窄还没接上。

## 匹配器

一句话 → 该由哪个专家接，纯规则，不调模型（`lib/router.js`）：

```text
触发词命中 × (1 + (len-1)×0.5，上限 2.5)
同义词命中 × 1.0（总量上限 2.0，已当触发词命中过的不重复计）
描述命中 × 0.5（总量上限 1.5）

最高分 < 1.0            → miss
最高分 - 次高分 < 0.35  → ambiguous，列前两名
否则                    → hit
```

按词长给权重是为了让「数据库」压过「数据」、「设计文档」压过「文档」——笼统词盖过具体词是最常见的错路由来源。

三种结论都是正常结果，尤其 **ambiguous 不是错误**：分差太小时说「像是 A 也可能是 B」比硬选一个错的好。

跑验收：

```bash
npm run accept              # a 集（回归）+ b 集（口语，门槛 70%）
node tools/match.mjs --set c # 泛化探针
```

`expert.yml` 里 `triggers` 写「这个领域叫什么」，`synonyms` 写「用户会怎么说」：

```yaml
triggers: [样式, 前端, 组件, 布局, 交互, React, Vue]
synonyms: [登录, 按钮, 表单, 首页, 弹窗, 滚动, 适配]
```

## 命中之后做什么

`agent/pre-step` 里拿用户那句原话判一次专家，两条后果：

1. **注入角色**（默认开）：命中就把该专家 `role.md` 作为一条 `source.kind = capability-router-role` 的消息追加进去。一条用户消息只注入一次。
2. **收窄目录**（默认关，配置 `narrow: true`）：把该专家 `skills` 之外的技能全部设成 `modelInvocable: false`——模型看不见，用户仍可 `/name` 调用。

收窄的实现是冒名接管：宿主没有「排除技能」的接口，只能交一份同名候选、`rank: -1` 压过原 provider（排序是 `rank → providerOrder → localOrder`，同名先到先得）。

代价写在明面上：

- 每被覆盖一个技能，宿主在目录重算时打一条 `ignored because a higher-priority skill already exists` 告警。只在缓存失效时出现，但切专家那一刻会有 N 条。
- 目录是全量重发的，每变一次 prefix cache 重算一次。所以同一专家不重复算目录，匹配落空立刻恢复完整目录（逃生口）。

```json
{ "role": true, "narrow": false, "alwaysVisible": ["research", "office", "pdf"] }
```

`alwaysVisible` 是跨领域技能白名单：调研、Office、PDF 这类跟哪个专家都能撞上的，不进收窄范围。

## 之后

- **缺口提示**：匹配落空时说一句「没有干这个的人」，而不是静默按普通对话处理。
- **造专家**：缺口确认后生成 `expert.yml` 草案，人审过再落盘。
- **否定式说法**：`没生效 / 没起作用 / 不起作用` 这类整类词还没进词表，是当前匹配的已知短板。

## 安装方式

**源码只有一份**，放在哪都行；`C:\dev\dsh-capability-router` 只是个不含空格的稳定别名（junction）。profile 再链接到别名：

```text
C:\Users\Alec\Documents\DeepSeekHermesData\DSH-capability-router dev   ← 唯一源码（git 仓库）
  ⇐ C:\dev\dsh-capability-router                                      ← junction，稳定别名
  ⇐ ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-capability-router        ← profile 安装位
```

别在 `~/.dsh/plugins/` 下再建副本——运行时根本不扫那个目录。

唯一受支持的安装动作：DSH → 插件 → 添加插件，输入**源码目录的绝对路径**。它会走 `dsh-plugin-manager` 的 `reconcile()`：登记 profile `package.json` 的 `dependencies` 与 `pnpm-lock.yaml` → 把包名推进 `dsh.profile.bundles` → 校验包内 patch 能解析。手写链接不会登记，插件面板看不见、版本兼容校验也不跑。

被 GUI 接受的前提是包里声明了 `dsh.bundle`，否则直接拒：`dsh-capability-router declares no dsh.bundle`（`dsh-plugin-manager/lib/index.js:1866` 的 `not-a-bundle` 分支）。本包已声明：

```json
"dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "cordis.patch.yml" }, "compatibility": { … } }
```

包内 `cordis.patch.yml` 就是加载入口：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: capability-router
      name: dsh-capability-router
```

patch 的应用顺序是「各 bundle 的 patch → profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` → `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml`」（`dsh-app-boot` `readProfilePatches`）。**所以 profile 自己的 patch 里不要再写同一条 insert**，同一 id 会挂两次、检查点会重复注入。

带空格的路径 pnpm 11 实测能吃（`link:C:/Users/…/DSH-capability-router dev` 解析正常）；不想敲长路径也可以用 `C:\dev\dsh-capability-router` 这个别名，效果一样。手动兜底（GUI 不可用时）才需要自己建链接 + 改 profile `package.json` + 手写 insert。

建立链接（管理员或开发者模式下）：

```bash
cmd //c "mklink /J %USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-capability-router C:\dev\dsh-capability-router"
```

**`insert` 不能省。** 不带 `insert` 的 patch 是「按 id 覆盖已存在条目」，新 id 匹配不到时 `applyEntryPatches` 只输出一条 warn 就跳过，插件静默不加载，日志里也翻不到。只有 `insert` 分支能新增条目（不带 `id` 的 insert 直接 push 到根数组）。

改 YAML 会热重载；只改 `lib/` 下的源码不一定触发，必要时重启 DSH。

## 配置

`~/.dsh/capability-router/config.json`，缺省时用内置默认值：

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "intake": true,
  "hint": true,
  "narrow": false,
  "groups": {},
  "activeGroups": [],
  "hidden": [],
  "order": 5000
}
```

| 字段 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | 总开关；关掉后无任何注入，行为等同未安装 |
| `intake` | 是否注入系统提示里的长期原则段 |
| `hint` | 是否追加当轮检查点 |
| `narrow` | 是否按 `activeGroups` 收窄技能目录（尚未实现，开了只记录） |
| `groups` | 分组定义，`{ "分组名": ["技能名", …] }` |
| `activeGroups` | 收窄时保持可见的分组 |
| `hidden` | 永不进模型目录的技能名 |
| `order` | 原则段的排序位；dsh-purge 尾段在 5100，这里排它前面 |

也可以调 `saveConfig(patch)` 从代码里改。

## 验证

```bash
npm test          # 等价于 node test/smoke.mjs
```

九个场景：首次注入、同句去重、新句再注入、无真人消息、reject 透传、`hint:false`、`enabled:false`、配置写回、跨步去重。

测试会把 `DSH_HOME` 指到临时目录，不会污染真实状态。**这个隔离必须在 `import` 插件之前设置**，否则假 promptId 会写进真实的 `hints.jsonl`。

行为验证看下一轮：问一句「这个功能为什么不生效？」——如果它先回答判断再动手，而不是先跑十条命令，说明检查点在起作用。

## 两个实测出来的坑

**一、改 `lib/` 源码必须重启，热重载只能验配置。**

改 YAML 会触发配置重载，`apply()` 确实又跑一遍（`trace.jsonl` 里有 `event:"apply"`）。但**重载出来的那个实例，`agent/pre-step` 拿到的 payload 和 decision 里 `messages` 都是空的**：

```json
{"at":"…08:50:22","p":0,"d":0,"keys":"kind|messages","lastKind":null,"promptId":null}
```

事件其实还在触发（每步一条记录），只是没有消息，`lastUserPrompt()` 找不到"用户那句话"，于是什么也不注入。重启之后同一条路径立刻正常：

```json
{"at":"…08:54:40","p":1,"d":2,"keys":"kind|messages",
 "pkeys":"messages|turn|step|signal|agent","lastKind":"runtime-context",
 "promptId":"6f50972d-287a-4681-a532-6e188dbc1a1d"}
```

所以：**改 YAML 用来验证条目挂上没挂上；改源码只能重启。** 别指望热重载。

**二、`p=0` 不等于没挂钩。**

我一开始看到 `p=0` 以为是监听没注册上，白查了一轮。实际是「挂钩在、payload 空」。判断办法就是看 `trace.jsonl` 有没有持续的新记录——有记录说明 handler 在跑，没消息才是 payload 的问题。

## 打开诊断

`config.json` 里 `"debug": true` 后，每次 pre-step 会往 `~/.dsh/capability-router/trace.jsonl` 追加一行：

```json
{"at":"…","p":1,"d":2,"keys":"kind|messages","pkeys":"messages|turn|step|signal|agent",
 "lastKind":"runtime-context","promptId":"…"}
```

- `p` = `payload.messages` 长度，`d` = `decision.messages` 长度
- `pkeys` = payload 有哪些键，用来确认消息到底挂在哪
- `promptId` 有值 = 找到了真人消息

验收标准三条：`promptId` 非空、`hints.jsonl` 出现同一 id、下一轮回答先归类再动手。

文件超过 64 KB 自动只留后一半。查完把 `debug` 改回 `false`。

## 卸载

1. 从 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 删掉那两行 insert；
2. 删 junction：`cmd /c rmdir "C:\Users\Alec\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-capability-router"`（不带 `/s` 只删链接，不动源码）；
3. 重启。

源码目录留着不影响任何东西。`rmdir` 不带 `/s` 只删链接，不动源码——别用 `rm -rf`。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-tg-bridge

Drive [DeepSeek Harness](https://deepseek.com) from Telegram. It runs on the
machine that already has the harness, and it answers in the chat where you asked.

A forum topic is a project: its own session, working directory, model,
permissions and language. Two topics share the install and nothing else.

Never made a bot? [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md) goes from "no account" to a bot
that answers, one step at a time.

## What it does

- **A model per topic.** `/model` lists the routes the profile declares — provider
  and model together — and a tap switches this topic only. `/model <route> all`
  moves the default the other topics follow; `/model auto` hands the topic back.
  A chat for thinking out loud and a chat for engineering no longer share one model.
- **A topic is a project.** `/cd my-app`, and every turn runs from that directory —
  on a permission-enabled profile the sandbox is narrowed to it too, so the agent
  cannot write outside the project.
- **One edited message per turn.** Steps, a timer and the cache hit rate, plus the
  reasoning in a collapsed block you can tap open. A long turn adds a second
  collapsed block with every tool call. `/stop` is a button on that message.
- **`/diff` — review the turn, one hunk at a time.** The working tree is split into
  files and hunks; every hunk gets two buttons: explain it, or revert just that
  hunk. A button carries a hash of the hunk it was drawn from, so a press that
  arrives after the file moved on is refused instead of touching a line nobody was
  looking at. `/diff stat` is the file list alone.
- **An endpoint from the chat.** `/endpoint add <id> <https://url/v1> <KEY_ENV>
  [model,model]` writes the provider without an AI turn, and the key itself is
  never typed — only the name of the variable that holds it. The new models appear
  on `/model` as routes.
- **Input: text, voice, photos.** Any speech engine plugs in — a local script, any
  command-line tool, or an OpenAI-compatible API (see [`docs/VOICE.md`](docs/VOICE.md))
  — and the transcript is shown before the answer. A photo is read by the turn's own
  model through `read_image`, text and UI included; no second model is needed.
- **Goal and checklist per topic.** `/goal`, `/tasks`; both survive restarts and
  are prepended to every turn.
- **Two scopes for every setting.** `/reasoning <mode> all` moves the default,
  without `all` it moves this topic; language and pinning follow the same rule,
  and `/crew use reviewer` gives one topic its own effort, permissions and agent
  preset (four built-in sets, read-only, copyable).
- **It says what it cost.** A turn reports tokens and the cache hit rate; `/cost`
  says what the session has spent and `/prices` shows the rates it used.
- **Out of quota is not a dead end.** When the quota runs out it switches to a
  free model right away, and the answer says which route answered.
- **No lost messages.** A journal with acknowledgement and replay.
- **Knows how busy the computer is.** `/load` shows free space on the topic's disk,
  free RAM and average CPU, plus how many turns are running and waiting. `/load on`
  makes a prompt wait instead of starting while the machine is over a limit you set
  — kept, never refused, and one press sends it anyway.
- **Languages.** Menus and service messages in `en`, `ru`, `zh`; `/lang` pins the
  topic language, and without it a new topic takes the language of the message
  itself (Cyrillic → `ru`, Han characters → `zh`), then the Telegram
  `language_code`, then `en`.
- **"Stop" / "Retry" buttons and tool confirmations** sit in the message, so there
  is no command to type to stop a run.
- **`/report`.** One command turns "it broke" into a redacted document: version,
  profile, preset, model, directory, the last failure and the log tail, with keys
  and home paths removed before the file is written.
- **`dsh-tg check`.** Diagnostics in one command, changing nothing on the system.

## Requirements

- Node.js ≥ 24 (the version DeepSeek Harness ships; sessions are zstd-compressed)
- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` or newer in the `0.2.x` line (`>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`)
- DeepSeek Harness installed (`~/.dsh/profiles/headless`)
- A Telegram bot token from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather)

The supported harness range is declared in `engines.dsh`; that field decides
compatibility on its own (DSH ignores `peerDependencies` when it is present).
The range includes an explicit prerelease branch, because a plain `<0.3.0`
silently excludes `0.2.2-*` builds. A future `0.3.0` needs an explicit bump:
the bridge relies on the `0.2.x` CLI flags and profile layout.

## Ecosystem

The Chinese DSH community maintains the largest plugin catalogs and the
in-app markets that read them; this bridge follows their packaging rules so it
can be listed next to them:

- [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) — bilingual (English /
  中文) plugin list and the `dsh-plugin-catalog` npm package
- [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) — the Chinese-built
  in-app market with one-click install and themes
- [dsh-find-plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/dsh-find-plugin) —
  finds a plugin from chat instead of browsing a catalog

## Languages

- Menus (`/` in chat): three sets, `ru` by default, plus `en` and `zh`; a client whose locale matches neither gets the Russian set.
- Topic language: `/lang en|ru|zh`; stored in `state.json` and survives a restart.
- A new user gets the language from the Telegram `language_code`; anything that is not `ru`/`zh` → `en`.
- Translated so far: menus, the start message, turn status, errors, `/cd`, `/new`, `/stop`, `/lang`,
  the reply to an unknown command. Long reports (`/status`, `/sessions`, `/model` and similar)
  are still in Russian, that is the next pass.

## Installation

One command: your bot token and your numeric id. Nothing to edit by hand.

**Windows, macOS or Linux — Node.js 24 or newer.** `init` and the bridge run
anywhere; `setup` (stop, autostart, restart) is **Windows-only** today, so on
macOS and Linux use `sh install.sh`, which registers `launchd` or `systemd --user`.
`node setup.mjs --check` reports state on every platform.

```bash
npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest init --token 123456789:AA... --user 123456789
npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest setup
```

`init` writes the token, your id and the working directory; `setup` registers
autostart and starts the bridge.

### What it needs from DSH

The bridge is a client of the DSH CLI, and the surface it uses is small enough to
write down: `--profile`, `--json`, `--session-id`, `--expose-internals <cli.js>`
when the app binary runs the CLI, and the `{"type": ...}` JSON events on stdout.
Profiles are read as files (`cordis.patch.yml`, `package.json`) under
`~/.dsh/profiles`. `package.json` spells the supported range out in
`engines.dsh`, and it is capped below `0.3.0` on purpose: a minor bump may rename
an event, and a bridge that guesses is a bridge that answers with silence.

Two escape hatches, for a moved app or a DSH that ships differently:

```bash
DSH_BIN=/usr/local/bin/dsh        # the CLI itself, no entrypoint argument
DSH_CLI_JS=/opt/dsh/lib/cli.js    # just the CLI entrypoint, run by DSH_BIN
DSH_APP_DIR=/opt/DeepSeek-Harness # where the desktop app is installed
```

`/doctor` prints the command a turn would actually run, so a machine where these
matter says so instead of failing with an empty answer.

**As a DSH plugin** (the package carries a `dsh.bundle`; the catalog entry is
pending review):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-tg-bridge
```

The plugin starts one bridge when DSH boots and stops it on shutdown; if a
bridge is already running (for example from the scheduled task), it leaves it
alone. Run `npx dsh-tg-bridge@latest init ...` first so a config exists.

What `init` does:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| bot token | `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml` → `refs.DSH_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`; other keys are left alone |
| your id and working directory | `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/config.json`; an existing file is not overwritten |
| `headless` profile | checked, with a hint on how to create it if missing |

`init` flags: `--cwd <path>` (default `~/Projects`), `--voice` (enable
voice transcription), `--dry-run` (show what would be written, change nothing).

Optional provider settings live in `config.json`:

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `providerKeys` | extra env var names to pass to a turn, read from `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`; default `[]` |
| `pricesUrl` | retired: `/prices` always reads OpenRouter's public list and labels the number as a reference for the model |
| `vision.patch` | opt-in overlay profile for photo turns; default `""` — the turn's own model reads images |
| `vision.enabled` | set `true` to run photo turns on `vision.patch` instead of the topic profile |
| `fallbackModels` | ordered failover chain; default `[]` — see below |
| `fallbackEnabled` | `false` switches the whole chain off without editing the list; `/fallback off` sets it |
| `maxParallel` | how many topics run at once, 1–8, default `3`; also `/jobs 5` in the chat |
| `replayWindowMs` | how old a journaled update may be and still be replayed after a restart; default `600000` (10 min) |

Each `fallbackModels` entry is one attempt, tried in order after the turn's own
model refuses:

```json
{
  "provider": "router-a",
  "model": "some-model",
  "patch": "~/.dsh/tg-bridge/model-a.yml",
  "free": false,
  "off": false
}
```

`patch` is an overlay file with a single `agent-default-model` row
(`provider` + `model`); it is materialised once as its own profile, so the turn
keeps every other setting and only the model changes. `provider` is the id the
provider is written under in the profile — it decides whose key and host the
pre-flight probe asks, so the same model id on two routers stays two attempts.
`free` only adds `(free)` to the switch notice. `off` keeps an entry in the list
but out of the walk; an entry whose `patch` file is missing is skipped the same
way, and the chat says so instead of counting it.

The chain may mix companies: a 503 from one provider says nothing about another,
so a busy channel skips its own models and the next company is still tried. Put
models from different companies next to each other — two arms of one router are
one outage, not two chances — and keep the `:free` models at the end, as the
last resort.

**What starts a switch.** Anything the provider itself says no to: a 400/413/422
refusal (its own validator rejecting the request), 401/403 (key refused), 402 or
a quota/balance message (empty account), 404 (that model id is not carried),
429 (rate limit), 5xx and `get_channel_failed` / "all providers busy" (the pool
is down), a dropped connection or DNS/TLS failure, and an empty answer. A refusal
gets one other route, not the whole chain: it is replayed in full, and if the
second vendor refuses identically the request — not the route — is what is wrong,
so the reply says to start a fresh session with `/new`.

**What does not start a switch.** The turn time cap, `/stop`, a session or
directory error, a missing `dsh` binary: no other vendor changes those, and a
replay would cost a full turn to learn the same thing. They are listed in the
card so the distinction is visible instead of guessed.

### `/fallback` — the chain from the chat

```
/fallback                 the card: chain state, numbered routes, what starts a switch
/fallback on | off        the whole chain (per route: /fallback off 3)
/fallback use 3 | skip 3  one route back in or out
/fallback up 3 | down 3   move a route in the order
/fallback test [3]        ask each route (or one) with a 1-token request
/fallback add <provider>/<model>     write an overlay and append the route
/fallback first <provider>/<model>   put it at the head: tried before every other route
/fallback remove 3        drop a route from the list (its overlay file stays)
```

Every line has a button on the card: `● n` switches a route, `↑ n` / `↓ n` move
it, and the card redraws in place after each press. `test` proves the key and the
channel are alive — not that the provider accepts this conversation, so a route
can answer `ping` and still refuse a long prompt with a 400. The card says that
in as many words.

`test` also times each route: how long it takes to produce the first token, and
which live route is fastest right now. Two routes that both answer are not
equally good — 400 ms and 9 s feel like different products — and the head of the
chain is the one a person picks on that number. A route that did not answer
prints no time, so `no balance · 120 ms` can never read as "works, just slow".

`first` exists because `add` appends: when the route you want should answer
*before* the primary, appending it means moving it up eight times and guessing
where the head is. `/fallback first router-a/deepseek-v4.1-flash` writes the
same overlay and puts it at position 1 — or moves it there if it is already in
the chain.

Get your id from [@userinfobot](https://t.me/userinfobot), the token from
[@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather).

### Bot settings in Telegram

Three things without which the bot will stay silent in a group or work only halfway:

1. **Privacy mode → Disable** (`/setprivacy` in BotFather). Otherwise the bot sees
   only commands, not regular text in a topic.
2. **Topics enabled** in the group settings (Edit → Topics). Without them all work
   goes to a single chat and per-topic sessions are not created.
3. **Pin Messages** permission for the bot. Only needed to pin the first
   message of a topic; without it the bridge keeps working but will not pin.

You do not need to set up the command menu by hand: `init` and `setup` install it
in Russian, English and Chinese at once. The menu is not refreshed by a plain
bridge restart, so after adding commands run `dsh-tg menu`. The full settings
table, permissions, checks and common errors are in
[docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md](https://github.com/aleksvega/dsh-tg-bridge/blob/master/docs/TELEGRAM-SETUP.md).

**Autostart** has two routes. `sh install.sh` writes `launchd` on macOS and
`systemd --user` on Linux; `dsh-tg setup` registers the `DSH-TG-Bridge` task on
Windows, which runs the guarded supervisor (the same launcher on logon and every
five minutes) so a crashed bridge comes back without a second poller. On macOS
and Linux `setup` declines and names `install.sh`, because it stops the old
bridge with `taskkill` and registers autostart through `schtasks`.

**Manual install** (if you want full control):

```bash
npm install -g dsh-tg-bridge
dsh-tg init --token 123456789:AA... --user 123456789
dsh-tg check     # report only, changes nothing
dsh-tg setup     # stop the old bridge and start the new one
```

If the bridge is already installed, `setup` restarts it on the new code and reinstalls
the command menu.

## Troubleshooting

Starting from nothing, or helping someone who is: [QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md)
has the same answers with the terminal output they will actually see.

Error replies end with a code, which tells you what to fix:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `INSUFFICIENT_QUOTA` | provider balance is empty: top up or stay on free models (`/prices`, `/model`) |
| `TG_CONFLICT` | a second process is polling the same bot: `/doctor`, then `/restart` |
| `MISSING_CREDENTIAL` | no provider key in the profile: add it in the DSH app |
| `NO_DSH_CLI` | DeepSeek Harness CLI not found: check the app installation |
| `NETWORK` | no network to the provider: retry, check VPN/DNS |
| `SANDBOX_DENY` | DSH denied access to a file or directory: check the project path and permissions |
| `UNKNOWN_MODEL` | the model from the config is unavailable: `/model` lists the working ones |
| `EMPTY_RESPONSE` | the model returned nothing: retry or switch model (`/model`) |
| `TURN_TIME_CAP` | the turn hit its own time ceiling: the work is saved, press Continue |
| `TURN_FAILED` | cause not recognized: `/doctor` and `/logs errors` |

## Checks

Send the bot:

| Command | Expected |
|---|---|
| `/doctor` | report: pid, Telegram, disk, directory, session |
| `/update` | which bridge runs, what npm has, and whether a newer release exists (`/update confirm` installs it) |
| `/thoughts [file\|all\|off]` | the last turn's reasoning as a message; `file`/`all` send the full log as a Markdown document, `off` hides the block |
| `/help` | commands grouped by category |
| `/cd my-app` | topic bound to the project, and the sandbox narrowed to it |
| `/diff [stat]` | what the turn changed, one hunk at a time: every hunk has "explain" and "revert this hunk"; a stale button is refused |
| `/report` | a redacted bundle (version, profile, preset, model, cwd, last failure, log tail) sent to the owner as a document; in a group, the path only |
| `/prices` | what the current model costs, and whose price that is: your provider's, the same model on another gateway, or "no public price" when nobody publishes one |

## Commands

```
Work:         /cd · /new · /stop · /send · /seed · /diff
Goals:        /goal (plan + checklist) · /goal reopen · /tasks (checklist only) · /tasks done|rm|edit <n>
Sessions:     /status · /sessions · /sessions <id> · /rewind [n|undo|fork [n]|branches]
Agents:       /agents · /agents <id> · /agents set model|depth|filter
Models:       /model · /model <route> · /model <route> all · /model auto · /endpoint · /prices
Tuning:       /effort · /permissions · /preset · /plan · /jobs · /remind · /every
Profiles:     /profile · /profile <name> · /profile new <name> from <template>
Sets:         /crew · /crew use|off|new|copy|rm · /crew model <v>
Extensions:   /skills · /plugins · /plugins search <word> · /plugins disable|enable <id> · /soul
Updates:      /update · /update confirm · /update on|off|check|auto · /subscribe on|off
Diagnostics:  /doctor · /logs [errors|N|text] · /report
Service:      /app · /restart · /help
Machine:      /load · /load on|off · /load limit cpu|ram|disk <n>
Settings:     /settings — the same switches as buttons, grouped in four tabs
Display:      /lang · /reasoning off|card|chat · /pin on|off · /thoughts
```

### Settings as a card

`/settings` draws the same switches that the commands set, in one message with
four tabs: what the bot says, who answers and how hard it works, new releases,
and the health checks. Each row shows what the setting is now and what a tap
would change it to. A tap runs the command a person would have typed
(`/reasoning chat`, `/update on`), so the card cannot disagree with the command:
it is a view of them.

The card stays after a tap. It is edited in place — same message, same buttons,
the value in force marked with `●` and one `✓ row: value` line saying what just
changed — so a second setting is one more tap instead of a second `/settings`.
`✓ Done` removes the card when you are finished with it; nothing else deletes it.

`📌 Pin the progress card` (`/pin on`) keeps the running card pinned, so the
clock, the speed and the step list are one tap away instead of a scroll. Telegram
gives a chat one pinned message, so each turn's card replaces the last one. Off by
default: a bot that pins without being asked takes that slot in someone else's
chat, and a group needs the right to pin at all.

Nothing on the card is only available on the card. `/settings` is for people who
would rather press a labelled button than remember which of `/effort`,
`/preset` and `/crew` changes what.

Every command answers `/help` in the chat, in the language you write in: a
message written in Cyrillic or Han characters switches the topic to Russian or
Chinese even when the phone's menu is set to another language, and `/lang`
pins a choice above that. The Telegram menu shows the same list, minus
`/subscribe`: it is one line, and a person who turns it off should not have to
find it in a menu again.

## Updates

The npm tag `latest` is a label, not an updater: installing a package pins the
version on disk, and nothing moves until something moves it. Two switches, both
about this install (not about a topic, because it is the install that updates):

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/update` | one line: what runs here, what is published, which switches are set |
| `/update on` | tell me about new releases: one message per version, checked once a day |
| `/update off` | stop telling me; nothing installs, nothing moves |
| `/update auto` | besides telling me, install the release by itself (checked hourly) |
| `/update confirm` | install the new release now, by hand |

Nothing above installs except `confirm` and `auto`, and even those only change the
files: the running process keeps its old modules until `/restart confirm`, so a
bad release never lands mid-chat. `confirm` and `auto` copy the replaced files to
`update-backup-<date>` and print the path; copying that folder back is the way to
roll back, with no state to undo.

`/subscribe on|off` says the same thing as `/update on|off`, for people who do not
want to read `/update` first. It is not in the Telegram menu on purpose.

There are no notices about failures. The bridge cannot decide what counts as one
for you, and "something failed" that nobody can act on is noise; errors stay in
the chat where they happened, under `/doctor` and `/logs errors`.

## How it works

```
Telegram → bridge.mjs → dsh --profile headless --json → reply
             │
             ├─ pending/ journal + ack  (messages are not lost)
             ├─ per-topic queue         (turns in topics run in parallel)
             ├─ progress + buttons      (you can see the work is going)
             └─ fail-fast on quota      (free models as a fallback)
```

The bridge is a single process with long polling. Each turn spawns a separate
CLI process that exits after the answer, so "no DSH process" between
turns is normal, not a failure.

### Steering during a turn

If you write in a topic while a turn is still running, the message does not queue
behind it: the bridge drops the task into `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/steer/`, the `dsh-steer-inbox`
plugin hands it to the live agent on its next step, and the agent immediately replies with a short
line in the chat: what it is doing now and where it put the addition. If the agent stays silent
for 90 seconds, the bridge writes one neutral line itself so there is no silence.

Attachments work the same way. A voice note is transcribed first and its transcript is echoed in
the chat, then the text is steered into the running turn; a photo or a file is downloaded to a
local path and that path is steered, exactly as an idle turn would hand it over.

What each kind of attachment becomes inside a running turn:

| Sent | Inside the turn | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| voice note, audio file, audio sent as a document | transcript, echoed as `🎤 …` before the steer | any engine you point `voice` at: `script`, `command` or an OpenAI-compatible `openai` endpoint; **off by default** |
| small text file (`.md`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.py`, `.log`, … up to 60 KB) | the content itself between `<file>` markers — no tool call needed | nothing |
| PDF, archive, binary, anything bigger | its local path under `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/inbox/` | nothing; the agent opens it with its own tools |
| video, video note, animation | its path; the agent can pull frames or sound out with ffmpeg | ffmpeg, only if frames or audio are needed |
| photo | its path plus one honest line; the turn reads it with `read_image`, and says so in one line if it cannot | a model that accepts images |

Voice is the one row with a hidden prerequisite: something has to turn audio into
text. Faster-whisper is what `init --voice` writes, but it is not the only answer —
`voice.provider` also takes `command` (whisper.cpp, Vosk, a wrapper of your own) or
`openai` (OpenAI, Groq, a local server; anything that speaks
`/audio/transcriptions`). With no backend configured, a voice note is not swallowed:
the bridge says what is missing and points at [`docs/VOICE.md`](docs/VOICE.md).

A caption does not turn the attachment into a text-only message: it is folded into the same
hand-over, so "why did this fail" plus a `.log` file arrives as one steer.

An album is one request, not ten. Telegram delivers it as one update per file, all sharing a
`media_group_id`; the bridge collects the group (1.2 s of quiet after the last item, at most
4 s) and hands it over once — one steer into a running turn, one turn when the topic is idle.

### When a turn hits the time ceiling

`turnTimeoutMs` (default 30 min, this install 75) is a ceiling, not a target: if a turn reaches
it, the bridge stops it with `⏱` instead of letting one runaway loop own the topic for hours.
Nothing is lost — the session and every file the turn produced stay in place — so the message
carries **⏵ Continue**, which asks the agent to check the state and go on from where it stopped.
That is deliberately not the same as **Retry**, which would redo the whole task from the start.

This needs the plugin from this repository:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile headless add link:<path-to-repository>/plugin/steer-inbox
```

and a line in `~/.dsh/profiles/headless/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: steer-inbox
      name: 'dsh-steer-inbox'
```

The bridge checks the profile itself: if the line is missing, it does not write the task
(it would just expire) and behaves as before, queueing the message.

### Live thoughts and reasoning

Two things land in the same progress message, and neither sends a chat message of its own.

**The model's reasoning.** Every `thinking` block the CLI commits is folded into one
Telegram `<blockquote expandable>`: collapsed it is a single line, tapped it opens the whole
trail of the turn, and it stays there after the turn ends — the same way the desktop app shows
a reasoning section you can expand. The block is written once, in the final edit of the turn,
and never touched again: Telegram re-collapses an expanded block on every edit of its message,
which used to yank the chat away from a half-read paragraph. While the turn runs the message
only gets a counter (`🧠 Размышления · 4821`) and the last three steps, so the live edits stay
short. Escaped, and trimmed to its tail when a turn thinks longer than a message can hold; the
panel never exceeds one message. A cut block says `… · начало скрыто · /thoughts file`, which
sends the whole log as a document. If the API refuses the markup, the same content is retried
as plain text.

**The steps.** Three calls fit inline. A turn that makes more moves its complete step list into
a second collapsed block, added in that same final edit, so "what did it actually run" is one
tap away instead of a count.

**The agent's own notes.** The agent can add a short decision trail:

```bash
node ~/.dsh/tg-bridge/say.mjs --thought "checking why the watchdog fired twice"
```

The note is appended to `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/thoughts/<chat>_<thread>.jsonl`; the progress
message shows the last two as `💭` lines. The command needs no ids: it falls back to the
newest turn's thought file, because tool shells do not inherit the bridge environment.
`--thought` sends a Telegram message of its own only in `/reasoning chat` mode.

A decision the person must know before the turn ends — a release shipped, a cause found,
a blocker — goes to the chat as one plain line instead:

```bash
node ~/.dsh/tg-bridge/say.mjs --note "1.10.1 is on npm; restart to load it"
```

`--note` sends a real message and takes the same no-ids fallback as `--thought`. The split
is deliberate: `--thought` is the working trail (inside the progress message, and in `chat`
mode also as its own messages), `--note` is the short line that changes what the reader
expects to happen next — useful in `card` and `off` mode, redundant in `chat`. The progress
message itself opens with the request echoed back (`⏳ Принял: «…» · 3 с`), so the first
thing the person sees after sending names their task rather than a generic spinner.

`/reasoning` is the switch for the 💭 mechanism, and it has three ends:

- `/reasoning card` (the default) — every turn carries a short instruction to leave one line
  at each decision point (task clear, cause found, risky change, result checked), and the
  progress message shows the last two;
- `/reasoning chat` — the same lines, each also posted as its own message, so a turn that
  runs for twenty minutes is read as it happens instead of scrolled back to afterwards.
  The prompt says so explicitly, so a line is written to stand alone;
- `/reasoning off` — drops the instruction and the `💭` lines for that topic, for when the
  step list is all you want.

A topic switched to `chat` mid-turn does not dump the steps already in the card: forwarding
starts with the next line written. The setting lives in `state.json` per topic, so a chatty
research topic and a terse deploy topic can differ; a `true`/`false` written by an older
release still reads as `card`/`off`. The settings card offers the same three ends as buttons.

The reasoning block itself is model output; `/thoughts` is what reads it back:

- `/thoughts` — the last turn as a message, in parts, deleted after three minutes;
- `/thoughts file` — the **whole** last turn as `reasoning-<date>-file.md`, sent as a document
  (a five-hour turn is tens of thousands of characters, which no chat message can hold);
- `/thoughts all` — every turn of the session in one file (a long session is a couple of MB);
- `/thoughts off` / `on` — keep the block out of the turn panel (the panel then shows
  `🧠 Размышления · N · /thoughts file`) or bring it back.

The log is built from the session file on demand, so nothing is duplicated while a turn runs.
Files land in `~/.dsh/tg-bridge/thoughts/` and older ones are pruned after a week.

### Profiles per topic

The desktop app lets you build several profiles for different kinds of work, each with its own
plugin set and model. The same switch works from a topic:

```
/profile                    current profile, available ones, hints
/profile rese
