# Voice Copilot for DeepSeek Harness A second model watches what `dsh` does: a cheap one narrates the work aloud, and a stronger one checks it at a few moments in each task. This plugin connects it to the Voice Copilot companion, a separate program: ```sh uv tool install voice-copilot # or: pipx install voice-copilot dsh plugin --profile add -w ./plugins/deepseek-harness # for each profile you use ``` Type `vc off`, `vc on`, `vc status` or `vc check` as the whole message, or `/vc off` and so on. These never reach the model. Pick a narrator in the panel's Commentator tab: dsh has no way to run a one-off call without saving a session. Your messages from the panel reach the agent as real user messages. What it reports to the companion, at `127.0.0.1` only, is what it sees: your prompts, tool calls with their input and output, and the model's text and reasoning. See [docs/plugins.md](../../docs/plugins.md). Tested on dsh 0.2.1-rc.5, a developer preview that warns of breaking changes.

> **Listen to Control.** Hear what your coding agent is doing, and get warned when it goes off track. Coding agents now work for minutes at a time: they read files, edit code and call tools. You can watch the terminal the whole time, or you can look away and find out about a wrong turn after it happened. Voice Copilot lets you look away and still hear about it in time. A cheap model tells you, in a sentence or two, what the agent is doing right now. A stronger model, the Supervisor, reviews the work at checkpoints, speaks up when the agent drifts, and in Supervisor+ mode pauses it until you decide what happens next.

The loop above is a real session. Codex wrote that its new tests passed. All three had failed, along with 83 others, and the Supervisor named the line that broke them. The narrator and the Supervisor ran on local models there.

▶ Watch the 60-second demo · Website · Quickstart

## Why this exists One prompt can now start minutes of autonomous work. The part you care about (what the agent understood, what it changed, which risks it noticed) is buried in text that scrolls faster than you can read. Reading all of it defeats the point of delegating, and ignoring it means you learn about a bad turn after the damage is done. Plain text-to-speech reads logs word for word, which is noise. Voice-coding tools help you dictate prompts to the agent but tell you nothing about what it does next. Voice Copilot works in the other direction: it listens to the agent on your behalf, turns the stream into short spoken updates you can follow with your eyes off the screen, and gives you a way to interrupt when you want to steer. ## How it works Two models watch the agent's event stream, and they have opposite budgets. The narrator is cheap: the weakest model your CLI offers, or Haiku 4.5 through the API. Every few seconds it says what the agent is doing, in one or two sentences. It summarizes what happened; it does not read the model's hidden thinking aloud. The Supervisor is the most capable model your CLI can run, and it only looks at checkpoints: the end of a turn, a run of tool calls, a failure that repeats. It gets the goal, a running summary and the recent transcript, then answers `OK` or says what is wrong. In Supervisor+ mode it also pauses the agent and waits for you. ``` coding agent ──► event stream ──► narrator (cheap) ──► spoken update ──► you (Claude/Codex) (json / proxy) supervisor (strong) ──► warning · agent paused (listen · resume · interrupt) ``` With Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI, both models run through the CLI you launched, with its login and its models, so you need no extra API key. Other CLIs need an API provider, which you choose in the Commentator tab. Oversight costs a small fraction of one agent turn, and you hear about a bad turn while it can still be stopped. The details are in [docs/supervisor.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/supervisor.md). ## Quickstart (two commands) > Goal: hear Voice Copilot narrate a real session. You need Python 3.11+ and a > coding CLI you already log in to. With Claude Code or Codex there is no API key > to find: the narrator and the Supervisor reuse that CLI's login by default. **1. Install and connect:** ```bash uv tool install voice-copilot # or: pipx install voice-copilot voice-copilot setup ``` *Expected:* it connects whichever of Claude Code, Codex, Pi, oh-my-pi and DeepSeek Harness you have, asks to turn itself on, and plays a test line. The panel is at `http://127.0.0.1:8765`. Click once in it if the browser blocks autoplay. **2. Start your CLI the way you always do**, and give it a task. *Expected:* it says `Voice Copilot is connected. For the list of commands, type vc`, and within a few seconds you **hear** what the agent is doing. The panel's **Trace** tab shows every event, line and verdict. That's the loop: **start your CLI, listen, step in when it matters.** **Any other CLI** goes through the local proxy, with the same commands: `vc gemini`, `vc opencode`, `vc copilot`, `vc qwen`, `vc aider`. Or run `voice-copilot serve` and press **Launch** next to a CLI on the panel's Launch tab, which needs no env vars. > **Voice input is off in this build** while the push-to-talk → speech-to-text → > agent path is reworked. Narration, the launcher and the trace work as usual. > To turn voice input back on, set `voice_input: {enabled: true}` in the config > file (`voice-copilot config` prints its path). ## Who it's for Vibe coders build by feel and let the agent do most of the typing, and a fast wall of diffs and tool calls breaks the flow. Voice Copilot tells you in plain language what the agent decided and changed, so you keep track of where it is going and can step in the moment it drifts. Professional engineers run long autonomous sessions with Claude Code or Codex on real codebases, where the risk is a confident wrong turn buried in minutes of output. Voice Copilot tells you the root cause, the risk and the next step as the work happens, so you can do something else and still interrupt early, instead of reviewing a large bad diff afterwards. Listening also lets you follow more than one session without watching every token. Multitaskers and reviewers hand work off and need to know when to step in. The narration runs in the background; when a line tells you something matters, open the trace. Authors of coding CLIs can have their tool expose a clean event stream for companions like this one (see the integration RFC below). > **Status: 0.3.0 alpha, plugins and chat commands.** It is aimed at advanced users > who are comfortable testing CLI workflows and sending feedback. Voice Copilot > is made by Volodymyr Moskvin at [Conus Vision](https://conus.vision), and we > welcome collaboration: [info@conus.vision](mailto:info@conus.vision). ## What it does - Follows a coding CLI in real time: through the local proxy for the CLIs in the launcher, or through stream-JSON for Claude Code and Codex. - Has a Supervisor, the strongest model your CLI can run, review the agent at checkpoints and warn you out loud when it drifts, goes in circles, touches files outside the task or runs something destructive. Supervisor+ also pauses the agent on a hard stop and shows a Resume banner in the panel. - Uses a small narrator model to sum up decisions, file edits and reasoning in short spoken lines. One setting picks the CLI's weakest model for the narrator and its strongest for the Supervisor, from the CLI's own catalog. - Treats listening as the main experience: you hear what matters, read the trace when it helps, and interrupt only when you need to. - Runs a local panel in the browser with play, pause, mute, skip and interrupt buttons, the live trace and all settings. - Launches about 25 coding CLIs with one click each (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Hermes, Droid, Pi, Cline, Copilot CLI, Oh My Pi, DeepSeek Harness, Qwen, Gemini, Aider and more), plus a plain Terminal with every proxy route set. A CLI is narrated when its model traffic goes through the proxy; a CLI that only talks to its vendor's own service still launches, but gives the narrator nothing to work with. - Connects to Claude Code, Codex, Pi, oh-my-pi and DeepSeek Harness through plugins, so a CLI you start yourself is narrated with nothing rerouted. `voice-copilot setup` connects them. Nine more (OpenCode, Hermes Agent, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI, Grok Build, Droid, OpenHands, Kimi Code) report through their own hooks once `voice-copilot integrate` has set them up. - Takes commands in your chat: type `vc` in any connected CLI for the list. Only a message that is exactly a command counts, so a sentence that mentions `vc` still goes to your agent. - Lets you step in from the panel: on Claude Code your message reaches the agent as a real message in the middle of its turn. See [docs/plugins.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/plugins.md) for how it arrives on the other CLIs. - Offers push-to-talk (`Alt+Space`, off in this build): your question goes through speech-to-text and is typed into the running agent, or queued for its next turn. - Pauses the agent (`Alt+P`, or automatically while you speak) by suspending its process with `psutil`, so it cannot race ahead while you talk. Only the agent's own process is suspended; processes it started keep running. - Narrates in English, Spanish, French, Ukrainian and Russian. - Loads speech output, speech input and the narrator model as plug-ins. Each can run on your computer: the narrator on a local model (Ollama or another OpenAI-compatible server), speech output with Piper voices, speech input with faster-whisper. ## What Voice Copilot is not It is not a dictation app or a voice keyboard, and it does not replace Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI or any other coding agent. It does not read raw terminal logs, the model's hidden thinking or its full answers aloud. It is also not one more chat window that you have to watch all day. ## Install options The Quickstart uses the light default. Extras add optional backends: ```bash # light default: cloud TTS and STT pipx install voice-copilot # + local TTS (Piper voices through sherpa-onnx) pipx install "voice-copilot[local-tts]" # + local STT (faster-whisper) pipx install "voice-copilot[local-stt]" # + ElevenLabs TTS pipx install "voice-copilot[elevenlabs]" # every extra pipx install "voice-copilot[all]" ``` With `local-tts`, pick `piper` as the voice in Settings. The extra adds about 45 MB and no PyTorch. The first line in each language downloads its voice once (about 65 MB, from the sherpa-onnx releases on GitHub) into `voices/` next to the config file; after that speech output needs no network. A short line takes a fraction of a second on a laptop CPU. Silero and Deepgram are reserved names without an engine yet, and selecting them says so. Or with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/): ```bash uv tool install voice-copilot uvx voice-copilot run claude -p "refactor the auth module" ``` Codex works the same way: `voice-copilot run codex -p "explain what this repo does"`. ## Narrate _any_ CLI through the proxy The **Launch** tab does this for you. To wire it up by hand (`voice-copilot run ` only knows `claude` and `codex`), run the proxy as a standalone service and point your CLI's base URL at it. That covers aider and any other CLI that reads its endpoint from a base-URL variable: ```bash voice-copilot proxy # → prints ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/anthropic # OPENAI_BASE_URL =http://127.0.0.1:8766/openai/v1 # ...and OpenRouter / Groq / Mistral / Ollama / Gemini # in another terminal: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8766/anthropic \ aider --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 ``` Not every CLI reads that variable. Crush reads `OPENAI_API_ENDPOINT`, Goose needs `GOOSE_PROVIDER=openai`, Cline takes the URL through `cline auth`, and Copilot CLI routes only bring-your-own-key models, through `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`. Amp, Auggie and Droid's hosted models go to their vendor whatever you set. The Launch tab says this for each CLI. Where a CLI has hooks, `voice-copilot integrate ` narrates it without the proxy. The panel lists each client that connects. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Crush and Cline send a session id with every request, so two terminals running the same CLI show up as two entries; other clients are told apart by User-Agent and API key. Pick one in the header dropdown to narrate it; the others keep running silently. Supported upstream providers: | Provider | Env var | Upstream | | --- | --- | --- | | Anthropic | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `api.anthropic.com` | | OpenAI | `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | `api.openai.com` | | ChatGPT plan (Codex) | `openai_base_url` config value (`-c openai_base_url=…`) | `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex` | | OpenRouter | `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` | `openrouter.ai/api` | | Groq | `GROQ_BASE_URL` | `api.groq.com/openai` | | Mistral | `MISTRAL_BASE_URL` | `api.mistral.ai` | | DeepSeek | `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` | `api.deepseek.com` | | DeepSeek, Anthropic format (DeepSeek Harness) | `DEEPSEEK_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` (DeepSeek Harness reads it as `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`) | `api.deepseek.com/anthropic` | | Ollama | `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` | `127.0.0.1:11434` (local) | | Gemini | `GEMINI_BASE_URL` (Gemini CLI reads `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL`) | `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` (passed through, not narrated yet) | | OpenCode Zen | `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` (the launcher writes it) | `opencode.ai/zen/v1` | CLIs that sign in with OAuth (a Claude Code subscription, the Codex login flow) work as they are: the proxy only sees the bearer token on the wire and forwards it. The OAuth round trip in the browser happens on other domains, which the proxy does not touch. If you already point a CLI at another endpoint (an Anthropic-compatible vendor or a company gateway), `vc` keeps it: the proxy forwards to your endpoint instead of the default upstream above, and the panel says so. ## Use it as a plugin Keep starting your CLI the way you always do, and let its plugin bring Voice Copilot along: the first session starts it, and you can correct the agent mid-turn from the panel. ```sh uv tool install voice-copilot voice-copilot setup ``` `setup` connects Claude Code, Codex, Pi, oh-my-pi and DeepSeek Harness, whichever you have. Any other CLI works through `vc `. Then type `vc` in the chat for the list of commands: `vc off` for this session, `vc off all` for every one, `vc check` to have it look at the agent right now, `vc ask` to ask the second model, `vc speed`, `vc volume`, `vc model`, `vc review` and more. The model never sees those, and a message that only mentions them goes to it as usual. [docs/plugins.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/plugins.md) covers all of them, how a plugin compares with `vc `, how your messages reach the agent and how to add other CLIs. Nine more CLIs report through their own hooks or plugin. Connect one and keep the panel running: ```bash voice-copilot integrate gemini # or opencode, hermes, qwen, copilot, grok, droid, openhands, kimi voice-copilot serve gemini # any terminal, as usual ``` The Plugins section of the panel's Settings tab has the same Install button per CLI. OpenCode, Hermes Agent and Kimi Code were tested end to end; the others follow each CLI's hook reference. Every step is in [docs/integrations.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/integrations.md). ## Hotkeys | Action | Default combo | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Interrupt (pause & listen) | `Alt+Shift+Space` | Suspends the CLI process and stops the line being read. | | Pause / resume toggle | `Alt+P` | Manual pause of the child CLI. | | Mute TTS | `Alt+M` | Stops narration without affecting the agent. | | Skip current narration | `Alt+Shift+N` | Drops the line being spoken, keeps the queue. | | Push-to-talk | `Alt+Space` | Off in this build (see the voice input note above). | You can rebind all of them under **Settings → Hotkeys**. ## Providers Every layer is pluggable. The defaults use cloud services, so `pipx install voice-copilot` works without extra setup. | | Default (light) | Local (extra) | Premium cloud | Secret name | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **TTS** | `edge-tts` | `piper` | `elevenlabs`, `openai` | `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` | | **STT** | `openai-whisper-api` | `faster-whisper` | `deepgram` (not implemented yet) | `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY` | | **LLM** | `auto` (the launched CLI, no key); API: `anthropic` (Haiku) | `openai-compat` (Ollama) | `openai`, `github-copilot` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_COMPAT_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_COPILOT_TOKEN` | Switch providers in the **Settings** tab or in the config file. Every backend, its install extra and its default model are listed in [docs/providers.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/providers.md). ## Configuration The config file lives in your platform's config folder: `~/.config/voice-copilot/config.yaml` on Linux, `~/Library/Application Support/voice-copilot/config.yaml` on macOS and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\voice-copilot\config.yaml` on Windows. `voice-copilot config` prints the exact path, and the launcher profiles sit next to it in `proxy-cli.yaml`. You can edit both by hand or in the Settings tab, which refuses to save a provider it cannot start. Saved settings apply at once: the narrator, the voice, speech input, hotkeys and the debounce. Only the panel's host and port need a restart. The Supervisor is configured with `commentator.supervisor.mode` (`off`, `watch` or `guard`), `commentator.supervisor.model` and `commentator.supervisor.every_n_tools`. `commentator.auto_tier_models: true` picks the weakest and strongest model per CLI, and `commentator.per_cli..supervisor_mode` overrides the mode for one CLI. See [docs/supervisor.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/supervisor.md). Secrets live in the OS keychain (Credential Manager, Keychain or Secret Service) or in a `.env` file next to where you run `voice-copilot` (copy [`.env.example`](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/.env.example)). Shell exports take precedence. Values from `.env` are only for Voice Copilot: the agent it launches does not see them. There are no fallbacks between providers. If the configured one fails, the error shows up in the panel and narration stops, so a broken setup is never silent. The panel and the proxy listen on `127.0.0.1`. To open the panel from a phone or another computer, start it with `VOICE_COPILOT_HOST=0.0.0.0 voice-copilot serve`. It prints a link with an access token. Another device needs that link once; its browser then keeps the token in a cookie. Your own computer needs no token. On a machine you share with other people, set `VOICE_COPILOT_TOKEN` to a secret of your choice: every request then has to carry it, the panel opens with it, and the hooks and plugins send it from the same variable. ## Interception strategies 1. Stream-JSON mode of the target CLI, used by `voice-copilot run claude` and `run codex`. 2. An HTTP reverse proxy (`voice-copilot proxy`, the launcher, `vc`, or `run … --proxy`). The CLI's base URL points at a local port, so the proxy sees the raw model stream, including `thinking` blocks that the terminal UI may hide. It works with any CLI that reads its endpoint from a base-URL variable or setting. The CLI talks plain HTTP to localhost and the proxy talks HTTPS upstream, so there are no CA certificates to install and no TLS interception. When `--proxy` runs next to a stream-JSON adapter, the adapter drops its own copies of the model events and the proxy is the single source. 3. The `vc` terminal wrapper runs any program in a real terminal and narrates it through the proxy when the CLI is in the catalog. An unknown CLI runs without narration until you add a proxy profile for it. 4. The CLI's own plugin or hooks report to the panel at `/api/companion/v1` (see [docs/integrations.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/integrations.md)). This needs no proxy, sees permission prompts and tool results, and is the only strategy that can hold or stop a CLI running in a terminal Voice Copilot did not start. See [docs/architecture.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/architecture.md). ## Roadmap Voice Copilot is in its first alpha, and the goal right now is to test the core idea with advanced users. Planned work: - grow the Supervisor: richer checkpoints (diff-aware review, cost and time budgets) and corrections delivered to the agent as well as spoken - improve the quality and timing of narration and cut its noise - make multi-session workflows and session switching stable - run the hook integrations of Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Copilot CLI and the others against each CLI, carry the `vc` words through them, and add Cline and Amp - refine the companion interface with CLI authors so it fits real integrations - improve advanced configuration, onboarding and developer documentation - explore richer host UIs such as VS Code while keeping the core small The core is MIT-licensed so that adopting it and contributing to it stay easy. The CLI companion integration RFC is in [docs/cli-companion-interface.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/cli-companion-interface.md), and its normative schema is in [docs/schemas/cli-companion-interface.schema.json](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/schemas/cli-companion-interface.schema.json). ## Development ```bash git clone https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot cd voice-copilot uv sync --extra dev uv run voice-copilot serve --demo # emit synthetic events, exercise the UI uv run ruff check . uv run mypy src/voice_copilot uv run pytest ``` ## Troubleshooting - No voice output: most browsers allow autoplay only after one click, so click anywhere in the panel. If that doesn't help, open DevTools in the panel and check that `audio_header` frames and audio bytes arrive over the WebSocket. - The narrator stays silent: check `commentator.min_importance` in Settings and set it to `low` to hear everything while you debug. When several `vc` sessions run at once, only one of them narrates: on Windows the one whose terminal or panel has focus, on macOS and Linux the one whose panel had focus last (see `focus.narrate_only_when_focused`). - The panel answers `403 unexpected Host header`: it only accepts `localhost`, IP addresses and the host it was started with, which keeps other web pages out. Open it as `http://127.0.0.1:`. - The panel says it needs its access link (HTTP 401): it was opened from another device without the token. Open the link `voice-copilot serve` printed at start, the one that ends in `?token=`. The token is kept in `panel-token` next to the config file. - Microphone denied: browsers only allow the mic on a trusted origin such as `http://127.0.0.1:`. Don't serve the panel from a LAN IP without HTTPS. - `keyring` finds no backend on headless Linux: install `keyrings.alt` into the same environment (`pipx inject voice-copilot keyrings.alt`), or put the keys in environment variables. ## Get involved - Star the repo. It is the clearest sign that listening to an agent is useful to people, and it helps other engineers find the project. - Tell us how you use it: open an issue or write to [info@conus.vision](mailto:info@conus.vision). Real workflows shape the roadmap. - If you build a coding CLI, let's design the companion interface together (see the [integration RFC](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/docs/cli-companion-interface.md)). Contact: [info@conus.vision](mailto:info@conus.vision) · [conus.vision](https://conus.vision) ## License The code is released under the MIT license, so individuals, teams, companies and other open-source projects can use, modify, fork and redistribute it with little friction. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/LICENSE) and [LICENSING.md](https://github.com/conus-vision/voice-copilot/blob/main/LICENSING.md).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# `dsh-feishu-notify` — DSH (Cordis) adapter

Feishu (Lark) cards from **DSH** when a turn ends, when the harness needs your decision, or when it
needs an **answer** from you (including plan review).
Sending goes through the shared `feishu-notify` CLI, which resolves the webhook from **your own
config** — this package ships **no address** and never talks HTTP itself.

> **Status: implemented, not yet published.** Everything below is measured against DSH
> **0.2.0-rc.2** on this machine. `packages/dsh` was linked into a throwaway profile (**since
> deleted**) and the turn-end path (card arrival, `--channel dsh` resolution, uninstall) was verified
> end-to-end; the
> `user-questions/request` waterfall is implemented against the shipped `.d.ts` and covered by stub
> tests, but **has not been observed firing inside a live DSH** (see “Verified vs not” at the end).

## What it does

Two subscriptions — `session/event` (the post-commit fire-and-forget feed) and the blocking
`user-questions/request` waterfall — mapped to cards:

| Hook | Card | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `session/event` → `turn/end`, `reason.kind === 'completed'` | ✅ 任务完成 | turn wall-clock, model, folded per-turn tokens, session-cumulative output |
| `session/event` → `turn/end`, `kind === 'error'` | ❌ 任务失败 | `LlmFailure` message / code / HTTP status |
| `session/event` → `turn/end`, `kind === 'aborted'` | ⏸ 任务已中断 | cancellation cause (`user` / `parent` / `hook` / `disposed`) |
| `session/event` → `turn/end`, `kind === 'blocked'` | 🚫 任务被拦下 | |
| `session/event` → `turn/end`, `kind === 'max-tokens'` | ⚠️ 已达 token 上限 | |
| `session/event` → `turn/end`, any other `kind` | ❓ 未知状态 | never throws; the raw `kind` is printed verbatim |
| `session/event` → `approval/asked` | 🔔 需要你决定 | tool name + asker's reason |
| `session/event` → `tool/result` with `isError` | ❌ 工具失败 | **off by default** (`toolFailures: true` to enable) |
| `user-questions/request` | ❓ 需要你回答 | the question list (`header` / `question` / options) |
| `user-questions/request` with `intent.kind === 'plan-review'` | ❓ 需要你回答 · 计划待批 | the same card, marked, plus the `approve` label |

Metrics are **omitted, never invented**: no model → no model line, no token usage → no token line.
There is deliberately **no tok/s** — DSH only gives turn wall-clock time (tool waits included), and
dividing by that would be a meaningless number.

## `user-questions/request` is a **blocking** waterfall (read this before changing it)

DSH's only real “the harness needs an answer from you” hook is the Cordis **waterfall**
`user-questions/request` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-user-questions/lib/types/types.d.ts:145`):

```ts
'user-questions/request'(this: Scoped<Agent>, request: AskUserQuestionRequestEvent,
                         next: () => Promise<AskUserQuestionAnswer>): Promise<AskUserQuestionAnswer>
```

Two rules keep this adapter transparent:

1. **Fire-and-forget.** The handler starts the `spawn` and returns; it never `await`s the send.
   Awaiting an external process inside a blocking hook is how one plugin turns its own network
   round-trip into someone else's latency.
2. **Always delegate.** `next()` must be called and its promise returned — in a Cordis waterfall a
   listener that does not call `next()` **vetoes the rest of the chain**
   (`@deepseek-ai/cordis/lib/index.js:317-331`), so the real answering UI would never see the
   question and `ask()` would resolve with a bogus answer.

Net effect: the handler is transparent (the promise you get back is exactly `next()`'s), and the
only thing we add before delegating is a `spawn`. See `tests/user-questions.test.mjs` for the
falsifiable version of this — a hanging sender promise must not stop `next()` from being called
synchronously.

## Not implemented (and why)

- **Answering from the card.** The approval/question waterfalls belong to the DSH client UI. Cards
  are one-way (same as the opencode adapter) — we notify, we never answer.
- **`agent/turn-stopping` as “turn finished”.** It fires *before* the turn closes and another listener
  may `agent.steer()` it back to life — using it would send false “done” cards.
- **`sessionStats` / TPS / generation-only time.** That projection is mounted by the `dsh-web-app`
  bundle only, so non-web profiles don't have it.
- **`session/event → user-question-reply`.** The original task design assumed this; it is wrong.
  `user-question-reply` is a `MessageSourceMap` member
  (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-user-questions/lib/types/types.d.ts:104`), i.e. `user/message.source.kind`, not a
  session event — registering that name would never fire. The real hook is the waterfall above.

## Config

Only two keys; the webhook and channel definitions still live in the CLI's own config
(`~/.config/feishu-notify/config.json`):

```yaml
# profile cordis.patch.yml — a patch config replaces the whole config
- id: feishu-notify
  name: dsh-feishu-notify
  config:
    channel: dsh          # the --channel name, not an address
    toolFailures: false
```

Every card class is on by default (turn end, approvals, user questions / plan review); only
`toolFailures` is opt-in because a single turn can produce dozens of failing tool calls.

## Which bot do the cards go to? (the `dsh` channel)

`channel: dsh` is a **name**, never an address — the CLI resolves it from *your* config. On the
machine this was built on, `dsh` points at **its own bot** (it was split off from `default` after
the adapter shipped; the fingerprints differ — every `doctor` result row prints one). The wiring is
config, not code: the plugin only ever passes `--channel dsh`.

To point DSH at a different bot, only the CLI config changes — nothing in this plugin:

```bash
# 1. create the bot in the Feishu group, copy its webhook, then feed it on stdin so it never
#    lands in argv / shell history (the plugin still ships no address):
printf '%s' 'https://open.feishu.cn/open-apis/bot/v2/hook/…' \
  | feishu-notify-cli channel add dsh --webhook-stdin --force

# 2. verify reachability + see the effective wiring (prints masked address + fingerprint):
feishu-notify-cli doctor --channel dsh
```

`--force` is required because the channel already exists. After the swap the plugin needs no
restart of its config — it only ever passes `--channel dsh`.

> **Checking whether two channels share a bot.** A masked address cannot answer that: the unique
> part of a Feishu webhook is the *token* (`…/bot/v2/hook/<token>`), and that is exactly what gets
> redacted. `doctor` closes the gap — each result row prints a **fingerprint** (sha256 of the
> webhook, first 8 hex chars), and channels sharing one bot are called out
> (`⚠ … 指向同一机器人`). Equal fingerprints ⇒ same bot; the call-out is an advisory, not a
> failure — reusing one bot for several channels is a legitimate choice.

## Install (once published)

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <name> pnpm add dsh-feishu-notify
```

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the plugin manager appends it to `dsh.profile.bundles`
automatically. For local development, point the dependency at this directory instead
(`link:` / `--dsh-dev-dir` via `feishu-notify-cli install --target dsh`).

## Uninstall

`dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-feishu-notify` also drops it from `dsh.profile.bundles`.
If you added an `- id: feishu-notify` override to the profile's own `cordis.patch.yml`, delete that
line too — a patch matching no row only produces a startup warning, but it is still litter.

## Troubleshooting

Failures are logged at **ERROR level unconditionally** (no debug flag gates them):

- **No card at all.** Check the DSH log for `dsh-feishu-notify: 找不到发送端 feishu-notify`.
  The sender is resolved on every send: `FEISHU_NOTIFY_BIN` → `~/.local/bin/feishu-notify` → `PATH`
  → give up. If `FEISHU_NOTIFY_BIN` is set but not executable, it is **not** silently ignored —
  that error means exactly what it says.
- **Cards go to the wrong bot.** The `--channel` name must exist in the CLI config; note this
  adapter, unlike the opencode one, does **not** retry without `--channel`.
- **No “需要你回答” card.** That hook is a **scope-filtered** waterfall: listeners tagged with an
  agent scope only see that agent's questions, while an untagged listener (this plugin registers on
  the root context) is admitted globally (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope/lib/index.js:329-337`). If you
  re-register it from an agent-scoped context you narrow it deliberately. Note we are a *listener*,
  not an answerer — if no UI claims a request DSH still reports `NO_PROVIDER`, exactly as it would
  without us.
- **Version drift.** Built against DSH 0.2.0-rc.2. No `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer is declared on
  purpose (rc versions in peer ranges are a minefield); every service is duck-typed.

## Development

```bash
npm test -w packages/dsh
```

No DSH runtime is needed: pure mapping functions and a fake-`ctx` harness cover the event mapping,
plus a real `spawn` against a stub executable that proves the argv contract.

## Verified vs not

| Area | State |
|---|---|
| `turn/end` → card, real profile, `--channel dsh` resolution, uninstall | ✅ observed end-to-end in a throwaway profile |
| `user-questions/request` mapping + fire-and-forget / `next()` contract | ⚠ stub tests only — **never observed firing in a live DSH** (no real `ask_user_question` was driven through a live profile) |
| Root-context listener admitted by the scoped waterfall | ⚠ read from `dsh-scope` source (untagged ⇒ global), not observed at runtime |
| `approval/asked`, `tool/result`, the other four `turn/end` reason kinds | ⚠ stub tests only |
| Install from the npm registry (`dsh plugin … add dsh-feishu-notify`) | ⚠ package is not published yet |
| DSH versions other than 0.2.0-rc.2 | ⚠ not tested |

# feishu-notify (monorepo)

Feishu (Lark) bot notifications for local AI agents — one config layer, one sender, one
adapter per agent. **No webhook is ever compiled in**: the address is resolved at send
time from the user's own config, and if it cannot be resolved the sender exits `2` with
guidance instead of delivering to somebody else's bot.

This repository is a **single repo with three packages** (`npm` workspaces): the CLI is built, and
both adapters (opencode, DSH) are built and awaiting publication.

## Packages

| Package | Path | Status | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `feishu-notify-cli` | [`packages/cli`](./packages/cli) | ✅ **implemented** (not on npm yet) | The core: the `feishu-notify` bash sender + the `feishu-notify-cli` Node config/diagnostics/`install` CLI. Ships both binaries. |
| `opencode-feishu-notify` | [`packages/opencode`](./packages/opencode) | ✅ **implemented** (not on npm yet) | opencode v2 plugin: cards on turn end / permission / form, routed with `--channel opencode`. Holds **no** webhook — it calls the sender, which resolves the address from your config. |
| `dsh-feishu-notify` | [`packages/dsh`](./packages/dsh) | ✅ **implemented** (not on npm yet) | DSH (Cordis) bundle: cards on turn end / approval / **user questions & plan review**, routed with `--channel dsh`. Also holds no webhook. |

Legend: ✅ implemented and measured · ⚠ assumed / not directly observed · ✖ not implemented.
Per-area verification state (including what is *not* yet observed in a live DSH) is in
[`packages/dsh/README.md`](./packages/dsh/README.md#verified-vs-not).

## Layout

```
.
├── package.json                 # private root: workspaces ["packages/*"], test fan-out
├── LICENSE                      # MIT (every package carries the same copy)
├── README.md / README.zh-CN.md  # this file — repo overview
└── packages/
    ├── cli/                     # the implemented core package
    │   ├── package.json         #   name: feishu-notify-cli, bin ×2, files whitelist
    │   ├── bin/feishu-notify    #   the sender (bash)
    │   ├── bin/feishu-notify-cli#   config/init/channel/doctor/resolve/footer/install (Node)
    │   ├── lib/                 #   config resolution, commands, sender, wiring self-check, install targets, secret gate
    │   ├── tests/               #   assertions + byte-exact golden fixtures
    │   └── README.md            #   the full documentation for the package
    ├── opencode/                # the implemented adapter (not published yet)
    │   ├── package.json         #   name: opencode-feishu-notify, main → src/feishu-notify.ts
    │   ├── src/feishu-notify.ts #   the plugin (no webhook: passes --channel, the CLI resolves it)
    │   ├── scripts/deploy.mjs   #   copy the plugin to the live dir; --check is a drift gate
    │   ├── tests/               #   module / channel / sender-resolution / routing / live-hash suites
    │   └── README.md            #   install, events, channel semantics, troubleshooting
    └── dsh/                     # the implemented DSH/Cordis adapter (not published yet)
        ├── package.json         #   name: dsh-feishu-notify, dsh.bundle.patch → cordis.patch.yml
        ├── cordis.patch.yml     #   the bundle layer: one `insert` row for the plugin (channel: dsh)
        ├── lib/index.js         #   turn end / approval / tool failure / user questions (no webhook)
        ├── tests/               #   pure mapping + fake-ctx harness + real-spawn stub executable
        └── README.md            #   events, the blocking user-questions waterfall, channel/bot, limits
```

## Start here

The complete documentation — install, config format, command reference, agent
compatibility, security model, rollback — lives in the package READMEs:

- [`packages/cli/README.md`](./packages/cli/README.md) (English) · [`README.zh-CN.md`](./packages/cli/README.zh-CN.md) (中文)
- [`packages/opencode/README.md`](./packages/opencode/README.md) (English) · [`README.zh-CN.md`](./packages/opencode/README.zh-CN.md) (中文)
- [`packages/dsh/README.md`](./packages/dsh/README.md) (English) · [`README.zh-CN.md`](./packages/dsh/README.zh-CN.md) (中文)

Quick version (install the CLI **globally** — two real binaries in one bin directory; do not point
your wiring at a development checkout, which is how the 2026-10-18 rename made notifications fail
silently):

```sh
npm i -g feishu-notify-cli            # puts both commands on PATH
feishu-notify-cli init                # asks for your webhook, verifies with a test card
feishu-notify-cli doctor              # wiring self-check (sender/resolver/Node, dangling symlinks) + per-channel reachability
feishu-notify-cli install --dry-run   # show what would be merged into your agent configs; writes nothing
feishu-notify-cli install             # wire it up: claude-code writes; opencode is declared once its package is published; dsh is gated
```

Add `--channel <name>` when you want a target pinned to a specific bot: for Claude Code it is
appended to the hook command, for opencode it is written into `options.channel`. Without it, each
caller uses your config's `activeChannel`.

From a clone (this is also the state until the package is published):

```sh
node packages/cli/bin/feishu-notify-cli init
# or, from inside the package:
cd packages/cli && node bin/feishu-notify-cli init
```

## Develop

```sh
npm test                      # from the repo root: fans out to every workspace
cd packages/cli && npm test   # the CLI suite
cd packages/opencode && npm test   # the plugin suite (includes the live drift gate)
cd packages/dsh && npm test   # the DSH adapter suite (no DSH runtime needed)
npm run secret-scan           # the publish gate (whole-repo git index + the CLI tarball)
```

`npm test` from the root runs the workspace `test` scripts (`packages/cli`,
`packages/opencode` and `packages/dsh`). The plugin suite's live-hash gate **skips** on a machine where the plugin was
never deployed (`deploy --check` exit `2`); it fails only on real drift. The secret gate
deliberately scans the **whole repository index** (not just the current directory) so that neither
the root files nor the other packages can drift out of its view.

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` English | [中文](README.zh.md) The shared dsh core as a profile bundle: [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) inserts every base plugin row — model adapters, the shared [`agent-default-model`](../../core/agent-default-model/README.md) selection, tools, persistence, policy, settings/credentials, telemetry, and the core spawn/fork subagent providers — over the empty profile root, as the first layer of every profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` list. The optional Codex and Claude Code providers stay outside this package and its production dependency closure; a Profile installs either [product provider Bundle](../../subagent/README.md) only when needed. The default `@deepseek-ai/dsh` production closure therefore includes neither product provider, the Claude Agent SDK, nor the Codex wrapper and platform payloads. Later bundle layers (e.g. [`dsh-web-app`](../web-app/README.md)) and the user's profile `cordis.patch.yml` override these rows by id; a patch replaces a row's whole `config`, so mode-specific values live in mode bundles, not here. The package has no runtime API; the profile composer resolves the patch through the `dsh.bundle.patch` manifest field, never through code. The patch gates both shell stacks by platform on its own rows: `bash-sandbox`/`tool-bash` carry `disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'` (bash has no Windows runner), and their twins `pwsh-sandbox`/`tool-pwsh` mount on win32 only with the inverted expression — one shared patch file, exactly one shell stack per host. The permission surface stays exactly as on POSIX: `sandbox`/`sandbox-policy` enforce the file-effect policy through the Windows ACL restricted-token runner (the win32 chain of `dsh-sandbox-local` → `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`), the permission switcher and the approval service run unchanged, and `fs-sandbox` keeps fencing `ctx.fs` writes — mounting `dsh-fs-local` alongside it would double-register `ctx.fs` and fail the load. A Windows host that prefers the unconfined local pwsh executor or full access overrides these rows through its profile or home `cordis.patch.yml` (the bash-restore recipe must be complete: disable `pwsh-sandbox`/`tool-pwsh` AND re-enable `bash-sandbox`/`tool-bash` — both executor families register the same `bash` service, so an incomplete recipe fails loud at load). POSIX hosts see the pwsh rows disabled. The row set and its rationale are documented inline in the patch file; the [generated composition graph](../../../apps/cli/composition.md) renders it. ## Model Experience Indirectly, through the inserted rows: this bundle selects the shipped persona-less prompt base, tool set, and DeepSeek adapter that mode bundles specialize, and contributes no model-visible text of its own. #### KV Cache effect None directly; each inserted row's package owns its effect. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work - **A patch replaces whole row configs** — profile overrides must restate every field a row keeps; there is no deep-merge layer. - **The Windows temp grant is a private per-session subdirectory** — `workspace-write` confines writes to the workspace plus the session's own temp subdirectory (`\dsh-`, TMP/TEMP rewritten for confined children); `read-only` grants nothing. See `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`. # DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness (dph) English | [中文](README.zh.md) **DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness** is an independent agent harness product for paper-writing workflows. It adopts the open-source [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) as its technical foundation — reusing the Cordis plugin system and the session/tool-execution stack — and builds a durable, auditable writing-workflow layer on top. The product is independent of its foundation: the CLI entry (`dph`), branding, user-data directory (`DPH_HOME`, default `~/.dph`), and default branch are entirely its own, and upstream is synced selectively through the `upstream` remote only. > **Maintainers / 接手者**：start from [`docs/PROJECT-MAP.md`](docs/PROJECT-MAP.md) — the single authoritative entry for architecture, load-bearing modules, run/test commands, and the production/test separation rules (`runs/` directory, `.env.` credentials). All development workflow constraints (branching, gates, delivery, push, task process) are codified in [`docs/PM-HANDBOOK.md`](docs/PM-HANDBOOK.md) — read it before your first commit. Current progress: [`docs/PROGRESS.md`](docs/PROGRESS.md); known issues: [`docs/DESIGN-DEBTS.md`](docs/DESIGN-DEBTS.md). ## What it does A run takes a task and drives it through **plan → execute → review → revise → deliver**, with every fact durable before it is acted on: - **Durable workflow engine** — versioned run/node/event/artifact records in `storage-domain`; an event log that replays fail-closed; runs survive process restarts and recover at startup. - **Node executor with review policies** — fast mode delivers after one revise round; strict mode allows three and fails when defects persist. A node that spends its attempts pauses for review instead of failing, so a resumed run continues from it. - **Cost and context control** — spend is derived from token counts against a configured price table and a daily ceiling (never trusted from a provider field); prompts are fitted to the model's window by trimming declared low-priority sections first. - **Audit trail** — append-ordered, retention-pruned, credential-redacted; staging, activation, rollback, migration, and every run boundary reach it. - **Signed skills and releases** — skill packages verify manifest, file hashes, trust root, and Ed25519 signature before loading; releases are signed manifests of content-addressed artifacts with staged rollout, health confirmation, and automatic rollback of an unproven version. - **Legacy migration** — a dry-run, resumable importer for predecessor data; the source is never modified. The writing layer mounts as one profile bundle over storage-capable modes: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-paper` inserts the composition, the signed skill catalog, its provider, and the invariant companion into any profile. Full subsystem reference: [docs/subsystems/paper.md](docs/subsystems/paper.md). ## Relationship to the open-source foundation - `vendor/` carries the pinned Cordis source; most `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages under `packages/` are foundation capabilities (all `private: true`, never published to npm). - `packages/paper/*` is this product's increment: workflow state machine, review-loop executor, cost budgets, audit, signed skills and releases, legacy migration. - Upstream updates land only through a reviewed, selective merge from the `upstream` remote; this repository's `main` branch never points at an official snapshot. - Coexistence with an official dsh install is conflict-free: the CLI command is `dph`, user data lives under `DPH_HOME` (default `~/.dph`), and `~/.dsh` is never read or written. ## Run Requires Node.js ^22.19 or ≥24 (Corepack included) and Git. ### Windows quick start 1. Install [Node.js LTS](https://nodejs.org/) (the installer enables Corepack); 2. Clone this repository: ```bat git clone -b main https://github.com/dddsx3/DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness.git cd DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness ``` 3. Double-click `setup.bat` (equivalent to `corepack enable && pnpm install && pnpm run build`), or run those commands yourself; 4. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; 5. Double-click `start.bat` (equivalent to `pnpm dph web`) and open `http://127.0.0.1:3080`. Pass `--no-open` to suppress opening a browser. ### macOS / Linux ```sh git clone -b main https://github.com/dddsx3/DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness.git cd DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness corepack enable pnpm install pnpm run build pnpm dph web ``` ### Enabling the writing layer Add the bundle to a profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` list: ```yaml dsh: profile: bundles: - '@deepseek-ai/dsh-base' - '@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app' - '@deepseek-ai/dsh-paper' ``` Configure role routes in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` by row id (`paper`, `paper-skill-catalog`, …): ```yaml - insert: - id: paper config: executor: provider: deepseek-official model: deepseek-v4-flash # A reference resolved through the credentials seam — never a value. credentialRef: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY defaultMode: fast ``` Conservative by default: no price table charges nothing, no trust root refuses every signed package and release, and unsigned packages load only in development mode. See the [patch file](packages/paper/paper-bundle/cordis.patch.yml) for every row and field. ## Development Start with the [development guide](docs/development.md) and [architecture documentation](docs/architecture.md). The writing layer's design decisions are recorded in [.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-22-paper-foundation-seams.md](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-22-paper-foundation-seams.md); the product identity and namespace decisions are recorded in [.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-22-independent-product-identity.md](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-22-independent-product-identity.md). For agents, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Contributions: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Built on the open-source DeepSeek Harness with thanks to its authors; third-party dependencies are disclosed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` English | [中文](README.zh.md) The dsh browser-surface bundle. [`cordis.patch.yml`](cordis.patch.yml) rides over [`dsh-base`](../base/README.md): it sets the coding persona, inserts the Web host rows (webserver, API gateway, workspace, projection cache, storage) and the browser plugin roster, the always-on client-plugin reload chain ([`dsh-client-hmr`](../../client/hmr/README.md), idle until a rebuild watcher rewrites client bundles), and mounts this package's `web-runtime` glue plugin (config `{openBrowser, printUrl, surfaceContext, trustedHosts}`). That plugin resolves the built frontend dist through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-frontend`'s exports, samples bind-dependent LAN trust once, provides it as `webRuntime` to the browser-trust fence and client roster, mounts the [`frontend-static`](../../host/frontend-static/README.md) fallback owner, and registers the harness-source and web-surface prompt sections plus the bash-visible `DPH_WEB_URL` runtime variable when `surfaceContext` is true. After its Loader tree settles, it prints the `dsh web:` URL line when `printUrl` is true and opens the canonical host URL in the default browser when `openBrowser` is true and the inherited `SSH_CONNECTION` and `SSH_TTY` are blank or absent. An SSH launch keeps the URL line but suppresses browser handoff because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address. Immediately before a handoff, the runtime prints `dsh web: opening the default browser; pass --no-open to disable`. A short-lived Node helper runs the maintained platform opener with the canonical scrubbed child environment. On Windows it stays alive until the short-lived PowerShell launcher exits, because `open` reports spawn before that launcher has handed the URL to the shell; elsewhere the helper stops after the opener accepts spawn. A helper failure writes a diagnostic with its reason and the manual URL to stderr without stopping the server, and no path waits for the browser to exit. This bundle also owns the app command line: the ordinary `web-startup` provider ([`src/startup.ts`](src/startup.ts)) injects `ctx.cmdlineArgs` ([`dsh-cmdline`](../../boot/cmdline/README.md)), parses `--host`, `--port`, repeatable `--trusted-host`, `--no-open`, and the app's `--help`, then provides `webStartup`; browser opening defaults on for local launches, and `--no-open` turns it off for this invocation. It rejects `--host 0.0.0.0` before publishing that service because the CLI intentionally does not support all-interfaces binding yet. Flag-configured rows inject the service and read it directly from lazy config, so nothing binds a port before argument resolution and `dsh --profile web --help` starts no server. [`dsh-headless`](../headless/README.md) is a sibling surface over the same base and does not mount this bundle. ## Model retry defaults Web uses the shared bounded normal default of five eligible retries after the initial request. The `deepseek-official` route and settings-added pi-ai routes use that default when they omit `retryPolicy`; explicit provider policies still win. Web adds no retry-specific composition override, so the same omission behavior applies to non-Web profiles. ## Model Experience ### Harness-source and Web-surface context #### What the model sees When `surfaceContext` is true, the `harness:source` section identifies the on-disk Harness implementation without claiming it is the working directory, and the `app:web-surface` global section (order −98) orients the model to the GUI: the canonical local URL, the "this page" referent, the update contract (the reload receiver is always on; no-refresh reloads additionally need the `pnpm run dev:web` watcher), and the instruction not to start replacement servers. `DPH_WEB_URL` additionally appears in the managed bash environment with its description, resolved per invocation from the live server. When it is false, neither section nor the variable is registered. #### Token effect One source line and one prompt paragraph per session plus two managed-environment variable lines; constant per process. #### KV Cache effect The prompt section sits near the system prompt's head and is stable for the life of the process (the port is a boot fact), so it does not invalidate the cache across turns. ## Known Limitations and Deferred Work - **The frontend dist must be built** — `require.resolve` of the dist fails loud at activation with a build hint; there is no source-serving fallback. - **`lanAddresses` is a boot-time snapshot** — interface changes after boot are not re-advertised; the printed LAN URL always matches the configured trust fence. - **Only handoff startup is observable** — observation ends when the platform opener accepts spawn, except that Windows waits for its short-lived PowerShell launcher to exit; a later browser exit is not reported, and the printed URL remains the manual fallback. - **SSH forwarding owns the browser URL** — the printed canonical URL names the remote host's loopback endpoint; automatic handoff is suppressed, and the SSH client or editor must expose and open its local forwarded address. - **Browser command overrides are launch-only** — a discovered `.env` may not set `BROWSER`; only an inherited value may reach an opener path that honors the variable, so a checkout cannot choose an executable for automatic handoff. # DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness (dph) English | [中文](README.zh.md) **DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness** is an independent agent harness product for paper-writing workflows. It adopts the open-source [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh) as its technical foundation — reusing the Cordis plugin system and the session/tool-execution stack — and builds a durable, auditable writing-workflow layer on top. The product is independent of its foundation: the CLI entry (`dph`), branding, user-data directory (`DPH_HOME`, default `~/.dph`), and default branch are entirely its own, and upstream is synced selectively through the `upstream` remote only. > **Maintainers / 接手者**：start from [`docs/PROJECT-MAP.md`](docs/PROJECT-MAP.md) — the single authoritative entry for architecture, load-bearing modules, run/test commands, and the production/test separation rules (`runs/` directory, `.env.` credentials). All development workflow constraints (branching, gates, delivery, push, task process) are codified in [`docs/PM-HANDBOOK.md`](docs/PM-HANDBOOK.md) — read it before your first commit. Current progress: [`docs/PROGRESS.md`](docs/PROGRESS.md); known issues: [`docs/DESIGN-DEBTS.md`](docs/DESIGN-DEBTS.md). ## What it does A run takes a task and drives it through **plan → execute → review → revise → deliver**, with every fact durable before it is acted on: - **Durable workflow engine** — versioned run/node/event/artifact records in `storage-domain`; an event log that replays fail-closed; runs survive process restarts and recover at startup. - **Node executor with review policies** — fast mode delivers after one revise round; strict mode allows three and fails when defects persist. A node that spends its attempts pauses for review instead of failing, so a resumed run continues from it. - **Cost and context control** — spend is derived from token counts against a configured price table and a daily ceiling (never trusted from a provider field); prompts are fitted to the model's window by trimming declared low-priority sections first. - **Audit trail** — append-ordered, retention-pruned, credential-redacted; staging, activation, rollback, migration, and every run boundary reach it. - **Signed skills and releases** — skill packages verify manifest, file hashes, trust root, and Ed25519 signature before loading; releases are signed manifests of content-addressed artifacts with staged rollout, health confirmation, and automatic rollback of an unproven version. - **Legacy migration** — a dry-run, resumable importer for predecessor data; the source is never modified. The writing layer mounts as one profile bundle over storage-capable modes: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-paper` inserts the composition, the signed skill catalog, its provider, and the invariant companion into any profile. Full subsystem reference: [docs/subsystems/paper.md](docs/subsystems/paper.md). ## Relationship to the open-source foundation - `vendor/` carries the pinned Cordis source; most `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages under `packages/` are foundation capabilities (all `private: true`, never published to npm). - `packages/paper/*` is this product's increment: workflow state machine, review-loop executor, cost budgets, audit, signed skills and releases, legacy migration. - Upstream updates land only through a reviewed, selective merge from the `upstream` remote; this repository's `main` branch never points at an official snapshot. - Coexistence with an official dsh install is conflict-free: the CLI command is `dph`, user data lives under `DPH_HOME` (default `~/.dph`), and `~/.dsh` is never read or written. ## Run Requires Node.js ^22.19 or ≥24 (Corepack included) and Git. ### Windows quick start 1. Install [Node.js LTS](https://nodejs.org/) (the installer enables Corepack); 2. Clone this repository: ```bat git clone -b main https://github.com/dddsx3/DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness.git cd DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness ``` 3. Double-click `setup.bat` (equivalent to `corepack enable && pnpm install && pnpm run build`), or run those commands yourself; 4. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; 5. Double-click `start.bat` (equivalent to `pnpm dph web`) and open `http://127.0.0.1:3080`. Pass `--no-open` to suppress opening a browser. ### macOS / Linux ```sh git clone -b main https://github.com/dddsx3/DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness.git cd DeepSeek-For-Paper-Harness corepack enable pnpm install pnpm run build pnpm dph web ``` ### Enabling the writing layer Add the bundle to a profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` list: ```yaml dsh: profile: bundles: - '@deepseek-ai/dsh-base' - '@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app' - '@deepseek-ai/dsh-paper' ``` Configure role routes in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` by row id (`paper`, `paper-skill-catalog`, …): ```yaml - insert: - id: paper config: executor: provider: deepseek-official model: deepseek-v4-flash # A reference resolved through the credentials seam — never a value. credentialRef: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY defaultMode: fast ``` Conservative by default: no price table charges nothing, no trust root refuses every signed package and release, and unsigned packages load only in development mode. See the [patch file](packages/paper/paper-bundle/cordis.patch.yml) for every row and field. ## Development Start with the [development guide](docs/development.md) and [architecture documentation](docs/architecture.md). The writing layer's design decisions are recorded in [.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-22-paper-foundation-seams.md](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-22-paper-foundation-seams.md); the product identity and namespace decisions are recorded in [.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-22-independent-product-identity.md](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-22-independent-product-identity.md). For agents, follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Contributions: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Built on the open-source DeepSeek Harness with thanks to its authors; third-party dependencies are disclosed in [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-connect-qoder

把 Qoder（通义灵码国内版 / 国际版）的模型接入 DeepSeek Harness，并提供账号池、每日签到、积分读数与模型管理。

English · 安装 · 工作原理 · 配置 · 账号池 · 更新日志 · 问题反馈

一个独立的 [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle 插件。它把 Qoder 账号的模型接到 DSH 的模型选择器，同时提供模型管理与只读的用量概览。**国内版与国际版是两个并行的供应商（`qoder` / `qoder-global`），可同时使用**；插件设置卡片以 tab 区分两者，方便统一管理。 > Qoder 官方不提供 OpenAI 兼容端点（其官方 SDK 只是 agent 启动器），因此本插件直连 Qoder 的 cosy 网关，实现了协议的最小客户端，无需在 Qoder 桌面端登录——只需一个 PAT（Personal Access Token）。 ## 功能特性 - **双供应商并行接入（国内版 + 国际版）** —— 国内版注册为 `qoder` provider（`gateway.qoder.com.cn`），国际版注册为 `qoder-global` provider（`api1.qoder.sh`）。**配置了 PAT 的区域其模型会出现在 DSH 模型选择器里**：两个区域都有 PAT 时两组同时可选，不同会话可以各选一边，互不干扰。**没有 PAT 的区域不列出任何模型**（一个请求也发不出去，列出来只会点到就失败）；配置 PAT 后「刷新模型」即可让模型自动出现——provider 本身始终注册着，因为它的设置卡片正是配置入口。模型名内嵌上游积分倍率（如 `Qwen3.8-Flash · x0.00`），与 Qoder 自身模型菜单一致。 - **插件卡片 tab 切换** —— 设置卡片顶部为「国内版 / 国际版」两个 tab，各含独立的 PAT、模型管理与用量概览；每个 tab 的目录、勾选与状态完全隔离。 - **正文按「账号 / 模型 / 诊断」分栏** —— 每个区域 tab 之下再把正文分成三栏。账号栏是账号池、积分读数开关与关于凭据的每一条说明（点一下即生效）；模型栏是勾选、上下文档位、思考强度与逐模型测试（草稿，点「保存」才落地）——两者的提交语义本来就不同，分开之后保存按钮就挨着它保存的东西。**切栏不重新拉取、不丢未保存的草稿**（非活动栏仍挂载）。诊断栏是一张只读的事实表：区域、**上游域名**（与真正发请求的主机名同一处事实）、服务账号、凭据来源、积分读取时刻、目录模型数、已启用数、账号池开关，以及上游最近一次错误的**原文**——它存在的唯一理由是被整段贴进问题反馈，所以里面没有任何会改设置的控件。 - **可单独关闭任一版本供应商** —— 每个 tab 右侧有一个勾选框（默认都勾选）。**取消勾选即把该供应商从 DSH 模型选择器里彻底撤掉**（不是只藏起 tab）：它的路由与「设置 → 模型」页的目录条目一并摘除。PAT、用量与勾选**全部保留**，重新勾选即完整恢复。注意：若某会话此前选中的正是被关闭供应商的模型，该会话再调用会报 `NO_ADAPTER`。 - **模型管理** —— 从上游刷新完整模型目录，逐项勾选启用或禁用；模型行显示倍率（`(0.50x)`）、上下文/输出上限、思考强度档位与免费标记，行右有「图片」「可关闭思考」开关、上下文档位选择器与「测试」按钮。勾选状态写入本地配置，立即同步到模型选择器。**目录里有几个模型就排几行，列表自己不设高度上限、不出内滚动条**——这条列表的用途是「看见并勾选模型」，只露七八行、把其余的藏进第二条滚动条（面板本身已经在滚）会让「有这个模型吗」变成一个需要先发现、再去拖的动作；要看全就滚页面。**上游的 `auto` 不列出来**：它是该区的默认**路由**，网关在请求时才决定把它解析成哪个模型，所以价格与上下文都由别人临时决定，插件无法如实描述——它不是模型，不该占一行让你勾选。 - **活动优惠徽标** —— 上游在模型目录里自带活动规则（`promotion`：文案、时段、时区），模型行就在名字旁画一枚小胶囊，如「错峰 4 折」。**文案原样来自上游**（中文界面取 `badge.zh`，英文界面取 `badge.en`），插件不翻译也不改写；悬停给出上游的说明、时段与时区，以及活动文档链接原文。什么时候画由**渲染时刻**决定：有上游声明的墙钟时段（支持跨零点、按上游时区算）就按时段现算，没有时段才退回上游的 `active`——所以夜里读到的目录不会把徽标冻结到第二天早上，早上启动的进程也不会因此整晚不显示；没有活动字段的模型什么都不画。同一枚徽标也画在宿主的**模型选择器**里（`conversation.input.model.label` 槽位，issue #12）——选择器才是做选择的地方，与卡片共用同一套判定、文案与样式。取证与判定规则见 [docs/PROMO_BADGE.md](docs/PROMO_BADGE.md)。 - **模型可用性测试** —— 每个模型行有一个「测试」按钮，直达上游确认该模型此刻能否使用：限流（429）报「被限流」、凭据无效报「凭据无效」、内容审核拒绝报「内容被审核拒绝」、额度耗尽报「额度已耗尽」，其余上游瞬时故障如实分类。探测在后台发起，**凭据不会传到页面**；结果不写入设置，也不改变你已保存的勾选。**它发的是真实请求**（会消耗少量上游额度），因此只能按单个模型手工点，没有「测试已勾选」这类批量按钮。 - **每日签到** —— Qoder 有官方每日签到活动（个人用户每天可领 100 Credits，30 天有效）。账号池提供「一键签到所有账号」：逐账号领取、已领过的按幂等处理（不重复领取、不算失败），签到后积分自动刷新。国内版与国际版都已接通（国际版需要本机 Qoder 客户端的设备风控组件，取不到时如实报错而不是假装「今天没有活动」）。 - **活动（只读）** —— 卡片在区域作用域内、额度读数之下多一条「活动」列表，逐条列出上游当前下发的活动：每日 100 Credits 签到行（带额度与「可领取 / 已领取」状态）与「1024 创造力集结」「首月订阅 Credits 翻倍」这类 banner（`VIEW_DETAILS`）。**标题与描述原样来自上游**（按界面语言取 `zh` / `en`，缺哪边用另一边），「查看详情」是真正的链接（上游的 `detailUrl`，缺失时退回活动落地页）；**只读**，不签到、不改账号。上游没下发就显示「当前没有活动」，读不到则显示原因（不是装作没有）。此前本插件只读签到用的那一小片活动数据，banner 行被整行跳过（用户实拍 2026-10-25），现已整份读取。 - **积分（只读）** —— 账号池逐账号显示剩余积分与最近积分包的到期时间（来自 Qoder 的 `sash/api/v2/me/usage`，凭 `jt-` jobToken 查询）；临期的积分包会高亮。查询是**只读**的、不消耗积分；读不到时（凭据被拒 / 上游未响应）如实说明原因并给出路，不留一片空白。 - **安全 loopback shim** —— 每区域一个随机端口 + 进程内随机 secret，真实 Qoder PAT **不交给 pi-ai**：pi-ai 只与本地 shim 对话，shim 用 cosy 会话（jobToken）做上游请求。 - **多账号池（PAT）** —— 每区域一个本地 vault `$DSH_HOME/.qoder-accounts..json`（0600），把设置 PAT、环境变量与 vault 账号三源去重合并；卡片可新增（粘贴 `pt-…`，经 `JobToken` 交换校验并取显示名，也可自填备注名）/ 改名账号，也可显式选择某一账号服务（`regions..accountId`，留空自动按 settings → env → vault 选取）。**移出池**与**删除**是两件事：移出池 = 在池表格里取消勾选并保存（凭据留着，随时勾回）；删除 = 池表格行内的「删除」按钮，二次确认后抹掉 vault 里的 PAT 并自动退出池与区域选择（不可恢复；设置/环境变量里的 PAT 不归本插件管，不提供删除按钮）。 - **按实测排序与自动换号** —— 「一键测试所有账号」对池内每个成员发真实请求（目标模型默认自动挑本区域倍率为 0 的免费模型），结果落 `$DSH_HOME/.qoder-pool..json`；开启账号池后，聊天流在首字节前按 `rankPool`（可用性 → 快过期的积分优先 → 到期最近 → 积分高 → id）选出服务账号，失败时依次换下一个可用账号重试，失败回写 `live-request` 探测。关掉开关则插件不替你选、也不替你换，失败如实报错。**上游报额度耗尽必显示**：对话路径上一旦上游的业务码命中配额族（110 当日用量 / 113 配额 / 118 Credits 耗尽等），该区域卡片就出现一条「上游报额度耗尽」通知（最近一次时刻 + 业务码，悬停是脱敏后的上游原文）——与账号池开关无关，因为逐账号的 `out-of-credit` 明细只活在池视图里，池关着时这条通知是那次失败**唯一**可见的出口（0.7.x 的「今日额度疑似已用尽」胶囊拆掉后留下的缺口）。限流（HTTP 429 短窗）**不会**被标成耗尽——那是冷却，不是没额度。 - **账号转移（导入 / 导出）** —— 按区域把 vault 账号导出为传输文件，预览后按索引导入；跨区域域名（`qoder.com.cn` / `qoder.sh`）正向匹配，不匹配的记录计入 `skipped`。 - **思考强度与上下文预算** —— 上游按模型声明 `thinking_config.efforts`，卡片只列出**真实存在**的档位（Qwen 系 `low/medium/xhigh`、DeepSeek/GLM 系 `low/high/max`），选定即保存、每个请求自动带上（与 Qoder 客户端同一发送字段，双写顶层与 `parameters`）；上下文档位同样只来自上游 `context_config` 声明的档位，未声明时不渲染控件、不编造选项。 - **诚实的模型能力** —— 上游的 `is_vl` 是**平台**的图片输入声明而非模型原生能力，且它对几乎每个模型都是 `true`，所以本插件**不拿它当能力答案**，只认一张按精确 model id 键控的核对表：核对过的才预勾选，没核实的（含全新模型）一律不勾，并在开关 tooltip 里说明「为什么没勾」。表的依据是**厂商文档 + 真机实测**：2026-10-29 用「发一张画着数字 `7` 的图、问是哪个数字」逐个测了**两个区域目录并集里的全部 14 个模型**，**全部读图成功**，因此当前目录里没有纯文本模型（此前按命名推断的「code 系模型应是纯文本」被实测推翻）。「关闭思考」同样只对上游显式声明、且不在已知拒绝集里的模型提供。宁可少给一个选项，也不要让用户按下去就失败。 - **缓存命中如实上报** —— 上游的 `usage` 带 `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`，插件把它一路透传到宿主，所以 GUI 轮次统计里的「缓存命中」是真实比例（修复前这里恒显 0%：字段在归一路径上被丢掉了，那个 0% 是不可信的读数，不是缓存没生效的证据）。**命中数是 `prompt_tokens` 的子集，不是额外增量**——所以它不会被加进总数（那会把命中的前缀算两遍）。上游没报这个字段时就不写，不会用 0 顶替「不知道」。 - **composer 积分读数（位置可选）** —— 会话输入区按区域显示 `QD CN` / `QD AI` 与**当前计费账号**的余额（如 `QD CN · 92`；池接管时是接管者的余额，悬停写明归属），点开是逐账号的余额表，点某一行即切换到该账号，页头的「设置」按钮直接打开本插件的设置页；受每区域「在对话框显示积分」开关控制（默认开，opt-out）。**读数可放在两个位置之一**（卡片上的二选一下拉，每区域独立，默认不变）：**输入框工具栏**（`conversation.input.right`，紧挨模型选择器左侧、与权限切换器隔开）或**输入框下方**（`conversation.composer.dock`，即 shell 渲染轮次 / tok/s / token / 缓存命中那一行的常驻栏，读数是追加在自带统计之后）。之所以可选：输入框工具栏是**共享的 list 插槽**，另一个把东西停在那里的插件可能把读数挤到看不见——此时切到「输入框下方」即可（对齐 workbuddy issue #62）。 - **命令行诊断与现场验证** —— `dsh-connect-qoder doctor|status|logout [--json] [--region cn|global]`：`doctor` 报 PAT 来源、cosy 指纹派生、pi-ai 代际、宿主心跳存活与 vault 账号计数；`status` 报凭据来源、上游可达性与当前剩余积分；`logout` 清除指定区域的 vault 账号与账号池测量副本。另有 `pnpm run probe:cosy`（不依赖宿主直连 cosy 链路验证）与 `pnpm run probe:vault`（只读 dump vault / 账号池测量，PAT 只显示掩码）。 ## 工作原理 ```text DSH PiAiAdapter（每个 provider 一套） -> 安全 loopback shim（每区域一个随机端口 + 进程内随机 secret） -> QoderUpstreamClient（cosy 协议最小客户端） -> 国内版 https://gateway.qoder.com.cn/algo/api/v2/... -> 国际版 https://api1.qoder.sh/algo/api/v2/... -> Qoder SSE（OpenAI 形状增量） -> DSH 本地执行工具并回传结果 ``` 国内版与国际版各持一套完整的运行时栈——上游客户端、模型 catalog、回环 shim、adapter——按区域配置（网关 / openapi / 目录路径）隔离，所以**两个区域的模型可以同时可选、被不同会话使用**。 凭据是 PAT（设置卡片 `regions..pat` 或环境变量，见[配置](#配置)），设置项优先。每次会话按需惰性交换 **jobToken**：PAT 只在这个交换请求里使用一次，之后的对外请求全部携带 cosy bearer（自定义 Base64 载荷 + MD5 签名）与「机器指纹」会话头。**PAT 从不进入 pi-ai，也从不外发到网关之外；本插件不读不写 Qoder 桌面端的本地登录文件。** 模型的 cosy 编码与签名细节（自定义字母表、`n/3` 重排、`cosy&&` 签名、RSA/AES 会话封装）见 `src/cosy.ts` 的头部注释；错误分类（内容审核 / 限流 / 额度耗尽 / 瞬时故障）与 DSH 重试语义的对应见 `src/upstream.ts`。 ## 安装 ### 从发布包安装（推荐） ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add @dmh2002/dsh-connect-qoder # Desktop dsh plugin --profile web add @dmh2002/dsh-connect-qoder # Web ``` 装完**重启该 profile 的 DSH 进程**（bundle 的 host 半边在启动时加载）。也可以在 DSH 的「插件市场 / Bundles」里搜 `dsh-connect-qoder` 一键安装。 > **`dsh` 命令报 `Cannot find module `Qoder` / `Qoder Global` 两个分组。 ## 配置 ### PAT（Personal Access Token） 在 Qoder 账户设置里创建 PAT（`pt-…` 开头）。两种提供方式，**设置卡片优先于环境变量**： | 区域 | 发证入口 | 设置项 | 环境变量 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 国内版（qoder.com.cn） | 控制台 → 设置 → API 令牌 | 卡片「国内版」tab → 添加 PAT | `QODERCN_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` | | 国际版（qoder.sh） | 控制台 → Settings → Personal Access Tokens | 卡片「国际版」tab → 添加 PAT | `QODER_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` | - PAT 只保存到本地插件配置（`regions..pat`），从不上传、不进入任何网络请求。 - 未配置 PAT 的区域不列出任何模型；`doctor` 命令会指出哪个区域缺 PAT。 - **逐步操作说明见 [`docs/PAT.md`](docs/PAT.md)**（含创建流程、验证机制、优先级与常见问题）。 ### 区域启停 卡片每个 tab 右侧的勾选框控制该区域是否参与模型选择（opt-out：**显式取消勾选才停用**）。停用只摘除路由与目录条目，配置全部保留。 ### 侧边栏面板（可选，默认关闭） 卡片「账号」栏里有一行「在侧边栏显示 Qoder」：勾上之后，DSH 侧边栏会多一个 Qoder 图标行，点开就是**这张卡片的整页版**（同样的账号池、模型目录、诊断栏，只是占满中央那一列），页头带一个「返回会话」。 - **默认关闭，且是一次显式的 opt-in**。这一行占的是 `sidebar.panellist` —— **所有插件共用的全局侧边栏座位**，点开还会接管中央面板，所以打开它是对你整个侧边栏的决定，不是对这张卡片的偏好。「插件」页本来就能看到同一张卡片，所以没主动勾过的人**升级后界面不会有任何变化**。 - **点一下即生效，不用保存**。关掉时如果整页正开着，中央那一列会自动回到对话（宿主会丢掉 `main` key 已不存在的那次选中）。 - 存为顶层配置项 `sidebarPanel`（**没有区域轴**：侧边栏只有一行、一个整页，与国内版/国际版无关）。所以某一区域签出、甚至两个区域都关掉时它仍可打开——面板本身就是你去添加第一个 PAT 的地方之一。 - 判据是 `=== true`：缺席、`false`、以及被手工改成字符串 `"true"` 的垃圾值，一律读作关闭。 ### 多账号池与凭据来源 除设置 PAT 与环境变量外，每区域还有一个本地 vault（`$DSH_HOME/.qoder-accounts..json`，权限 0600）保存多个 PAT 账号。三源按 **settings → env → vault** 的优先级去重合并（同一个 PAT 只在最高优先级的来源里列出一次）。 - 卡片可新增（粘贴 `pt-…`，经 `JobToken` 交换校验并取回显示名，也可自填备注名）/ 改名 vault 账号，也可显式选择某一账号服务（`regions..accountId`，留空自动）。删除 vault 账号在池表格的行内「删除」按钮（需二次确认）；取消勾选并保存只是把它移出轮换，PAT 仍留在本地。 - 选中的凭据只用于会话的 jobToken 交换与后续 cosy 请求，从不进入 pi-ai 或页面。 - `logout [--region cn|global]` 会清除指定区域的 vault 账号与账号池测量副本（`$DSH_HOME/.qoder-accounts..json` 与 `.qoder-pool..json`）。 - 勾选成员、一键签到、一键测试与自动换号的规则见[账号池](#账号池)。 ## 账号池 一台机器上往往有多个 Qoder 账号（多个 PAT）。**账号池**把这些账号收成一次点击：勾进池子，然后「一键签到所有账号」或「一键测试所有账号」；再打开**启用账号池**，插件就会在请求失败时自动换号接着跑。 **每个区域（国内版 / 国际版）各有独立的一池**：成员、目标模型、积分与签到状态互不影响——两边的账号本来就属于不同的供应商。**两个区域都有每日签到**：国际版的签到活动只下发给带设备风控头的请求，插件按区域读取本机 Qoder 客户端自带的设备身份组件；取不到时如实报错，不会把「拿不到设备身份」伪装成「今天没有活动」。 ### 自动换号（开启账号池即生效） - **谁来服务由排序决定**：开启后**每一次请求**都发给池内排序最靠前的可用账号，所以「当前使用」显示的是排序的结果，不一定是你手动选的那个。 - **失败时继续往下试**：某个请求在上游失败时，插件**依次**用池内其他可用账号重试，直到有一个接手、或全部不可用为止才把错误报出来。 - **哪些失败会换号**：429 限流、额度耗尽、401/403 凭据被拒、5xx 网关与网络故障——这些都是**某个账号**的状态，换一个很可能就过了。 - **哪些不会**：请求本身不合法（HTTP 400）——同一个请求体换谁都是同样的 400，重试只是让你多等几轮；**流已开始之后**也不会重放（字节已经发出去了）。 - **已知不可用的账号会被跳过**：处于限流冷却期内、或凭据已被上游拒绝的成员不参与选择。**从没测过的账号按「默认可用」参与**——刚添加的账号不该因为「还没测」就被排除。 - **手动选择从不被改写**：池子通过运行时覆盖决定「谁服务」，**不写回你保存的选择**；关掉开关，你选定的账号立刻完全生效。 - **失败会被记下来**：一次失败会写成该账号的测量（含上游报文中给出的恢复时间），下一个请求直接从可用账号开始，不必每次先撞一遍同一个限流账号。 - **换号会告诉你**：换号是插件替你做的决定，所以它会说出来——回答开头带一条引用块提示，例如 `> [dsh-connect-qoder] 「450702134816」被限流，已改用池中另一个账号回答。`。提示说的是**失败的那个账号**（你选中的那个），不点名接管者；连换多次只写一条，说的是紧邻换号的那次失败。没换号就一个字都不写。 ### 这个开关到底控制什么 **它只控制「插件要不要自己决定」，不控制「你能不能操作」。** | | 账号池 **开启** | 账号池 **关闭** | | --- | --- | --- | | 谁服务 | 由排序**自动**选出（可用优先 → 积分包快过期 → 到期最近 → 积分高 → id） | **你**在设置区的「使用哪个账号」里选定 | | 请求失败 | **自动**换下一个可用账号重试 | 不换号，如实报错 | | 一键签到 / 一键测试 | 可用 | **仍然可用** | | 目标测试模型 | 可改 | **仍然可改** | 最后两行是刻意的：签到与测试是**手动动作**，作用于你勾选的成员，与「插件是否自动路由」是两件事。 **唯一的硬约束**：池里一个成员都没勾选时，批量动作一律拒绝。空的池**绝不**退化成「那就对全部账号执行」——那是唯一会花掉你没授权过的积分的解读。 ### 重试预算可以调（`regions..retry`） 宿主有一个「原地重试」环：一次请求失败但值得再试时，它等一小段时间再发一次。等待阶梯由插件声明、宿主执行，默认跟随宿主（不填就是宿主的默认值，升级不会改变你现在的行为）。 Qoder 上游偶尔会回 `RESOURCE_LIMIT`（业务码 `10605`）并**自己申报**「请等 N 秒再来」。插件现在会把这个值写进给宿主的失败文案（形如 `[upstream retry-after 5s]`），你能直接看出上游只要求等多久，而不是只看到「上游报了个 4xx」。 想改预算就配这三个数字（都在区域级，两个区域各配各的）： ```yaml regions: cn: retry: maxRetries: 4 # 最多重试几次（0 = 跟随宿主默认） initialDelayMs: 5000 # 首次退避毫秒（0 = 跟随宿主默认） maxDelayMs: 30000 # 退避上限毫秒（0 = 跟随宿主默认） ``` 上面的 `5000 → 30000` 兼顾了上游两种常见形态：瞬时限流（申报 5 秒）与 `queueType:p2` 排队（约 30 秒）。**三个 0 表示跟随宿主默认**，所以留空与不写这个配置等价。 > 此前这一项只能是宿主的默认值，想调就得改 `node_modules` 里的构建产物 —— 而那会在升级时静默还原。 ### 排序规则（开启账号池后决定谁服务） 1. **可用优先** —— 被测量判定为不可用（限流未到恢复时间、凭据被拒等）的排到最后； 2. **积分高者优先** —— 只在有**新鲜读数**时参与（卡片轮询、批量测试或保存时读到的那份，10 分钟内有效）：请求路径**不会**为了排序去打上游，否则一页对话就变成 N 个额外请求； 3. **快过期的积分包优先** —— 3 天内到期的先花，过期即作废； 4. 最后按账号 id 收尾，保证顺序是**全序**、可复现。 ### 两个批量动作 - **一键签到所有账号** —— 逐个账号领取当日的官方签到活动。**先查状态再领取**，已领过的直接标「已签到」而**不发写入请求**（幂等，不重复领取）；任何单个账号失败只标记该行，**不中断整批**。签到会改变余额，因此批次结束后作废该区域的积分缓存，卡片不会继续显示领取前的数字。 - **一键测试所有账号** —— 对每个成员发一次真实请求，得出「这个账号此刻能不能用这个模型」。目标模型默认由「自动」挑本区域**倍率为 0 的免费模型**（多个候选取上下文窗口最大的），你也可以显式指定——但**在免费模型出现之前测试保持关闭**，避免在你不知情的情况下花掉积分。测试走的是与模型行同一套探测，因此**有真实成本**。 两种批量动作都**不锁住界面**：按钮自己变成「签到中… / 测试中…」，每处理完一个账号，那一行立刻落位、活动日志也**逐条**写下（时间戳是各自完成的那一刻，不是整批结束的那一秒）；其余界面照常可用。只有**保存配置**与**删除账号**会挡一道——前者在写盘、后者不可逆。 设置卡片的排布：顶部是**两格独立的供应商卡片**（国内版 / 国际版），每格自带边框与底色、右端有自己的开关，选中的那格描品牌色边——**一格就是一个单位**，点名字切 tab、点开关启用该供应商。再往下是「在对话框显示积分」与「显示位置」两行（整行可点，主标题下一行是说明），第三行是**可选的「在侧边栏显示 Qoder」**，然后是账号池、模型管理。这三行都是**立即生效，不需要点保存**：前两行管积分读数显不显示、显示在哪里，第三行管侧边栏那一行（以及它打开的整页）在不在。 不提供**自动**签到：签到会真实领取奖励，只在你点按钮时执行。 ## 命令行诊断 在**已装本插件的 profile 目录里**跑（推荐，无需全局安装）： ```bash cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop pnpm exec dsh-connect-qoder doctor # PAT 来源 + cosy 指纹派生 + pi-ai 代际 + 心跳 + vault 计数（纯本地，不发请求） pnpm exec dsh-connect-qoder status # 每区域凭据来源 + 上游模型目录可达性 + 剩余积分（需 PAT） pnpm exec dsh-connect-qoder logout --region cn # 清除指定区域的 vault 账号与账号池测量副本 pnpm exec dsh-connect-qoder doctor --json # 机器可读输出 ``` `status` 会真实交换一次 jobToken 并拉取模型目录（随后只读查询一次用量），因此需要对应区域的环境变量或 vault PAT；`doctor` 完全离线。 > **两条实测过的注意事项**： > 1. **别用 `node node_modules/dsh-connect-qoder/lib/bin.js` 这种裸路径**——0.3.0 起包名带作用域，软链在 `node_modules/@dmh2002/dsh-connect-qoder`，写旧路径只会得到 `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`（缺的是**入口文件**，不是 peer）。 > 2. CLI 依赖宿主提供的 peer 包（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write` / `dsh-home-paths`）。本机实测：pnpm 会随包把它们装进 profile 的依赖树，`pnpm exec` 与 npm 装的 tarball 都能跑通。但这**取决于 pnpm 版本与 `auto-install-peers` 配置**——如果在你机器上报 `Cannot find package '@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write'`，那是这一层没装上；设置卡片与 provider **不受影响**（它们在宿主进程内，宿主自己解析这些名字）。同族 workbuddy 的 issue #47 是同一个形状，其修复方案（宿主优先、按需回落自带实现）适用于本项目，尚未移植。 ## 平台支持 | 平台 | 状态 | | --- | --- | | macOS | ✅ 已验证（开发与 CI） | | Windows | ✅ CI 测试通过（上游请求走标准 fetch，无平台专属路径） | | Linux | ✅ CI 测试通过 | ## 受支持的宿主范围 | 宿主 | peer 范围 | | --- | --- | | DSH（`@deepseek-ai/*`） | `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.2.0-0 \|\| >=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0 \|\| >=0.2.1-rc.1 <0.3.0-0` | | `@earendil-works/pi-ai` | `>=0.85.0 <0.88.0 \|\| >=1.0.0 <2.0.0` | | Node.js | `^22.19.0 \|\| >=24.0.0` | > 范围由 `tests/dsh-line.spec.ts` 强制。DSH 至今只发预发布，而 node-semver 只有当范围里*某个*比较符与该版本的 `major.minor.patch` 元组完全一致、且自身也带预发布标签时，才会放行预发布版本。所以每开一条新线就得加一条分支：只写 `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.3.0-0` 会**静默排除整条 `0.2.0-rc.*`**（`0.2.0-rc.2` 曾是 `latest`），同理 `>=0.2.0-rc.1` 这一支**不含 `0.2.1-rc.1`**（桌面端 0.2.1-rc.1 已发布）。上界仍须带 `-0`（`<0.3.0` 不挡任何东西）。 > > **两套语义并存**（1.1.2 实测更正）：npm / pnpm 安装走 node-semver **标准**语义，新补丁号的 rc（如 `0.2.2-rc.1`）**确实**仍需手工追加一条分支 —— `UNGATED_PRERELEASES` 就是这份可见的待办表。但**宿主的插件兼容门禁不是标准语义**：`dsh-app-boot` 用 `semver.satisfies(v, range, { includePrerelease: true })`，在这个语义下 `>=0.2.1-rc.1 <0.3.0-0` 一支就覆盖**整条 `0.2.x` 线**（`0.2.2-rc.1`、`0.2.9` 都放行），`0.3.0-rc.1` 仍被上界拦住。1.1.0/1.1.1 曾断言「没有任何静态范围能覆盖任意 `0.2.x` 预发布」，那句话只对 npm 成立，对宿主门禁不成立，已更正。GA 版本（如 `0.2.1`）对既有分支本来就判 true。 > > **pi-ai 单独列一行**是因为它换了主版本：0.2.1-rc.1 宿主把 pi-ai 从 0.85 换到 1.x，而两代的上下文契约不同（1.x 在 Models 层归一化）。声明与检测必须一致，否则就是 1.1.0 修掉的那个静默丢工具缺陷 —— 详见 [`docs/DSH-0.2.1-RC1-FOLLOWUP.md`](docs/DSH-0.2.1-RC1-FOLLOWUP.md)。 ### 当前宿主基线：0.2.1-rc.5（2026-10-30 实测） 宿主升到 `0.2.1-rc.5`（`DeepSeek Harness.app`，nightly 通道；`app.asar` 内全部 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 均为 `0.2.1-rc.5`，内置 pi-ai `1.1.0`）。**本插件不需要任何运行时代码改动**，理由逐条如下： | 检查项 | 结论 | | --- | --- | | 插件依赖的宿主包（`dsh-llm` / `dsh-llm-pi-ai` / `dsh-settings` / `dsh-atomic-write` / `dsh-attachment` / `dsh-host-webserver` / `dsh-home-paths` / `dsh-client-ui-slots` / `dsh-client-ui-settings` / `dsh-client-ui-settings-plugins` / `dsh-client-ui-renderer` / `dsh-client-locale` / `dsh-client-ui-primitives`） | 与 rc.3 **逐字节相同**（仅 `package.json` 的版本号不同） | | 宿主内置 pi-ai | `1.1.0`（rc.3 起未变）—— `generationOf()` 仍判 `modern` | | `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` | `3.18.5`（rc.3 的 `3.18.4` → `3.18.5`）；两个版本的 `lib/` 与 `src/` **逐字节相同**，只有 `package.json` 版本号不同，落在声明的 `>=3.18.2 <4.0.0` 内 | | rc.4 / rc.5 的运行时改动 | 共 13 个提交，非版本号改动只有 40 个文件；**没有一条**落在插件导入的宿主包上 | | 插件用到的三个槽位 | `conversation.input.model.label`、`conversation.input.right`、`conversation.composer.dock` 的 `kind` / `scope` / 注册字段 / owner props 在 rc.3→rc.5 **逐字未变** | | `plugins.bundle.config` / `plugins.row.config` | keyed 槽位的 `key` 语义（裸包名 / `<包名>#<行 id>`）未变，卡片照常挂载 | | 插件在 rc.5 上的实际加载 | `Config` 目录里 `include:dsh-connect-qoder` 状态 `schema`；四个槽位占用者全部 `active: true`，其中模型标签由 `dsh-connect-qoder-client`（priority `-1`）占据 | | peer 范围 | `evaluatePluginCompatibility(manifest, {}, '0.2.1-rc.5')` → `undefined`（= 兼容）；rc.3 / rc.4 / rc.5 三者都放行 | | 回归 | `pnpm run typecheck` 与 `pnpm test`（1032 passed / 8 skipped）全绿 | rc.4 / rc.5 的改动**全部**落在本插件不涉及的面上： - **rc.4 的推理 Body Slot 字段分裂**（`conversation.chat.reasoning.body` 新增 `rawText`，`text` 改为「已处理的显示文本」）：这是本轮**唯一**的破坏性扩展点，宿主为此专门发了 `docs/upgrade-guide/v0.2.1-rc.4/reasoning-body-props/` 迁移指南。**本插件不注册该槽位**（`src/` 与构建产物 `lib/client.js` 里都没有 `conversation.chat.` 开头的注册），所以不受影响；受影响的只有 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-cot-translation` 那类包装组件。 - **rc.4 把两处诊断从 stdout 挪到 stderr**（`llm-deepseek-account` 的模型目录、`mcp-client` 的资源列表），因为 ACP 档案的 stdout 专供 JSON-RPC。本插件的宿主半边**从不写 stdout**（只用 `ctx.logger`，`src/bin.ts` 的 stdout 属于独立 CLI），因此无泄漏面。 - **rc.4 去掉 `session.moreViewsCurrent` 语言键**、View 标签页 tooltip 改为按溢出才显示：本插件没有使用该键，也不渲染 View 标签页。 - **rc.5 只改推理块的显示预处理**（`reasoningText()` 剥离 `` 包裹）：本插件产出的是标准 `reasoning_content` 增量，不含 `` 包装。 > rc.3 带来的**环境**变化（不是插件的问题）：宿主 app 目录名从 `DSH NEXT.app` 变为 `DeepSeek Harness.app`，旧路径上的 `dsh` shim 会失效 —— 见[安装](#安装)一节的说明。 ## 安全说明 - PAT 只写入本地插件配置（或环境变量），**从不进入任何网络请求**；对外请求一律使用 cosy 会话令牌（jobToken）+ 机器指纹头。 - 本地 shim 用随机端口的 loopback 服务 + 进程内 secret 鉴权，并校验 Host / Origin / Content-Type，请求体有 64MB 上限。 - 本插件只读你显式提供的 PAT；**不读取、不修改** Qoder 桌面端的本地登录/凭据文件。 - 诊断输出（`doctor` / `status` 与卡片探测）均脱敏，不打印任何令牌样式的字符串。 ## 市场收录与展示 本插件声明了可安装的 `dsh.bundle` manifest（`dsh.bundle.patch: ./cordis.patch.yml`），因此可以用 `dsh plugin add` 安装。社区市场通常从 [Awesome DSH Plugin](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin) 注册表同步条目；仓库内的提交草稿位于 [`awesome-dsh-plugin-submission/dingminhua__dsh-connect-qoder.yml`](awesome-dsh-plugin-submission/dingminhua__dsh-connect-qoder.yml)。 **收录目录规范**（依据 [contributing.md](https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/blob/main/contributing.md)）： - 每个插件一个 YAML：`data/plugins/__.yml`，字段为 `url`（与仓库地址完全一致）、`name`（`owner/repo`）、`category`（有效值之一，本项目为 `model`）、`description.en`（必填，以句号结尾）/ `description.zh`（可选）；描述中含 `: ` 必须加引号。 - 仓库需声明 `dsh.bundle` manifest、被 `dsh-plugin` topic 标记、创建满 1 天且处于活跃维护；描述必须属实、不带营销词——它会被逐条对照代码核对。 - 注册表的两个 README 由脚本生成，不得手工编辑；修改 YAML 后在其仓库执行 `npm ci` + `node scripts/generate-readme.mjs` 重新生成。 - 一个 PR 最多收录 3 条；只改自己的条目。 市场卡片中的截图与 GitHub README 徽章是两套机制： - **市场截图**按当前约定由**插件自己仓库根目录的 `screenshots.json`** 声明（本项目声明了 [screenshots.json](screenshots.json)）；注册表的 `data/screenshots.json` 是旧约定下的回退，**不再添加新键**。 - **GitHub 徽章**由本 README 顶部的 Shields 图片链接生成；**市场图标/占位图**由具体市场的展示规则决定，不是 npm 字段，也不是 README 徽章。 ## 已知限制 - 依赖 Qoder 的 cosy 网关与 `sash` 接口（**非官方开放 API**），上游变动后插件可能需要随之调整。协议行为参照 [Zhengyuuuui/qoder2api](https://github.com/Zhengyuuuui/qoder2api)，本项目独立实现，不复制其源码。 - **每日签到**是 Qoder 面向**个人用户**的运营活动（企业版账号不参与），规则与额度以官方为准；国际版的签到活动要求请求带本机 Qoder 客户端的设备身份，因此**未安装 Qoder 客户端的机器上国际版签到不可用**（插件如实报错，不静默降级）。 - 图片输入与「可关闭思考」按**已核实**的清单给出：清单外的模型一律不预勾选，因此某些其实可用的模型可能需要你手动勾一次。**图片开关是白名单**——保存过一次选择后，未勾的模型就是关着的；把勾全部取消再保存，它们会保持关闭，不会被默认值重新打开。 - workbuddy 的修复方案（宿主优先、按需回落自带实现）适用于本项目，尚未移植。 ## 免责声明 - 本项目**仅供个人学习和研究使用**，仅驱动使用者自己的 Qoder 账号在本机调用，请勿用于商业用途或超出个人合理使用的场景。 - 使用者需遵守 Qoder / 通义灵码的服务条款；因使用本项目产生的任何后果（包括但不限于账号被限制、额度被清空、服务中断），由使用者自行承担。 -
