## Built-in component intelligence

Uiverse component reuse is a core feature of intelligent UI, shared by frontend development and live content presentation.

| Path | Automatic behavior | Source evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intelligent content rendering | Local analyzers recognize charts, tasks, records and flows; semantic roles select approved card/control adapters while keeping the chosen theme. Empryo and other v1 themes participate automatically; explicit component themes keep their selection. | Fifteen compiled source-backed adaptations carry original component IDs and SHA-256 on rendered elements. |
| Frontend development | The model discovers the bundled skill for frontend/UI tasks, searches suitable components and reads their complete source before adapting new controls. Existing suitable project controls take precedence. | All **3,802 components in 11 categories** from the official Galaxy snapshot, with authors, license, original source and hashes. |
| Source-preserving review | Original/comparison views retain text, tables, units and qualifications; isolated previews can be inspected within the authorized task. | The same pinned archive backs lookup and live adapter provenance. |

The archive pin is [`adbd2adde0a299a3956ea288fb444ec01891ca41`](https://github.com/uiverse-io/galaxy/tree/adbd2adde0a299a3956ea288fb444ec01891ca41), dated 2024-09-02. It is a complete snapshot of that archive, rather than a current full-site mirror. Live presentation uses the curated compiled adaptations; the full archive supplies development lookup and sandbox previews. OpenUI still owns its chart marks and native form internals.

The component capability is silent: it adds no library sidebar, page or popup. Its model-invocable skill loads on demand through DSH's official skill mechanism. `solar_ui_search`, `solar_ui_source` and `solar_ui_preview` are included in this plugin; a separately installed component plugin is unnecessary. Normal tool history and the owner's permissions remain in effect. Actual model selection varies with the model and task; runtime semantic layout selection itself requires no extra model call.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Original content] --> B[Local semantic analysis]
  B --> C[Component role selection]
  C --> D[Theme-consistent live adapters]
  U[Pinned Uiverse archive] --> C
  U --> S[Silent frontend skill and tools]
```

See [component architecture and boundaries](docs/design/integrated-uiverse.md), [runtime selector](src/uiverse-render.ts), [silent Host capability](src/uiverse/host.ts) and [source manifest](resources/uiverse/upstream.json).

## Research workspace (preview)

The conversation-level **研究工作区** control adds report, judgments, sources and technical-comparison views inside the current UI-owned output. Reading remains source-preserving. Citation links and table cells open the report-local evidence inspector; returning to a source block retains the report. The inspector distinguishes a reference recorded in the report from an independently checked external source.

The first six components cover judgments, conditions, evidence inspection, technical comparisons, alternative/challenging material and open questions. Explicitly different conditions are grouped separately for charts while every original table row stays available. No causal edge, statistical significance or numeric confidence is invented.

**AI 整理** is opt-in: review its inline fee notice and start a visible request in the current conversation using its selected model. The plugin does not change model/provider/tool settings. The requested task is organization of supplied report text; execution still follows the existing session's permissions, not a new isolated research engine. Returned quote anchors and report identity are checked, but AI interpretations remain **待复核**. Human notes/review and editable question drafts are stored separately. Follow-up drafts are copy-only and never sent automatically.

Research metadata lives only in this plugin's `research/` namespace. Reopening the same source restores its notes; changed source text cannot silently reuse a pending analysis. Uncertain submissions are not replayed. No other plugin's code, original report or session data is rewritten. Cross-session topics, autonomous research, cross-report change analysis and scenario simulation are future work.

This is source/build candidate behavior; the new archive requires centralized Desktop installation acceptance. See [design and interfaces](docs/design/research-workspace.md) and the [candidate acceptance record](docs/acceptance/2026-11-01-research-workspace.md). Screenshots and private runtime receipts are never committed or uploaded.

## What it does

- Optional takeover of standard assistant/tool output and generated content. One conversation-level **显示** control switches visual, original and comparison views.
- Local content analysis chooses suitable icons, charts, table columns, relationship graphs, read-only task boards and list/detail layouts. It preserves original text, cells, units, qualifications and complete tables. Unsupported content remains readable; no model call is required to choose a layout.
- Unmodified OpenUI components supply Markdown, charts, forms and streaming UI. React Flow and ELK supply source-relationship diagrams with animated edges, pause, pan/zoom and keyboard selection. Edges describe source relationships and do not assert that work executed.
- Content-aware Uiverse adapters are selected automatically for supported UI-owned semantic surfaces. Three explicit component themes also supply coordinated buttons, inputs, toggles, cards and loaders, with original-source comparison. Foreign pages retain token/CSS appearance compatibility and their original behavior. See [mapping and compatibility](docs/design/uiverse-component-themes.md).
- Selectable data-only themes control color, typography, roundness, density, depth and transparency. Compatible independent conversation pages receive reversible appearance rules while retaining their original components and behavior.
- An optional, explicitly configured MCP Apps adapter preserves UI metadata and uses an isolated bridge. Existing MCP connections are untouched. This connector remains off by default.

The official DSH navigation and settings stay in place. Disabling takeover restores original output/page presentation. Disabling or uninstalling this plugin removes its owned styles, controls and listeners; retained plugin data remains in its own namespace. It does not patch foreign plugin packages, source or configuration.

Compatibility target: **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2**, macOS arm64. Install a built archive through the official plugin manager. Back up affected profile configuration and quit the app before updating an existing installation:

```sh

See [design / compatibility](docs/design/paper-flow.md).

**界面主题** includes built-in Empryo and **简洁**. The default online source also offers **炭墨 · Carbon**, **钴夜 · Cobalt**, **暖金 · Amber** and **雾白 · Porcelain**, adapted from the supplied Unslop references; see [theme collection and attribution](docs/design/unslop-themes.md). Import a UTF-8 `.dsh-theme.json` package, then select it; importing alone does not activate it. Download the current package or an authoring example from Settings. ### Optional MCP Apps

Set this plugin's native `mcpEndpoint` Config to the explicitly chosen HTTP(S) server and enable MCP Apps. URLs containing embedded credentials are refused. This adapter denies external resource networks, device permissions and sampling. Model/tool actions use DSH's normal tool guards; durable action receipts prevent automatically replaying an outcome that is uncertain. Opening a saved result reuses that result rather than rerunning the original tool.

## Data and boundaries

Plugin-owned data is confined to `$DSH_HOME/solar/intelligent-experience-platform/`: versioned settings, per-session artifacts, widget state and action receipts. Config limits default to 1 MiB per artifact and 500 artifacts per Session; exceeding them fails explicitly rather than silently truncating source data. Historical sessions cannot recover metadata that the original host never saved.

Appearance support is a bounded adapter to known public conversation-view outlets and neutral variables. # Real output replay fixture

Test-only plugin for `tools/real-output-demo.mjs`. It reads an existing Vitest JSON report through one real local DSH tool call, saves the exact formatted Markdown as a content artifact, and retains a normal persistent Session. Its local adapter replays actual output; it does not claim a live model chose the presentation. There is no OpenUI source, chart type or icon instruction in the output. The platform's ordinary content path performs that selection.

The helper requires absolute `--dsh-home`, `--package` (stable built `.tgz`), `--report` (actual Vitest JSON), and unused `--receipt` paths. It installs only in a unique retained test profile, blocks external model routes, checks existing profile manifests, and does not change shared presentation settings. Private reports and receipts remain outside Git.

`reportToMarkdown(report, { sha256 })` is a pure formatter exported from `index.mjs`. It preserves actual file durations without rounding, shows counts separately, and labels timings as this test run rather than a DSH performance benchmark.

# dsh-intelligent-UI

An independent open-source presentation plugin for the official DeepSeek Harness Desktop, with an offline UI component library built in. This repository contains the intelligent renderer, silent frontend-development tools and themes in one project and one installable plugin. It builds and tests on its own and uses the official application unchanged.

The historical package name **`@lisihao/dsh-solar-intelligent-experience-platform`**, RPC/tool names and data directory are retained for installed-user compatibility. They do not introduce a dependency on another project. The public preview is distributed as a prebuilt GitHub Release archive. npm publication is not required; community-market listing depends on the catalog maintainers accepting its entry.

**内置组件智能**：同一个插件包含 Uiverse 离线组件库、静默前端开发 skill 和自动内容渲染。开发时可按需检索 3,802 个真实组件；展示图表、任务、记录和流程时，自动使用 15 个经过适配验证的组件，并保留原文、数据与来源。

## Built-in component intelligence

Uiverse component reuse is a core feature of intelligent UI, shared by frontend development and live content presentation.

| Path | Automatic behavior | Source evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Intelligent content rendering | Local analyzers recognize charts, tasks, records and flows; semantic roles select approved card/control adapters while keeping the chosen theme. Empryo and other v1 themes participate automatically; explicit component themes keep their selection. | Fifteen compiled source-backed adaptations carry original component IDs and SHA-256 on rendered elements. |
| Frontend development | The model discovers the bundled skill for frontend/UI tasks, searches suitable components and reads their complete source before adapting new controls. Existing suitable project controls take precedence. | All **3,802 components in 11 categories** from the official Galaxy snapshot, with authors, license, original source and hashes. |
| Source-preserving review | Original/comparison views retain text, tables, units and qualifications; isolated previews can be inspected within the authorized task. | The same pinned archive backs lookup and live adapter provenance. |

The archive pin is [`adbd2adde0a299a3956ea288fb444ec01891ca41`](https://github.com/uiverse-io/galaxy/tree/adbd2adde0a299a3956ea288fb444ec01891ca41), dated 2024-09-02. It is a complete snapshot of that archive, rather than a current full-site mirror. Live presentation uses the curated compiled adaptations; the full archive supplies development lookup and sandbox previews. OpenUI still owns its chart marks and native form internals.

The component capability is silent: it adds no library sidebar, page or popup. Its model-invocable skill loads on demand through DSH's official skill mechanism. `solar_ui_search`, `solar_ui_source` and `solar_ui_preview` are included in this plugin; a separately installed component plugin is unnecessary. Normal tool history and the owner's permissions remain in effect. Actual model selection varies with the model and task; runtime semantic layout selection itself requires no extra model call.

```mermaid
flowchart LR

  B --> C[Component role selection]

  U[Pinned Uiverse archive] --> C

```

The conversation-level **研究工作区** control adds report, judgments, sources and technical-comparison views inside the current UI-owned output. Reading remains source-preserving. Citation links and table cells open the report-local evidence inspector; returning to a source block retains the report. The inspector distinguishes a reference recorded in the report from an independently checked external source.

The first six components cover judgments, conditions, evidence inspection, technical comparisons, alternative/challenging material and open questions. Explicitly different conditions are grouped separately for charts while every original table row stays available. No causal edge, statistical significance or numeric confidence is invented.

**AI 整理** is opt-in: review its inline fee notice and start a visible request in the current conversation using its selected model. The plugin does not change model/provider/tool settings. # dsh-plugin-shop **The plugin shop for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)** — browse, install, enable, disable, and update dsh plugins, with every catalog change tracked in Git. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-shop?logo=npm&color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-shop) [![plugins](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2FLivXue.github.io%2Fdsh-plugin-shop%2Fv1%2Findex.json&query=count&label=plugins&color=blue)](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) [![filtered](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2FLivXue.github.io%2Fdsh-plugin-shop%2Fv1%2Findex.json&query=rejected&label=filtered&color=orange)](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-plugin-shop?color=blue)](LICENSE) [![plugin CI](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop/actions/workflows/plugin.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop/actions/workflows/plugin.yml) [![catalog](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2FLivXue.github.io%2Fdsh-plugin-shop%2Fv1%2Fbadge.json)](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop/actions/workflows/daily.yml) English | [中文](README.zh.md)
--- ## 📦 Install the shop Install the shop manually, or have an agent follow the automated steps below. ### 🧑 Manual installation **Prerequisite:** Node.js. You can run DeepSeek Harness without a global installation using the command in its official documentation: `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh web`. Plugin management uses `dsh plugin`, which invokes both `dsh` and `pnpm`. Install these tools with `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh pnpm`, then check that both are available with `dsh --version` and `pnpm --version`. ```sh # With dsh installed globally, run the following command. # Specify the version: pnpm 11 restricts newly published releases by default, # so omitting the version may install an older release. The current version # is shown below; check for updates with `npm view dsh-plugin-shop version`. dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-shop@0.9.0 # Alternatively, run the installation command through npx: npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-shop@0.9.0 ``` Replace `web` with your profile name if you use a different one. Restart `dsh` after installation to load the new plugin, then open: > **Plugin shop** in the left sidebar ### 🤖 Installation with an agent An agent can run these steps without interaction. **The `--profile` option is required.** If it is omitted, `dsh plugin` exits with this error: `error: required option '--profile ' not specified`. ```sh # 1. List available profiles ($DSH_HOME defaults to ~/.dsh; exclude node_modules). ls -1 "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles" | grep -v '^node_modules$' # 2. Specify the version to bypass pnpm's release cooldown and ensure # that the expected version is installed. dsh plugin --profile add dsh-plugin-shop@0.9.0 # 3. Verify the installation; exit code 0 above only means pnpm resolved the package. dsh plugin --profile list --depth 0 # The output should include dsh-plugin-shop. # 4. Restart the profile to load the new plugin. dsh --profile ``` You can also verify step 3 by checking that `dsh.profile.bundles` in `$DSH_HOME/profiles//package.json` includes the plugin. For troubleshooting, see the [package README](packages/dsh-plugin-shop/README.md#failure-modes). ## 🖼️ Screenshots
A plugin your dsh would refuse to install says why on its card The plugin shop in dark mode
## ✨ Highlights - **🌐 Automatic discovery** — the catalog collects npm packages with the `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` keyword and GitHub repositories with either topic. Authors do not need to submit an application or join a queue. - **🧹 Strict screening** — every candidate is checked automatically on each build. Rejected plugins are recorded by name with one of seventeen predefined reasons and a detailed explanation to help authors troubleshoot. The `plugins` and `filtered` badges above show the current totals. - **🔌 Local dependency checks** — the shop checks each peer dependency a plugin requires against your profile and the modules dsh's web client provides. When the author declares which dsh versions or profiles a plugin supports, the shop also compares them with what you run. A card shows **Incompatible** only when a dependency is missing from your environment or the author's declared support does not cover it. - **🗓️ Daily updates** — the catalog is rebuilt daily, with changes committed to Git for review. Eligible new plugins are listed the next morning, and plugins whose repositories are no longer available are removed during the same process. - **🗂️ Seven categories** — authors can choose a category through `dsh.catalog`. Otherwise, the build assigns one automatically. ## 🗺️ How it works **The catalog is built daily in this repository.** The build code lives in `registry/`. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph HARVEST["1 · Discover — collect plugins from public sources daily"] direction LR NPM(["npm packages
keyword dsh-plugin
keyword deepseek-harness"]) GH(["GitHub repositories
with the same keywords
as topics"]) end subgraph GATE["2 · Screen — check every candidate on each build"] direction LR G1["Is it a loadable plugin?

Has a valid
dsh.bundle"] G2["Can it be reviewed?

Has a license and
an accessible source repository"] G3["Can it be installed?

Not deprecated on npm;
repository listings also require
no build scripts or
workspace: dependencies"] G4["Is the package information credible?

Check integrity, publication time,
and potentially misleading names"] G5["Is there information to display?

Has a valid dsh.catalog
or an npm description"] end subgraph SHELVE["3 · List — record plugin details"] direction LR CAT["One of seven categories"] PEER["Required peer dependency names,
without version ranges"] end NPM --> G1 GH --> G1 G1 -.-> REJ G2 -.-> REJ G3 -.-> REJ G4 -.-> REJ G5 -.-> REJ REJ[["Rejected — record the plugin name and explain why"]] G5 ==>|"All five checks pass"| CAT PEER ==> PUB[["4 · Publish — name JSON files by content hash, commit to Git, and publish to GitHub Pages and npm"]] ``` **The shop runs locally as an npm package.** Its code lives in `packages/dsh-plugin-shop/`. The catalog build and the local shop share a data schema; their code is independent. ```mermaid flowchart LR CAT[["Plugin catalog
index.json + plugins.sha256.json"]] CAT ==> HOST["5 · Host
Request multiple sources concurrently
Verify sha256 and cache the result"] HOST ==> DEP{"6 · Check dependencies
Look for each peer dependency
in your profile or web client"} DEP -->|"Missing dependencies"| BAD["Incompatible
The card lists
missing dependencies"] DEP -->|"All dependencies found"| GOOD["Ready to install"] BAD --> CLIENT["Client — the plugin shop page
Calls nine shop/* methods on the host
No network or filesystem access"] GOOD --> CLIENT CLIENT ==>|"dsh plugin add"| PROF[("your dsh profile")] ``` Two details are useful to understand: - **Every rejected plugin is documented.** The build report records its name and explains which check it failed, so authors can investigate. - **Compatibility depends on your local environment.** The catalog records the *names* of the peer dependencies a plugin requires, without version ranges. Nearly all dsh plugins declare `"*"`, but the harness's prereleases do not satisfy ordinary version ranges. Checking those ranges would incorrectly mark working plugins as incompatible. Instead, the shop checks whether each dependency is available in your profile or provided by dsh's web client. ## ✅ Project principles | | | |---|---| | **Open to the community** | Publish to npm with the `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` keyword to make your plugin discoverable. No separate submission to this project is needed. | | **Traceable changes** | Catalog updates are committed to Git daily, so you can inspect each change and its history. | | **Explicit trust levels** | A human review applies only to the exact version reviewed. Other versions cannot inherit that status, preventing an author from using an earlier review to endorse a malicious release. **Currently, `registry/verified.yml` is empty: no catalog entries have been reviewed by a human, and all plugins are in the community tier.** Automated screening cannot replace a review of the plugin's code. | | **Restricted UI permissions** | The browser interface has no network or filesystem access. Compromising it does not grant runtime privileges. | ## 🚫 Permissions and limitations > **The shop does not provide sandbox isolation.** Once loaded, a dsh plugin has > access to the full `ctx`, including your filesystem, shell, and requests sent to > the model. Installing a plugin means trusting it with these permissions. The shop > does not restrict what a running plugin can do. The shop does not display download counts, ratings, or reviews, and it will not offer installation from arbitrary URLs. For that, use `dsh plugin add` and decide whether to allow build scripts or pin a specific commit. ## 📚 Plugin catalog The catalog is built daily and published as static JSON through the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package and GitHub Pages. The shop requests it from multiple sources: your configured npm registry, npmmirror, npmjs, and GitHub Pages. It uses the first valid response to avoid delays from a slow connection to any one source. Each source serves identical data, which is checked against the sha256 hash in the index before use. Set `DSH_SHOP_CATALOG_URL` to use only a specific source. | File | Purpose | |---|---| | [`/v1/index.json`](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) | The index: `schemaVersion`, `builtAt`, the `count` of listed plugins, the `rejected` total, and content hashes. The badges above read these totals live. The file is small enough for regular polling. | | `/v1/plugins..json` | Plugin data, named by its content hash and safe to cache indefinitely. | | `/v1/stars..json` | GitHub star counts for each plugin, keyed by package name, when the daily build can retrieve them. | | `/v1/icons..json` | Plugin icons, each stored once as a data URL under the sha256 of its bytes. A plugin's `icon` field in the plugin data is its key here. Only icons that passed the daily build's checks are included, and the file is absent when there are none. | Each workflow run includes a rejection report listing every rejected plugin and the reason it was excluded, with details to help authors troubleshoot. When catalog content changes, the data filenames change with their content hashes, and the old files are removed. However, `index.json` is cached for ten minutes, so it may temporarily reference files that no longer exist. If you fetch data directly from `/v1/` and a data URL returns 404, fetch `index.json` again. Alternatively, read the same data from the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package, which always bundles the index with its matching data files. ## 🏷️ Listing a plugin Add `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` to the keywords in your `package.json` and publish to npm. The daily build will discover your plugin and list it once it passes the checks. If you do not publish to npm, your plugin can be listed from its GitHub repository: add either keyword as a repository topic and include `name` and `dsh.bundle` in the root `package.json`. The catalog pins a specific commit from the default branch as the plugin's version. The optional `dsh.catalog` section lets you specify the category, summary, and capabilities. Without it, the catalog generates a listing from your npm `description`. ```json { "name": "dsh-hello-plugin", "keywords": ["dsh-plugin"], "dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" }, "catalog": { "category": "tool", "summary": { "en": "...", "zh": "..." }, "capabilities": ["fs", "shell"] } } } ``` See [docs/schema.md](docs/schema.md) for the full field reference. **Common reasons for exclusion:** - No `dsh.bundle`, so the package cannot be installed as a plugin. - No license or source repository, so the package cannot be reviewed. - Neither `dsh.catalog` nor an npm `description`, leaving no plugin information to display. ### 🌾 Which packages are discovered? Discovery matches `dsh-plugin` and `deepseek-harness` in npm `keywords` or GitHub repository topics, regardless of the package name. The `cordis-plugin` keyword identifies the underlying framework, but does not establish that a package can be installed as a DSH plugin. Built-in plugins distributed with dsh declare no npm keywords, so this discovery process does not find them. If your community plugin uses Cordis and integrates with DSH, add either keyword and declare `dsh.bundle` in the appropriate manifest: - **For npm packages:** use the `package.json` of the package you publish. - **For GitHub repositories:** use the root `package.json`, which must also declare a `name`. In a monorepo, you can instead declare the bundle in the subpackage that provides the plugin. A general-purpose Cordis library without `dsh.bundle` cannot be installed as a DSH plugin. ## 🗂️ Repository layout | Path | Contents | |---|---| | `registry/` | The catalog pipeline. Core logic (`gate`, `tier`, `emit`, `pipeline`) uses pure functions; surrounding modules (`npm-client`, `build`) handle network requests, file access, and other side effects. | | `registry/verified.yml` | Human review records tied to specific versions. | | `registry/denied.yml` | The denylist, with a reason for each entry. | | `registry/snapshots/` | Daily `manifest.lock` snapshots. | | `packages/dsh-plugin-shop/` | The shop's npm package, containing the host and client components. | | `docs/design/` | Design specifications that guide the implementation. | ## 🛠️ Development ```sh pnpm install pnpm test # vitest pnpm typecheck ``` `pnpm build:catalog` collects live data from npm and GitHub, making thousands of network requests and taking several minutes. All policy decisions are covered by offline tests. Run the full build when you change data fetching or file output and need to verify the complete workflow. Project status and remaining work: [docs/plans/2026-08-18-remaining-work.md](docs/plans/2026-08-18-remaining-work.md). Design specification: [docs/design/2026-08-18-dsh-plugin-shop-design.md](docs/design/2026-08-18-dsh-plugin-shop-design.md). ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome. Here are three ways to help, starting with a small correction: - **Correct a classification.** A classifier assigns categories and determines whether a plugin is another plugin marketplace. The [build report](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/report.md) lists every decision that has not been reviewed by a human. Correcting one takes a single line of YAML, with no network access, TypeScript changes, or local build required. - **Publish your plugin.** Add a discovery keyword and publish. If the plugin does not appear in the shop, check the same build report for an explanation. - **Improve the pipeline.** Follow the specifications in [`docs/design/`](docs/design/) and the development conventions in `CLAUDE.md`. See the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for detailed instructions, and follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) when taking part in discussions. Report vulnerabilities or malicious plugins privately through the [security reporting process](SECURITY.md), not in a public issue. ## 📄 License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE) © LivXue

# dsh-plugin-shop **The plugin shop for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)** — browse, install, enable, disable, and update dsh plugins, with every catalog change tracked in Git. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-shop?logo=npm&color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-shop) [![plugins](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2FLivXue.github.io%2Fdsh-plugin-shop%2Fv1%2Findex.json&query=count&label=plugins&color=blue)](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) [![filtered](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2FLivXue.github.io%2Fdsh-plugin-shop%2Fv1%2Findex.json&query=rejected&label=filtered&color=orange)](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-plugin-shop?color=blue)](LICENSE) [![plugin CI](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop/actions/workflows/plugin.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop/actions/workflows/plugin.yml) [![catalog](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2FLivXue.github.io%2Fdsh-plugin-shop%2Fv1%2Fbadge.json)](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop/actions/workflows/daily.yml) English | [中文](README.zh.md)
--- ## 📦 Install the shop Install the shop manually, or have an agent follow the automated steps below. ### 🧑 Manual installation **Prerequisite:** Node.js. You can run DeepSeek Harness without a global installation using the command in its official documentation: `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh web`. Plugin management uses `dsh plugin`, which invokes both `dsh` and `pnpm`. Install these tools with `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh pnpm`, then check that both are available with `dsh --version` and `pnpm --version`. ```sh # With dsh installed globally, run the following command. # Specify the version: pnpm 11 restricts newly published releases by default, # so omitting the version may install an older release. The current version # is shown below; check for updates with `npm view dsh-plugin-shop version`. dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-shop@0.9.0 # Alternatively, run the installation command through npx: npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-shop@0.9.0 ``` Replace `web` with your profile name if you use a different one. Restart `dsh` after installation to load the new plugin, then open: > **Plugin shop** in the left sidebar ### 🤖 Installation with an agent An agent can run these steps without interaction. **The `--profile` option is required.** If it is omitted, `dsh plugin` exits with this error: `error: required option '--profile ' not specified`. ```sh # 1. List available profiles ($DSH_HOME defaults to ~/.dsh; exclude node_modules). ls -1 "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles" | grep -v '^node_modules$' # 2. Specify the version to bypass pnpm's release cooldown and ensure # that the expected version is installed. dsh plugin --profile add dsh-plugin-shop@0.9.0 # 3. Verify the installation; exit code 0 above only means pnpm resolved the package. dsh plugin --profile list --depth 0 # The output should include dsh-plugin-shop. # 4. Restart the profile to load the new plugin. dsh --profile ``` You can also verify step 3 by checking that `dsh.profile.bundles` in `$DSH_HOME/profiles//package.json` includes the plugin. For troubleshooting, see the [package README](packages/dsh-plugin-shop/README.md#failure-modes). ## 🖼️ Screenshots
A plugin your dsh would refuse to install says why on its card The plugin shop in dark mode
## ✨ Highlights - **🌐 Automatic discovery** — the catalog collects npm packages with the `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` keyword and GitHub repositories with either topic. Authors do not need to submit an application or join a queue. - **🧹 Strict screening** — every candidate is checked automatically on each build. Rejected plugins are recorded by name with one of seventeen predefined reasons and a detailed explanation to help authors troubleshoot. The `plugins` and `filtered` badges above show the current totals. - **🔌 Local dependency checks** — the shop checks each peer dependency a plugin requires against your profile and the modules dsh's web client provides. When the author declares which dsh versions or profiles a plugin supports, the shop also compares them with what you run. A card shows **Incompatible** only when a dependency is missing from your environment or the author's declared support does not cover it. - **🗓️ Daily updates** — the catalog is rebuilt daily, with changes committed to Git for review. Eligible new plugins are listed the next morning, and plugins whose repositories are no longer available are removed during the same process. - **🗂️ Seven categories** — authors can choose a category through `dsh.catalog`. Otherwise, the build assigns one automatically. ## 🗺️ How it works **The catalog is built daily in this repository.** The build code lives in `registry/`. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph HARVEST["1 · Discover — collect plugins from public sources daily"] direction LR NPM(["npm packages
keyword dsh-plugin
keyword deepseek-harness"]) GH(["GitHub repositories
with the same keywords
as topics"]) end subgraph GATE["2 · Screen — check every candidate on each build"] direction LR G1["Is it a loadable plugin?

Has a valid
dsh.bundle"] G2["Can it be reviewed?

Has a license and
an accessible source repository"] G3["Can it be installed?

Not deprecated on npm;
repository listings also require
no build scripts or
workspace: dependencies"] G4["Is the package information credible?

Check integrity, publication time,
and potentially misleading names"] G5["Is there information to display?

Has a valid dsh.catalog
or an npm description"] end subgraph SHELVE["3 · List — record plugin details"] direction LR CAT["One of seven categories"] PEER["Required peer dependency names,
without version ranges"] end NPM --> G1 GH --> G1 G1 -.-> REJ G2 -.-> REJ G3 -.-> REJ G4 -.-> REJ G5 -.-> REJ REJ[["Rejected — record the plugin name and explain why"]] G5 ==>|"All five checks pass"| CAT PEER ==> PUB[["4 · Publish — name JSON files by content hash, commit to Git, and publish to GitHub Pages and npm"]] ``` **The shop runs locally as an npm package.** Its code lives in `packages/dsh-plugin-shop/`. The catalog build and the local shop share a data schema; their code is independent. ```mermaid flowchart LR CAT[["Plugin catalog
index.json + plugins.sha256.json"]] CAT ==> HOST["5 · Host
Request multiple sources concurrently
Verify sha256 and cache the result"] HOST ==> DEP{"6 · Check dependencies
Look for each peer dependency
in your profile or web client"} DEP -->|"Missing dependencies"| BAD["Incompatible
The card lists
missing dependencies"] DEP -->|"All dependencies found"| GOOD["Ready to install"] BAD --> CLIENT["Client — the plugin shop page
Calls nine shop/* methods on the host
No network or filesystem access"] GOOD --> CLIENT CLIENT ==>|"dsh plugin add"| PROF[("your dsh profile")] ``` Two details are useful to understand: - **Every rejected plugin is documented.** The build report records its name and explains which check it failed, so authors can investigate. - **Compatibility depends on your local environment.** The catalog records the *names* of the peer dependencies a plugin requires, without version ranges. Nearly all dsh plugins declare `"*"`, but the harness's prereleases do not satisfy ordinary version ranges. Checking those ranges would incorrectly mark working plugins as incompatible. Instead, the shop checks whether each dependency is available in your profile or provided by dsh's web client. ## ✅ Project principles | | | |---|---| | **Open to the community** | Publish to npm with the `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` keyword to make your plugin discoverable. No separate submission to this project is needed. | | **Traceable changes** | Catalog updates are committed to Git daily, so you can inspect each change and its history. | | **Explicit trust levels** | A human review applies only to the exact version reviewed. Other versions cannot inherit that status, preventing an author from using an earlier review to endorse a malicious release. **Currently, `registry/verified.yml` is empty: no catalog entries have been reviewed by a human, and all plugins are in the community tier.** Automated screening cannot replace a review of the plugin's code. | | **Restricted UI permissions** | The browser interface has no network or filesystem access. Compromising it does not grant runtime privileges. | ## 🚫 Permissions and limitations > **The shop does not provide sandbox isolation.** Once loaded, a dsh plugin has > access to the full `ctx`, including your filesystem, shell, and requests sent to > the model. Installing a plugin means trusting it with these permissions. The shop > does not restrict what a running plugin can do. The shop does not display download counts, ratings, or reviews, and it will not offer installation from arbitrary URLs. For that, use `dsh plugin add` and decide whether to allow build scripts or pin a specific commit. ## 📚 Plugin catalog The catalog is built daily and published as static JSON through the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package and GitHub Pages. The shop requests it from multiple sources: your configured npm registry, npmmirror, npmjs, and GitHub Pages. It uses the first valid response to avoid delays from a slow connection to any one source. Each source serves identical data, which is checked against the sha256 hash in the index before use. Set `DSH_SHOP_CATALOG_URL` to use only a specific source. | File | Purpose | |---|---| | [`/v1/index.json`](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) | The index: `schemaVersion`, `builtAt`, the `count` of listed plugins, the `rejected` total, and content hashes. The badges above read these totals live. The file is small enough for regular polling. | | `/v1/plugins..json` | Plugin data, named by its content hash and safe to cache indefinitely. | | `/v1/stars..json` | GitHub star counts for each plugin, keyed by package name, when the daily build can retrieve them. | | `/v1/icons..json` | Plugin icons, each stored once as a data URL under the sha256 of its bytes. A plugin's `icon` field in the plugin data is its key here. Only icons that passed the daily build's checks are included, and the file is absent when there are none. | Each workflow run includes a rejection report listing every rejected plugin and the reason it was excluded, with details to help authors troubleshoot. When catalog content changes, the data filenames change with their content hashes, and the old files are removed. However, `index.json` is cached for ten minutes, so it may temporarily reference files that no longer exist. If you fetch data directly from `/v1/` and a data URL returns 404, fetch `index.json` again. Alternatively, read the same data from the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package, which always bundles the index with its matching data files. ## 🏷️ Listing a plugin Add `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` to the keywords in your `package.json` and publish to npm. The daily build will discover your plugin and list it once it passes the checks. If you do not publish to npm, your plugin can be listed from its GitHub repository: add either keyword as a repository topic and include `name` and `dsh.bundle` in the root `package.json`. The catalog pins a specific commit from the default branch as the plugin's version. The optional `dsh.catalog` section lets you specify the category, summary, and capabilities. Without it, the catalog generates a listing from your npm `description`. ```json { "name": "dsh-hello-plugin", "keywords": ["dsh-plugin"], "dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" }, "catalog": { "category": "tool", "summary": { "en": "...", "zh": "..." }, "capabilities": ["fs", "shell"] } } } ``` See [docs/schema.md](docs/schema.md) for the full field reference. **Common reasons for exclusion:** - No `dsh.bundle`, so the package cannot be installed as a plugin. - No license or source repository, so the package cannot be reviewed. - Neither `dsh.catalog` nor an npm `description`, leaving no plugin information to display. ### 🌾 Which packages are discovered? Discovery matches `dsh-plugin` and `deepseek-harness` in npm `keywords` or GitHub repository topics, regardless of the package name. The `cordis-plugin` keyword identifies the underlying framework, but does not establish that a package can be installed as a DSH plugin. Built-in plugins distributed with dsh declare no npm keywords, so this discovery process does not find them. If your community plugin uses Cordis and integrates with DSH, add either keyword and declare `dsh.bundle` in the appropriate manifest: - **For npm packages:** use the `package.json` of the package you publish. - **For GitHub repositories:** use the root `package.json`, which must also declare a `name`. In a monorepo, you can instead declare the bundle in the subpackage that provides the plugin. A general-purpose Cordis library without `dsh.bundle` cannot be installed as a DSH plugin. ## 🗂️ Repository layout | Path | Contents | |---|---| | `registry/` | The catalog pipeline. Core logic (`gate`, `tier`, `emit`, `pipeline`) uses pure functions; surrounding modules (`npm-client`, `build`) handle network requests, file access, and other side effects. | | `registry/verified.yml` | Human review records tied to specific versions. | | `registry/denied.yml` | The denylist, with a reason for each entry. | | `registry/snapshots/` | Daily `manifest.lock` snapshots. | | `packages/dsh-plugin-shop/` | The shop's npm package, containing the host and client components. | | `docs/design/` | Design specifications that guide the implementation. | ## 🛠️ Development ```sh pnpm install pnpm test # vitest pnpm typecheck ``` `pnpm build:catalog` collects live data from npm and GitHub, making thousands of network requests and taking several minutes. All policy decisions are covered by offline tests. Run the full build when you change data fetching or file output and need to verify the complete workflow. Project status and remaining work: [docs/plans/2026-08-18-remaining-work.md](docs/plans/2026-08-18-remaining-work.md). Design specification: [docs/design/2026-08-18-dsh-plugin-shop-design.md](docs/design/2026-08-18-dsh-plugin-shop-design.md). ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome. Here are three ways to help, starting with a small correction: - **Correct a classification.** A classifier assigns categories and determines whether a plugin is another plugin marketplace. The [build report](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/report.md) lists every decision that has not been reviewed by a human. Correcting one takes a single line of YAML, with no network access, TypeScript changes, or local build required. - **Publish your plugin.** Add a discovery keyword and publish. If the plugin does not appear in the shop, check the same build report for an explanation. - **Improve the pipeline.** Follow the specifications in [`docs/design/`](docs/design/) and the development conventions in `CLAUDE.md`. See the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for detailed instructions, and follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) when taking part in discussions. Report vulnerabilities or malicious plugins privately through the [security reporting process](SECURITY.md), not in a public issue. ## 📄 License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE) © LivXue

Verify the installation; exit code 0 above only means pnpm resolved the package. dsh plugin --profile list --depth 0 # The output should include dsh-plugin-shop. # 4. Restart the profile to load the new plugin. dsh --profile ``` You can also verify step 3 by checking that `dsh.profile.bundles` in `$DSH_HOME/profiles//package.json` includes the plugin. ## ✨ Highlights - **🌐 Automatic discovery** — the catalog collects npm packages with the `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` keyword and GitHub repositories with either topic. Authors do not need to submit an application or join a queue. - **🧹 Strict screening** — every candidate is checked automatically on each build. Rejected plugins are recorded by name with one of seventeen predefined reasons and a detailed explanation to help authors troubleshoot. The `plugins` and `filtered` badges above show the current totals. - **🔌 Local dependency checks** — the shop checks each peer dependency a plugin requires against your profile and the modules dsh's web client provides. When the author declares which dsh versions or profiles a plugin supports, the shop also compares them with what you run. A card shows **Incompatible** only when a dependency is missing from your environment or the author's declared support does not cover it. - **🗓️ Daily updates** — the catalog is rebuilt daily, with changes committed to Git for review. Eligible new plugins are listed the next morning, and plugins whose repositories are no longer available are removed during the same process. - **🗂️ Seven categories** — authors can choose a category through `dsh.catalog`. Otherwise, the build assigns one automatically. ## 🗺️ How it works **The catalog is built daily in this repository.** The build code lives in `registry/`. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph HARVEST["1 · Discover — collect plugins from public sources daily"] direction LR NPM(["npm packages
keyword dsh-plugin
keyword deepseek-harness"]) GH(["GitHub repositories
with the same keywords
as topics"]) end subgraph GATE["2 · Screen — check every candidate on each build"] direction LR G1["Is it a loadable plugin?

Has a valid
dsh.bundle"] G2["Can it be reviewed?

Has a license and
an accessible source repository"] G3["Can it be installed?

Not deprecated on npm;
repository listings also require
no build scripts or

The catalog build and the local shop share a data schema; their code is independent. ```mermaid flowchart LR CAT[["Plugin catalog
index.json + plugins.sha256.json"]] CAT ==> HOST["5 · Host
Request multiple sources concurrently
Verify sha256 and cache the result"] HOST ==> DEP{"6 · Check dependencies
Look for each peer dependency

The card lists
missing dependencies"] DEP -->|"All dependencies found"| GOOD["Ready to install"] BAD --> CLIENT["Client — the plugin shop page
Calls nine shop/* methods on the host

Nearly all dsh plugins declare `"*"`, but the harness's prereleases do not satisfy ordinary version ranges. Checking those ranges would incorrectly mark working plugins as incompatible. Instead, the shop checks whether each dependency is available in your profile or provided by dsh's web client. ## ✅ Project principles | | | |---|---| | **Open to the community** | Publish to npm with the `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` keyword to make your plugin discoverable. No separate submission to this project is needed. | | **Traceable changes** | Catalog updates are committed to Git daily, so you can inspect each change and its history. | | **Explicit trust levels** | A human review applies only to the exact version reviewed. Compromising it does not grant runtime privileges. | ## 🚫 Permissions and limitations > **The shop does not provide sandbox isolation.** Once loaded, a dsh plugin has > access to the full `ctx`, including your filesystem, shell, and requests sent to > the model. Installing a plugin means trusting it with these permissions. The shop > does not restrict what a running plugin can do. The shop does not display download counts, ratings, or reviews, and it will not offer installation from arbitrary URLs. For that, use `dsh plugin add` and decide whether to allow build scripts or pin a specific commit. ## 📚 Plugin catalog The catalog is built daily and published as static JSON through the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package and GitHub Pages. The shop requests it from multiple sources: your configured npm registry, npmmirror, npmjs, and GitHub Pages. It uses the first valid response to avoid delays from a slow connection to any one source. Each source serves identical data, which is checked against the sha256 hash in the index before use. Set `DSH_SHOP_CATALOG_URL` to use only a specific source. | File | Purpose | |---|---| | [`/v1/index.json`](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) | The index: `schemaVersion`, `builtAt`, the `count` of listed plugins, the `rejected` total, and content hashes. The badges above read these totals live. The file is small enough for regular polling. | | `/v1/plugins..json` | Plugin data, named by its content hash and safe to cache indefinitely. | | `/v1/stars..json` | GitHub star counts for each plugin, keyed by package name, when the daily build can retrieve them. | | `/v1/icons..json` | Plugin icons, each stored once as a data URL under the sha256 of its bytes. A plugin's `icon` field in the plugin data is its key here. Only icons that passed the daily build's checks are included, and the file is absent when there are none. | Each workflow run includes a rejection report listing every rejected plugin and the reason it was excluded, with details to help authors troubleshoot. When catalog content changes, the data filenames change with their content hashes, and the old files are removed. However, `index.json` is cached for ten minutes, so it may temporarily reference files that no longer exist. If you fetch data directly from `/v1/` and a data URL returns 404, fetch `index.json` again. Alternatively, read the same data from the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package, which always bundles the index with its matching data files. ## 🏷️ Listing a plugin Add `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` to the keywords in your `package.json` and publish to npm. The daily build will discover your plugin and list it once it passes the checks. If you do not publish to npm, your plugin can be listed from its GitHub repository: add either keyword as a repository topic and include `name` and `dsh.bundle` in the root `package.json`. The catalog pins a specific commit from the default branch as the plugin's version. The optional `dsh.catalog` section lets you specify the category, summary, and capabilities. Without it, the catalog generates a listing from your npm `description`. ```json { "name": "dsh-hello-plugin", "keywords": ["dsh-plugin"], "dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" }, "catalog": { "category": "tool", "summary": { "en": "...", "zh": "..." }, "capabilities": ["fs", "shell"] } } } ``` See [docs/schema.md](docs/schema.md) for the full field reference. **Common reasons for exclusion:** - No `dsh.bundle`, so the package cannot be installed as a plugin. - No license or source repository, so the package cannot be reviewed. - Neither `dsh.catalog` nor an npm `description`, leaving no plugin information to display. ### 🌾 Which packages are discovered? Discovery matches `dsh-plugin` and `deepseek-harness` in npm `keywords` or GitHub repository topics, regardless of the package name. The `cordis-plugin` keyword identifies the underlying framework, but does not establish that a package can be installed as a DSH plugin. Built-in plugins distributed with dsh declare no npm keywords, so this discovery process does not find them. If your community plugin uses Cordis and integrates with DSH, add either keyword and declare `dsh.bundle` in the appropriate manifest: - **For npm packages:** use the `package.json` of the package you publish. - **For GitHub repositories:** use the root `package.json`, which must also declare a `name`. In a monorepo, you can instead declare the bundle in the subpackage that provides the plugin. A general-purpose Cordis library without `dsh.bundle` cannot be installed as a DSH plugin. ## 🗂️ Repository layout | Path | Contents | |---|---| | `registry/` | The catalog pipeline. Core logic (`gate`, `tier`, `emit`, `pipeline`) uses pure functions; surrounding modules (`npm-client`, `build`) handle network requests, file access, and other side effects. | | `registry/verified.yml` | Human review records tied to specific versions. | | `registry/denied.yml` | The denylist, with a reason for each entry. | | `registry/snapshots/` | Daily `manifest.lock` snapshots. | | `packages/dsh-plugin-shop/` | The shop's npm package, containing the host and client components. | | `docs/design/` | Design specifications that guide the implementation. | ## 🛠️ Development ```sh pnpm install pnpm test # vitest pnpm typecheck ``` `pnpm build:catalog` collects live data from npm and GitHub, making thousands of network requests and taking several minutes. All policy decisions are covered by offline tests. Run the full build when you change data fetching or file output and need to verify the complete workflow. Project status and remaining work: [docs/plans/2026-08-18-remaining-work.md](docs/plans/2026-08-18-remaining-work.md). Design specification: [docs/design/2026-08-18-dsh-plugin-shop-design.md](docs/design/2026-08-18-dsh-plugin-shop-design.md). ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome. Here are three ways to help, starting with a small correction: - **Correct a classification.** A classifier assigns categories and determines whether a plugin is another plugin marketplace. The [build report](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/report.md) lists every decision that has not been reviewed by a human. Correcting one takes a single line of YAML, with no network access, TypeScript changes, or local build required. - **Publish your plugin.** Add a discovery keyword and publish. If the plugin does not appear in the shop, check the same build report for an explanation. - **Improve the pipeline.** Follow the specifications in [`docs/design/`](docs/design/) and the development conventions in `CLAUDE.md`. See the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for detailed instructions, and follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) when taking part in discussions. Report vulnerabilities or malicious plugins privately through the [security reporting process](SECURITY.md), not in a public issue. ## 📄 License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE) © LivXue

Instead, the shop checks whether each dependency is available in your profile or provided by dsh's web client. ## ✅ Project principles | | | |---|---| | **Open to the community** | Publish to npm with the `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` keyword to make your plugin discoverable. No separate submission to this project is needed. | | **Traceable changes** | Catalog updates are committed to Git daily, so you can inspect each change and its history. | | **Explicit trust levels** | A human review applies only to the exact version reviewed. Other versions cannot inherit that status, preventing an author from using an earlier review to endorse a malicious release. **Currently, `registry/verified.yml` is empty: no catalog entries have been reviewed by a human, and all plugins are in the community tier.** Automated screening cannot replace a review of the plugin's code. | | **Restricted UI permissions** | The browser interface has no network or filesystem access. Compromising it does not grant runtime privileges. | ## 🚫 Permissions and limitations > **The shop does not provide sandbox isolation.** Once loaded, a dsh plugin has > access to the full `ctx`, including your filesystem, shell, and requests sent to > the model. Installing a plugin means trusting it with these permissions. The shop > does not restrict what a running plugin can do. The shop does not display download counts, ratings, or reviews, and it will not offer installation from arbitrary URLs. For that, use `dsh plugin add` and decide whether to allow build scripts or pin a specific commit. ## 📚 Plugin catalog The catalog is built daily and published as static JSON through the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package and GitHub Pages. The shop requests it from multiple sources: your configured npm registry, npmmirror, npmjs, and GitHub Pages. It uses the first valid response to avoid delays from a slow connection to any one source. Each source serves identical data, which is checked against the sha256 hash in the index before use. The badges above read these totals live. The file is small enough for regular polling. | | `/v1/plugins..json` | Plugin data, named by its content hash and safe to cache indefinitely. | | `/v1/stars..json` | GitHub star counts for each plugin, keyed by package name, when the daily build can retrieve them. | | `/v1/icons..json` | Plugin icons, each stored once as a data URL under the sha256 of its bytes. A plugin's `icon` field in the plugin data is its key here. Only icons that passed the daily build's checks are included, and the file is absent when there are none. | Each workflow run includes a rejection report listing every rejected plugin and the reason it was excluded, with details to help authors troubleshoot. When catalog content changes, the data filenames change with their content hashes, and the old files are removed. However, `index.json` is cached for ten minutes, so it may temporarily reference files that no longer exist. If you fetch data directly from `/v1/` and a data URL returns 404, fetch `index.json` again. Alternatively, read the same data from the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package, which always bundles the index with its matching data files. ## 🏷️ Listing a plugin Add `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` to the keywords in your `package.json` and publish to npm. The daily build will discover your plugin and list it once it passes the checks. If you do not publish to npm, your plugin can be listed from its GitHub repository: add either keyword as a repository topic and include `name` and `dsh.bundle` in the root `package.json`. The catalog pins a specific commit from the default branch as the plugin's version. The optional `dsh.catalog` section lets you specify the category, summary, and capabilities. Without it, the catalog generates a listing from your npm `description`. ```json { "name": "dsh-hello-plugin", "keywords": ["dsh-plugin"], "dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./cordis.patch.yml" }, "catalog": { "category": "tool", "summary": { "en": "...", "zh": "..." }, "capabilities": ["fs", "shell"] } } } ``` See [docs/schema.md](docs/schema.md) for the full field reference. **Common reasons for exclusion:** - No `dsh.bundle`, so the package cannot be installed as a plugin. - No license or source repository, so the package cannot be reviewed. - Neither `dsh.catalog` nor an npm `description`, leaving no plugin information to display. ### 🌾 Which packages are discovered? Discovery matches `dsh-plugin` and `deepseek-harness` in npm `keywords` or GitHub repository topics, regardless of the package name. The `cordis-plugin` keyword identifies the underlying framework, but does not establish that a package can be installed as a DSH plugin. Built-in plugins distributed with dsh declare no npm keywords, so this discovery process does not find them. If your community plugin uses Cordis and integrates with DSH, add either keyword and declare `dsh.bundle` in the appropriate manifest: - **For npm packages:** use the `package.json` of the package you publish. - **For GitHub repositories:** use the root `package.json`, which must also declare a `name`. In a monorepo, you can instead declare the bundle in the subpackage that provides the plugin. A general-purpose Cordis library without `dsh.bundle` cannot be installed as a DSH plugin. ## 🗂️ Repository layout | Path | Contents | |---|---| | `registry/` | The catalog pipeline. Core logic (`gate`, `tier`, `emit`, `pipeline`) uses pure functions; surrounding modules (`npm-client`, `build`) handle network requests, file access, and other side effects. | | `registry/verified.yml` | Human review records tied to specific versions. | | `registry/denied.yml` | The denylist, with a reason for each entry. | | `registry/snapshots/` | Daily `manifest.lock` snapshots. | | `packages/dsh-plugin-shop/` | The shop's npm package, containing the host and client components. | | `docs/design/` | Design specifications that guide the implementation. | ## 🛠️ Development ```sh pnpm install pnpm test # vitest pnpm typecheck ``` `pnpm build:catalog` collects live data from npm and GitHub, making thousands of network requests and taking several minutes. All policy decisions are covered by offline tests. Run the full build when you change data fetching or file output and need to verify the complete workflow. Project status and remaining work: [docs/plans/2026-08-18-remaining-work.md](docs/plans/2026-08-18-remaining-work.md). Design specification: [docs/design/2026-08-18-dsh-plugin-shop-design.md](docs/design/2026-08-18-dsh-plugin-shop-design.md). ## 🤝 Contributing Contributions are welcome. Here are three ways to help, starting with a small correction: - **Correct a classification.** A classifier assigns categories and determines whether a plugin is another plugin marketplace. The [build report](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/report.md) lists every decision that has not been reviewed by a human. Correcting one takes a single line of YAML, with no network access, TypeScript changes, or local build required. - **Publish your plugin.** Add a discovery keyword and publish. If the plugin does not appear in the shop, check the same build report for an explanation. - **Improve the pipeline.** Follow the specifications in [`docs/design/`](docs/design/) and the development conventions in `CLAUDE.md`. See the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for detailed instructions, and follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) when taking part in discussions. Report vulnerabilities or malicious plugins privately through the [security reporting process](SECURITY.md), not in a public issue. ## 📄 License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE) © LivXue

All policy decisions are covered by offline tests. Run the full build when you change data fetching or file output and need to verify the complete workflow. Here are three ways to help, starting with a small correction: - **Correct a classification.** A classifier assigns categories and determines whether a plugin is another plugin marketplace. The [build report](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/report.md) lists every decision that has not been reviewed by a human. Correcting one takes a single line of YAML, with no network access, TypeScript changes, or local build required. - **Publish your plugin.** Add a discovery keyword and publish. If the plugin does not appear in the shop, check the same build report for an explanation. - **Improve the pipeline.** Follow the specifications in [`docs/design/`](docs/design/) and the development conventions in `CLAUDE.md`. See the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) for detailed instructions, and follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) when taking part in discussions. # dsh-plugin-shop **The plugin shop for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)** — browse, install, enable, disable, and update dsh plugins, with every catalog change tracked in Git. [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-plugin-shop?logo=npm&color=cb3837)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-plugin-shop) [![plugins](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2FLivXue.github.io%2Fdsh-plugin-shop%2Fv1%2Findex.json&query=count&label=plugins&color=blue)](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) [![filtered](https://img.shields.io/badge/dynamic/json?url=https%3A%2F%2FLivXue.github.io%2Fdsh-plugin-shop%2Fv1%2Findex.json&query=rejected&label=filtered&color=orange)](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) [![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-plugin-shop?color=blue)](LICENSE) [![plugin CI](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop/actions/workflows/plugin.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop/actions/workflows/plugin.yml) [![catalog](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2FLivXue.github.io%2Fdsh-plugin-shop%2Fv1%2Fbadge.json)](https://github.com/LivXue/dsh-plugin-shop/actions/workflows/daily.yml) English | [中文](README.zh.md)
--- ## 📦 Install the shop Install the shop manually, or have an agent follow the automated steps below. ### 🧑 Manual installation **Prerequisite:** Node.js. You can run DeepSeek Harness without a global installation using the command in its official documentation: `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh web`. Plugin management uses `dsh plugin`, which invokes both `dsh` and `pnpm`. Install these tools with `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh pnpm`, then check that both are available with `dsh --version` and `pnpm --version`. ```sh # With dsh installed globally, run the following command. # Specify the version: pnpm 11 restricts newly published releases by default, # so omitting the version may install an older release. The current version # is shown below; check for updates with `npm view dsh-plugin-shop version`. dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-shop@0.9.0 # Alternatively, run the installation command through npx: npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-shop@0.9.0 ``` Replace `web` with your profile name if you use a different one. Restart `dsh` after installation to load the new plugin, then open: > **Plugin shop** in the left sidebar ### 🤖 Installation with an agent An agent can run these steps without interaction. **The `--profile` option is required.** If it is omitted, `dsh plugin` exits with this error: `error: required option '--profile ' not specified`. ```sh # 1. List available profiles ($DSH_HOME defaults to ~/.dsh; exclude node_modules). ls -1 "${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/profiles" | grep -v '^node_modules$' # 2. Specify the version to bypass pnpm's release cooldown and ensure # that the expected version is installed. dsh plugin --profile add dsh-plugin-shop@0.9.0 # 3. Verify the installation; exit code 0 above only means pnpm resolved the package. dsh plugin --profile list --depth 0 # The output should include dsh-plugin-shop. # 4. Restart the profile to load the new plugin. dsh --profile ``` You can also verify step 3 by checking that `dsh.profile.bundles` in `$DSH_HOME/profiles//package.json` includes the plugin. For troubleshooting, see the [package README](packages/dsh-plugin-shop/README.md#failure-modes). ## 🖼️ Screenshots
A plugin your dsh would refuse to install says why on its card The plugin shop in dark mode
## ✨ Highlights - **🌐 Automatic discovery** — the catalog collects npm packages with the `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` keyword and GitHub repositories with either topic. Authors do not need to submit an application or join a queue. - **🧹 Strict screening** — every candidate is checked automatically on each build. Rejected plugins are recorded by name with one of seventeen predefined reasons and a detailed explanation to help authors troubleshoot. The `plugins` and `filtered` badges above show the current totals. - **🔌 Local dependency checks** — the shop checks each peer dependency a plugin requires against your profile and the modules dsh's web client provides. When the author declares which dsh versions or profiles a plugin supports, the shop also compares them with what you run. A card shows **Incompatible** only when a dependency is missing from your environment or the author's declared support does not cover it. - **🗓️ Daily updates** — the catalog is rebuilt daily, with changes committed to Git for review. Eligible new plugins are listed the next morning, and plugins whose repositories are no longer available are removed during the same process. - **🗂️ Seven categories** — authors can choose a category through `dsh.catalog`. Otherwise, the build assigns one automatically. ## 🗺️ How it works **The catalog is built daily in this repository.** The build code lives in `registry/`. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph HARVEST["1 · Discover — collect plugins from public sources daily"] direction LR NPM(["npm packages
keyword dsh-plugin
keyword deepseek-harness"]) GH(["GitHub repositories
with the same keywords
as topics"]) end subgraph GATE["2 · Screen — check every candidate on each build"] direction LR G1["Is it a loadable plugin?

Has a valid
dsh.bundle"] G2["Can it be reviewed?

Has a license and
an accessible source repository"] G3["Can it be installed?

Not deprecated on npm;
repository listings also require
no build scripts or
workspace: dependencies"] G4["Is the package information credible?

Check integrity, publication time,
and potentially misleading names"] G5["Is there information to display?

Has a valid dsh.catalog
or an npm description"] end subgraph SHELVE["3 · List — record plugin details"] direction LR CAT["One of seven categories"] PEER["Required peer dependency names,
without version ranges"] end NPM --> G1 GH --> G1 G1 -.-> REJ G2 -.-> REJ G3 -.-> REJ G4 -.-> REJ G5 -.-> REJ REJ[["Rejected — record the plugin name and explain why"]] G5 ==>|"All five checks pass"| CAT PEER ==> PUB[["4 · Publish — name JSON files by content hash, commit to Git, and publish to GitHub Pages and npm"]] ``` **The shop runs locally as an npm package.** Its code lives in `packages/dsh-plugin-shop/`. The catalog build and the local shop share a data schema; their code is independent. ```mermaid flowchart LR CAT[["Plugin catalog
index.json + plugins.sha256.json"]] CAT ==> HOST["5 · Host
Request multiple sources concurrently
Verify sha256 and cache the result"] HOST ==> DEP{"6 · Check dependencies
Look for each peer dependency
in your profile or web client"} DEP -->|"Missing dependencies"| BAD["Incompatible
The card lists
missing dependencies"] DEP -->|"All dependencies found"| GOOD["Ready to install"] BAD --> CLIENT["Client — the plugin shop page
Calls nine shop/* methods on the host
No network or filesystem access"] GOOD --> CLIENT CLIENT ==>|"dsh plugin add"| PROF[("your dsh profile")] ``` Two details are useful to understand: - **Every rejected plugin is documented.** The build report records its name and explains which check it failed, so authors can investigate. - **Compatibility depends on your local environment.** The catalog records the *names* of the peer dependencies a plugin requires, without version ranges. Nearly all dsh plugins declare `"*"`, but the harness's prereleases do not satisfy ordinary version ranges. Checking those ranges would incorrectly mark working plugins as incompatible. Instead, the shop checks whether each dependency is available in your profile or provided by dsh's web client. ## ✅ Project principles | | | |---|---| | **Open to the community** | Publish to npm with the `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` keyword to make your plugin discoverable. No separate submission to this project is needed. | | **Traceable changes** | Catalog updates are committed to Git daily, so you can inspect each change and its history. | | **Explicit trust levels** | A human review applies only to the exact version reviewed. Other versions cannot inherit that status, preventing an author from using an earlier review to endorse a malicious release. **Currently, `registry/verified.yml` is empty: no catalog entries have been reviewed by a human, and all plugins are in the community tier.** Automated screening cannot replace a review of the plugin's code. | | **Restricted UI permissions** | The browser interface has no network or filesystem access. Compromising it does not grant runtime privileges. | ## 🚫 Permissions and limitations > **The shop does not provide sandbox isolation.** Once loaded, a dsh plugin has > access to the full `ctx`, including your filesystem, shell, and requests sent to > the model. Installing a plugin means trusting it with these permissions. The shop > does not restrict what a running plugin can do. The shop does not display download counts, ratings, or reviews, and it will not offer installation from arbitrary URLs. For that, use `dsh plugin add` and decide whether to allow build scripts or pin a specific commit. ## 📚 Plugin catalog The catalog is built daily and published as static JSON through the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package and GitHub Pages. The shop requests it from multiple sources: your configured npm registry, npmmirror, npmjs, and GitHub Pages. It uses the first valid response to avoid delays from a slow connection to any one source. Each source serves identical data, which is checked against the sha256 hash in the index before use. Set `DSH_SHOP_CATALOG_URL` to use only a specific source. | File | Purpose | |---|---| | [`/v1/index.json`](https://LivXue.github.io/dsh-plugin-shop/v1/index.json) | The index: `schemaVersion`, `builtAt`, the `count` of listed plugins, the `rejected` total, and content hashes. The badges above read these totals live. The file is small enough for regular polling. | | `/v1/plugins..json` | Plugin data, named by its content hash and safe to cache indefinitely. | | `/v1/stars..json` | GitHub star counts for each plugin, keyed by package name, when the daily build can retrieve them. | | `/v1/icons..json` | Plugin icons, each stored once as a data URL under the sha256 of its bytes. A plugin's `icon` field in the plugin data is its key here. Only icons that passed the daily build's checks are included, and the file is absent when there are none. | Each workflow run includes a rejection report listing every rejected plugin and the reason it was excluded, with details to help authors troubleshoot. When catalog content changes, the data filenames change with their content hashes, and the old files are removed. However, `index.json` is cached for ten minutes, so it may temporarily reference files that no longer exist. If you fetch data directly from `/v1/` and a data URL returns 404, fetch `index.json` again. Alternatively, read the same data from the `dsh-plugin-shop-catalog` npm package, which always bundles the index with its matching data files. ## 🏷️ Listing a plugin Add `dsh-plugin` or `deepseek-harness` to the keywords in your `package.json` and publish to npm. The daily build will discover your plugin and list it once it passes the checks. If you do not publish to npm, your plugin can be listed from its GitHub repository: add either keyword as a repository topic and include `name` and `dsh.bundle` in the root `package.json`. The catalog pins a specific commit from the default branch as the plugin's version. The optional `dsh.catalog` section lets you specify the category, summary, and capabilities.
