evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Academic Harness

[![verify](https://github.com/raktim-mondol/academic-harness/actions/workflows/verify.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/raktim-mondol/academic-harness/actions/workflows/verify.yml)
![DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1–0.2.x](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-0.2.1--0.2.x-5b7bd5)
![Tested on Linux](https://img.shields.io/badge/tested%20on-Linux-2f855a)

**A research workbench for DeepSeek Harness** — literature and web discovery, verbatim paper memory, a writing oracle for LaTeX, systematic-review, meta-analysis, and reproducible-analysis ledgers, 762 scientific skills, and local self-improvement, all inside the DSH web UI.

Academic Harness is a **DSH profile**: it installs as a plugin, adds a preset with a research persona and academic tools, and keeps the general-purpose tools available on every preset.

![Architecture overview](docs/assets/diagrams/architecture.svg)

## Why Academic Harness

| Principle | What it means in practice |
|---|---|
| **Evidence, not citation-shaped guesses** | PaperMemory stores papers as content-addressed Markdown and anchors claims to exact quote spans. `quote_check` and `trace` verify a quotation before it becomes a citation; an empty `cite` means *do not invent one*. [Read more](docs/PAPERS.md#paper-memory) |
| **A writing oracle with a gate** | The vendored `ah_*` engine inventories every number, citation, unit, and claim in a LaTeX tree. A turn closes only when it introduced no open blocker or major. [Read more](docs/WRITING.md#academic-harness-engine) |
| **Auditable research ledgers** | Systematic reviews and hypothesis tournaments live in append-only logs under the workspace, so a resumed session sees the same protocol, screening decisions, and ratings. [Reviews](docs/RESEARCH.md#systematic-reviews) · [Tournaments](docs/RESEARCH.md#hypothesis-tournaments) |
| **Discovery across the real literature** | OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, PubMed/Europe PMC, arXiv, Crossref, DOAJ, publisher Crossref deposits, bioRxiv/medRxiv, INSPIRE, and keyed ADS/Scopus/Web of Science through one `literature_search` entry point, plus `journal_search`, `paper_get`, `paper_context`, `paper_resolve`, `openalex_citations`, `database_catalog`, `domain_search`, Consensus, Parallel, Firecrawl, Scite, CORE, Elicit, and FutureHouse. [Read more](docs/SEARCH.md) |
| **A lab notebook that survives context loss** | A JSONL notebook shared across the delegation tree, a schema-validated `scientific_result` card, and deletion-only reply folding at five levels. [Read more](docs/WORKSPACE.md) |
| **One question, one bounded investigation** | `deep_research` reads the request, sweeps the literature and a web lane, finds where the sources disagree, drafts, lets four critics attack the draft, and refuses to ship a report that cites a source it cannot support. Five syndicated copies of one release count as one voice. `effort=low|medium|high` is the only knob; a request that contradicts itself gets a question instead of a bill. [Deep research](#deep-research) |
| **Local-first by design** | Workspace search (zvec-grep), PaperMemory, TextFold, ledgers, and the RSI store stay on disk. No key is required to boot. [Read more](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#runtime-installs) |

## Install

Requires **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1–0.2.x** (`>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0`, the range in `package.json`) and **Linux** (the only platform tested so far; see [Requirements](#requirements-and-scope)).

```sh
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh
```

Then either:

**A — from the DSH Web UI (recommended):** open **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste `github:raktim-mondol/academic-harness`, click **Install**, and start a new chat.

**B — a dedicated CLI profile:**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile academic-harness add github:raktim-mondol/academic-harness
dsh --profile academic-harness
```

Confirm the preset selector at the top of the message box reads **Academic Harness**. The academic tools are preset-only; a session left on Standard/PTC will fail with `tools[name] is not a function`.

Full instructions, migration from `researchcraft`, troubleshooting, and the "one DSH surface at a time" rule are in **[Install and run](docs/INSTALL.md)**.

## What is inside

![Capability map](docs/assets/diagrams/capability-map.svg)

| Surface | Highlights | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| **Search and discovery** | `literature_search` router, `journal_search` (OpenAlex/DOAJ/Crossref metrics plus optional CiteScore/JIF), `paper_get` (merged metadata + BibTeX), `paper_context` (focused sections/snippets), `database_catalog`, `domain_search` (bioRxiv/medRxiv, INSPIRE, ACL, ADS, Scopus, Web of Science, Wikidata), OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, PubMed, arXiv, Crossref, DOAJ, publisher Crossref deposits, Consensus, Parallel, Firecrawl, Scite, Tavily, Exa, Perplexity, Jina, CORE, Elicit, FutureHouse | [Search](docs/SEARCH.md) |
| **Papers and evidence** | `paper_get`, `paper_download`, `paper_context`, `paper_fold`, `pdf_to_markdown`, `deep_review` (multi-pass manuscript critique with anchored comments and reference verification, powered by [open-deepreview](https://github.com/raktim-mondol/open-deepreview)), PaperMemory's 14 tools, `reference_library` (the native reference manager: BibTeX, BibLaTeX, RIS, and CSL-JSON in and out; imports Scopus and Web of Science RIS exports), `integrity_check`, Paper2Agent | [Papers](docs/PAPERS.md) |
| **Writing and citation** | `ah_*` writing oracle and gate, `citation` (including DOI/arXiv/INSPIRE/title → BibTeX), `manuscript_citations`, `reporting_check` (CONSORT/STROBE/PRISMA/ARRIVE/TRIPOD+AI/CARE/STARD), LaTeX, Supervisor-Skills paper lifecycle, `scientific-figure-making`, `diagram-design`, `image_generate`, `mermaid_render` (Pele) | [Writing](docs/WRITING.md) |
| **Submission and communication** | `submission_pack` journal checklist and hashed bundle (never submits); `journal_search match` advisory venue fit with due-diligence signals; `manuscript_diff` latexdiff/Markdown/DOCX revision artifacts and response-letter skeleton; `numbers_audit` numerical-reporting candidates; `presentation_build` posters and slides with a vision-QA checklist; `authorship` CRediT/ICMJE ledger | [Writing](docs/WRITING.md#submission-and-communication) |
| **Reviews, synthesis, and hypotheses** | `review` PRISMA-style ledger with dual-reviewer screening, structured extraction, risk-of-bias appraisal (RoB 2, ROBINS-I, QUADAS-2, Newcastle-Ottawa, AMSTAR 2, PROBAST, QUIPS, SYRCLE, CASP checklists), GRADE certainty and summary-of-findings tables, κ agreement, PRISMA flow and RoB exports; `meta_analysis` pairwise pooling, heterogeneity, subgroup/meta-regression, publication-bias diagnostics, and forest/funnel/SROC plots; `coscientist` Glicko-2 tournament, published-results feedback, cross-session priors | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md) |
| **Deep research** | `deep_research`: a self-driving investigation on an append-only run ledger — frozen query, effort levels (`low`/`medium`/`high`) inferred from the request, scholarly sweep plus a web lane, contradiction graph, loci and depth notes, three drafts, four adversarial critics, capped-hunk repair, cite check against PaperMemory, independence clustering, untrusted-source fencing, and a ship gate that reports `not_checked` honestly | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md#deep-research) |
| **Reproducible analysis and data** | `analysis_run` frozen plans with immutable run manifests (argv execution, hashed inputs/outputs, redacted logs, timeouts, run diffs); `experiment_log` sweeps with best-by-named-metric; `dataset_get` DOI downloads with checksums and licenses; `data_profile` leakage and split-overview profiling; `repro_package` reader-facing reproducibility packages with confirm-gated Zenodo drafts | [Reproducible analysis](docs/ANALYSIS.md) |
| **Provenance audit** | `provenance_audit` read-only cross-ledger index: joins review, reporting, deep-review, notebook, analysis, experiment, dataset, meta-analysis, and AH claim sidecars by stored ids and hashes; coverage, unsupported (`no_link`/`not_checked`/`unverified`/`stale`/`not_found`), stale hashes, impact, and Markdown/CSV/JSON/GraphML/Mermaid exports | [Provenance audit](docs/PROVENANCE.md) |
| **Study planning** | `power_analysis`: sample size, power, effect sizes, multiplicity correction, simulation | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md#study-planning) |
| **Study conduct, ethics, and grants** | `preregister` hashed write-once plans; `causal_dag` identification diagnostics and E-values; `design` seeded randomization/DOE; `ethics_protocol` and `deidentify` for ethics and PHI/PII review; `dmp` funder-shaped data-management plans; `grant_budget` multi-year budgets with arithmetic checks. None submits or certifies compliance | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md#pre-registration) |
| **Clinical and policy records** | `clinicaltrials`, `openfda`, `dataset_search`, `journal_policy`, `funder_policy` | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md) |
| **Workspace and notebook** | zvec-grep semantic search, lab notebook, `scientific_result`, `fold_text`, `research_template`, `sci_inspect` | [Workspace](docs/WORKSPACE.md) |
| **Compute and delegation** | `runpod_run`/`modal_run`/`vastai_run`, `subagent` with optional `subagent_pro`/`subagent_vision` routes, specialist briefs, `agent-browser` | [Compute](docs/COMPUTE.md) · [Agents](docs/AGENTS.md) |
| **Skills** | 762 bundled skills: 140 domain, 16 methodology, 503 expert profiles, 23 drug-discovery, 12 Supervisor-Skills research-lifecycle skills, plus writing, figures, agents, and compute | [Skills](docs/SKILLS.md) |
| **Self-improvement** | Local RSI: capture, diagnose, admit, inject, compare against control, promote or quarantine | [RSI](docs/RSI.md) |
| **Configuration** | Settings → Academic Harness API keys; every credential is optional at install | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) |

### Search tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `literature_search` | One-shot multi-source router with RRF fusion and cross-provider dedupe |
| `journal_search` | Venue discovery and metrics across OpenAlex, DOAJ, and Crossref; optional CiteScore/SJR/SNIP and JCR JIF/JCI |
| `paper_get` | Merge one paper across OpenAlex, S2, Crossref, Europe PMC, and arXiv; OA URL and canonical BibTeX |
| `paper_context` | Focus-ranked sections/snippets from S2, arXiv HTML, PMC BioC/PubTator3, optional publisher TDM, and OA PDF |
| `paper_resolve` | Convert DOI/PMID/PMCID/arXiv/OpenAlex/S2 and source-specific INSPIRE/ACL/bibcode/Scopus/WoS/Wikidata identifiers |
| `openalex_search` | OpenAlex works, authors, sources, and topics with filters, facets, and source metrics |
| `openalex_citations` | Forward, backward, or both citation trails with an OpenCitations fallback |
| `s2_search` | Semantic Scholar relevance, bulk, and paper-scoped snippet search |
| `pubmed_search` | Europe PMC by default; NCBI E-utilities on request; preprint filter |
| `arxiv_search` | Fielded arXiv queries, serialized to one request every 3 seconds |
| `crossref_lookup` | Canonical DOI metadata; polite pool via `CROSSREF_MAILTO` |
| `domain_search` | Source-specific bioRxiv/ACL/INSPIRE/ADS/Scopus/WoS/Wikidata actions |
| `database_catalog` | Source/key/capability catalog; reports key fields only as configured/not set |

Free sources need no key. ADS, Scopus, Web of Science, Springer, IEEE, and publisher TDM tiers use their own keys and are implemented but intentionally not live-tested here. Web and AI-native discovery remains available through `consensus_search`, `parallel_search`/`parallel_extract`, `brave_search`, `tavily_search`, `exa_search`, `perplexity_search`, `jina_read`, `core_search`, `elicit_search`, and `futurehouse_agent`, plus the Parallel, Firecrawl, and Scite MCP connectors. See [Search](docs/SEARCH.md) for routing and [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) for the key fields.

The complete tool list, with scope and links, is the **[tool index](docs/TOOLS.md)**. The [architecture guide](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) explains which tools are available on every preset and which are preset-only.

## How a request works

![Request lifecycle](docs/assets/diagrams/request-lifecycle.svg)

Discovery finds candidate papers, `paper_resolve` collapses their identifiers, `paper_get` produces one merged metadata/BibTeX record, and `integrity_check` reports retraction status. A downloaded PDF is stored as content-addressed Markdown in PaperMemory, and a quotation must pass `quote_check` or `trace` before the agent treats it as evidence. The notebook records the work; `scientific_result` records the final finding.

## Deep review

![Deep review](docs/assets/diagrams/deep-review.svg)

`deep_review` runs a full Deep-Review-style critique of one manuscript with the vendored
[open-deepreview](https://github.com/raktim-mondol/open-deepreview) engine. The paper is segmented
and every segment is reviewed with the whole manuscript in context; comments are anchored to a page
or a quotation, and a scholar-peer pass adds strengths and weaknesses, a claim-evidence map, a
nine-item reproducibility checklist and questions for the authors. `estimate` prices a run before it
starts, `review` runs on the session model (no separate key or endpoint), `show` reads a stored
review back, and `status` marks it stale after the manuscript changes. Artifacts stay in
`.dsh/deep-review/<key>/`, and `provenance_audit` indexes the claims stored there.
[Read more](docs/PAPERS.md#deep-review)

## Deep research

![Deep research](docs/assets/diagrams/deep-research.svg)

`deep_research` runs the investigation a literature question actually asks for, and keeps the
state a chat cannot. The request is frozen verbatim and re-read by every step, so a long run
cannot quietly drift onto a different question. It sweeps the literature through the existing
`literature_search` router and a web lane (Parallel, Exa, Tavily, Brave) for guidance documents,
registers, and reporting; finds where the sources contradict each other; picks the loci where
reading deeply would change the answer; drafts from three angles; then has four critics attack the
draft and repairs it with capped hunks — after synthesis the report cannot be regenerated, only
patched.

Two things it counts that a plain agent gets wrong. **Voice, not copies:** an independence
clustering pass groups DOI, exact and near titles, and identical bodies across hosts, so five
reprints of one press release argue with the weight of one source (distinct DOIs are never
merged). **Verified, not plausible:** every citation is checked against stored text in
PaperMemory, a quote nothing read is reported `not_checked` rather than passed, and an
unacknowledged retraction blocks the ship. Fetched pages arrive inside an
`<untrusted-source>` fence, so a page that tries to instruct the agent is read as content.

Scale is one knob — `effort=low|medium|high` — and it is inferred from the request when not given
("quickly" is low, "comprehensive systematic review" is high). A request that points both ways
returns `needs_input` with a question and creates nothing: no run, no model call. Runs are
resumable and budget-capped, so a crash continues at the step that died instead of restarting.
The pipeline shape — step-per-phase, the frozen canonical query, patch-only repair, the ship
gate, independence clustering, and untrusted-source fencing — is adapted from
[hyperresearch](https://github.com/jordan-gibbs/hyperresearch) (MIT); no upstream code is
vendored, and [NOTICE](NOTICE) records the attribution.
[Read more](docs/RESEARCH.md#deep-research)

## Documentation

| Start here | Go deeper | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| [Install and run](docs/INSTALL.md) | [Search](docs/SEARCH.md) | [Tool index](docs/TOOLS.md) |
| [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) | [Papers and evidence](docs/PAPERS.md) | [Configuration](docs/CONFIGURATION.md) |
| [Documentation home](docs/README.md) | [Writing](docs/WRITING.md) | [Changelog](docs/CHANGELOG.md) |
| | [Research](docs/RESEARCH.md) | [Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) |
| | [Workspace](docs/WORKSPACE.md) | [Optional tools](docs/OPTIONAL-TOOLS.md) |
| | [Compute](docs/COMPUTE.md) · [Agents](docs/AGENTS.md) · [Skills](docs/SKILLS.md) · [RSI](docs/RSI.md) | [Engine notes](docs/ACADEMIC-HARNESS-ENGINE.md) |

## Requirements and scope

- **Tested on Linux only.** The plugin, its runtime installs (PaperMemory, zvec-grep, TextFold), and the end-to-end browser tests have been run on Linux (Python 3.13, Node 24). macOS and Windows have not been tested and may not work; Python is needed for PaperMemory, `power_analysis`, the `sci_inspect` helpers, and the managed Modal SDK.
- **DSH 0.2.1–0.2.x.** The plugin's bundle patches the web-app layer, so the profile must include `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`; the standard `web` profile does.
- **A preset check matters.** The research persona, search connectors, PaperMemory, zvec-grep, paper tools, citation/review/tournament tools, and the `subagent_pro`/`subagent_vision` routes are scoped to the Academic Harness preset. Both routes inherit the session model unless you configure a provider/model. Only the general-purpose tools (`notebook`, `fold_text`, `scientific_result`, `sci_inspect`, images, LaTeX, PDF, Mermaid, compute, templates) are on every preset.
- **Keys are optional.** No credential is needed to install or start; each connector stays disabled until its key is present. Some runtimes install in the background on first use — see [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md#runtime-installs).
- **One DSH surface at a time.** `dsh-web`, `dsh-tui`, `dsh-martty`, and `academic-harness` share `$DSH_HOME`, port `3080`, and the zvec-grep daemon. Stop the previous one before starting another; see [Install](docs/INSTALL.md#one-dsh-surface-at-a-time).
- **Renamed in v0.16.0** from `dsh-researchcraft` / ResearchCraft. Old env names are still honored; migration is in [Install](docs/INSTALL.md#renamed-in-v0160).

## Development

```sh
npm install       # once, for the Settings page build
npm run build     # after any client/ change
npm run docs:diagrams   # regenerate the SVG figures from docs/diagrams/*.mmd
```

Server-side code is plain ESM JS with no build step. Tests are plain Node scripts; see [Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) for the full suite and the `paper_fold` live test.

## License

The Supervisor-Skills bundle is mixed-license: six skills are CC BY 4.0, five are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike), and `drawio-reconstruction` is MIT; those terms apply to those skill files, not to the plugin as a whole.

# billion-context

English | 中文

Context-compression plugin — billion-context is all you need.

small context windows (100K is enough) · 5× fewer tokens · month-long single sessions (billions of tokens) · high compression quality

npm install -g billion-context --prefix=~/.local

                                           

--- > **Cache health at a glance:** a healthy session keeps a **95–97%** prefix-cache hit rate — compression itself costs ≤2%. Sustained lower? Check attribution with `/acp` or `/acp-cache` (see [FAQ](#faq)); usual causes, in order: upstream cache TTL expiry · model switch · a bili bug (please report) · other/unknown. ## Community QQ Group: 1056132097 (full) 1108730198 (full) 1129868472 (open) --- ## 📄 Paper / Preprint - **[Model-Driven Incremental Hierarchical Compression: Training-Free Multi-Generational Context Management for Long-Lived Coding Agents](./paper/model-driven-incremental-hierarchical-compression-training-free-multi-generational-context-management-for-long-lived-coding-agents.md)** (English, v0.2) > 📝 **The paper itself is open-sourced under the MIT License as part of the codebase (`paper/`). It is a living document — anyone may edit it; improvements are welcome via pull request.** A production-scale longitudinal study: 4.5 months, three hosts, 174,327 model calls, 18.76B cumulative input tokens (~24.7B across all hosts), zero window violations on 204,800-token models, marathon sessions of 8,584–12,049 calls. ### 📊 Independent Third-Party Benchmarks - **[1,500-Item Cross-Benchmark Evaluation (`LongMemEval-S` · `ContextBench` · `MemoryAgentBench`)](./benchmarks/third-party-1500/README.md)** ([中文版](./benchmarks/third-party-1500/README.zh-CN.md)) — head-to-head comparison of `billion-context` (`v0.1.202`) against `full` context and 3 RAG arms (`bm25`, `embedding`, `embedding-rerank`) with `DeepSeek V4.1 Flash`, `Qwen3-Embedding-8B`, `Qwen3-Reranker-4B`, and `Pi Agent`: **#1 on ContextBench** (`0.3097` Utilized F1, `-58.3%` cost vs `full`), **+16.6% over best RAG on LongMemEval-S** (`79.20%` vs `62.60%`, `-71.1%` independent-session cost vs `full`), and **100% survival on 1.48M-token MemoryAgentBench TTL** (`30×` steady-state compression where `full` fails `199/199`). --- `billion-context` sits between **any** agent and its model API, rewriting Anthropic/OpenAI streams with [acp-kernel](https://github.com/ranxianglei/acp-kernel) compression. The model decides **when** and **what** to compress into high-fidelity summaries — not a hard truncation limit. ## Why Long coding sessions blow up context. Each provider charges per token, and once you pass the context window the session degrades or dies. `billion-context` compresses consumed conversation into layered summaries so you can run a single session for days — billions of tokens through one context window. Unlike a host's built-in summarizer, compression here is **incremental, reversible, and prefix-cache friendly**: summaries are written in small ranges, can be decompressed on demand, and the cache prefix stays intact. ## How it works ``` Agent (Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Aider ...) │ you point the agent's base URL at the proxy ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ billion-context│ 1. parse the request (Anthropic or OpenAI shape) │ proxy │ 2. run acp-kernel compression on the conversation │ │ 3. inject a `compress` tool + compression philosophy │ │ 4. forward to the real model API │ │ 5. rewrite the streaming response └─────────────────┘ │ ▼ real model API (Anthropic / OpenAI / compatible) ``` ### Context-management tools The proxy injects four context-management tools into the conversation; the model calls them itself as context grows, and the proxy executes `compress` server-side so folded ranges stay summarized in history until restored: - **`compress`** — fold a message range into a detailed summary. - **`decompress`** — restore a compressed range when exact details are needed again. - **`search_context`** — keyword search over compressed summaries and visible messages. - **`acp_status`** — context-usage overview plus which ranges are still compressible. ## Which do I need? Pick by your client: | Client | Use | |---|---| | **pi** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili pi` (launcher) or `bili plugin install pi` (native); standalone [`billion-context-pi`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context-pi) remains usable — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md#pi-pidev-coding-agent) | | **opencode** (1.x / 2.x) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili opencode` (launcher) or `bili plugin install opencode` (native); standalone [`opencode-acp`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/opencode-acp) remains usable on 1.x — full guide: [OpenCode](CLIENTS.md#opencode) | | **omp** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili omp` (built-in plugin) or `bili plugin install omp` (self-spawning native plugin, no launcher) | | **dsh** | `bili dsh` (launcher — full native plugin via `--patch`) or `bili plugin install dsh` ≡ `dsh plugin --profile add billion-context` (one unified lane) — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **kimi** | `bili plugin install kimi` (self-spawning native, Kimi Code ≥ 2.0.0) or `bili kimi` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **hermes** | `bili plugin install hermes` (self-spawning native, Python plugin #958) or `bili hermes` (cert-MITM) | | **zcode** (Z.ai / bigmodel coding plan) | `bili plugin install zcode` (self-spawning native, #1145) or cert-MITM via the GUI's Settings → Network or `/bili/` prefix — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **claude** | `bili claude` (launcher) or `bili plugin install claude` (native posture, #964 — managed settings block + session-owned proxy; see the notes below) | | **codex** | `bili codex` (launcher — the full zero-config posture) or `bili plugin install codex` (MCP-shell tools companion: **start bili first** — the shell never spawns a proxy and never routes codex's own traffic) — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md#codex-openai-codex-cli) | | **jcode** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili jcode` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (compiled Rust binary, no plugin seam, [#962](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/962)) | | **gemini** (Gemini CLI) | `bili gemini` (launcher, `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite) or `/bili/` prefix — launcher-only (no in-loop tool seam, #1043) | | **iflow** (iFlow CLI) | `bili iflow` (launcher, `IFLOW_BASE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite) or `/bili/` prefix | | **qwen** (Qwen Code) | `bili qwen` (launcher, cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix | | **antigravity** (Antigravity CLI / agy, Google) | `bili antigravity` (launcher, `CLOUD_CODE_URL` `/bili/` rewrite of daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com — Antigravity's real default upstream, #3129) or `/bili/` prefix — no plugin seam (closed Go language_server; its user-plugin surface is additive-only, #2115) — details: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md) | | **mcode** (MiniMax Code) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili mcode` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (event hooks only, no model-request seam, [#1050](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/1050)) | | **aider** | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) via `bili aider` (cert-MITM) or `/bili/` prefix — no native mode (shell-command-only hooks, no tool-injection seam, [#1048](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/1048)) | | **copilot** (GitHub Copilot CLI) | `bili copilot` (launcher, cert-MITM) — closed Go binary, no plugin seam (#1049) | | **amp** (Amp CLI) | `bili amp` (launcher, cert-MITM) — closed Go binary, no plugin seam (#1049) | | **crush** (Charm Crush) | `bili crush` (launcher, cert-MITM) — open-source Go binary, no plugin seam; built-in provider hosts whitelisted, custom `base_url`s auto-discovered from crush.json (#2340) | | **zed** (Zed editor) | `bili zed` (launcher, cert-MITM) — open-source Rust editor, no plugin seam; reqwest honors HTTPS_PROXY, CA via SSL_CERT_FILE (Linux env probing); built-in provider hosts whitelisted, custom `api_url`s auto-discovered from settings.json; loopback providers (ollama/lmstudio) stay direct via NO_PROXY (#2340) | | **goose** (Goose CLI) | `bili goose` (launcher) — rustls trusts no CA file, so no cert-MITM: openai/anthropic legs via `OPENAI_HOST`/`ANTHROPIC_HOST`, custom providers via a regenerated `GOOSE_PATH_ROOT` overlay (#1049) | | **everything else** (no context hook) | [`billion-context`](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context) — `bili ` (launcher, preferred) or `/bili/` prefix | **Native mode vs standalone extensions.** The host-native plugins (`bili plugin install …`) and the standalone in-process extensions (`billion-context-pi`, `opencode-acp`) are **mutually exclusive** — both active means double compression. The installer makes the switch: it replaces the legacy entries (bare name, `npm:` alias, versioned, path form; array or object shape) and snapshots the original config to `.bili-bak` once; a **project-local** install is not touched — remove that one by hand. As a runtime safety net for manual installs, the native entries set `BILLION_CONTEXT_NATIVE=` synchronously at load so a standalone extension can stand down at action time. On the pi side the marker needs `billion-context-pi` **0.1.72+**, and the pi-native entry scans both pi settings files once its proxy is up and warns loudly when it spots a co-resident legacy entry the installer never saw — that warning is the only visible signal while an old `billion-context-pi` silently double-compresses. ## Install Linux / macOS — install with a user-level prefix (no `sudo`, no npm config changes, and `bili`'s self-update never hits permission errors): ```bash npm install -g billion-context --prefix=~/.local ``` The `bili` command lands in `~/.local/bin` — already on PATH in most distros; if not, add `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`. On nvm or Homebrew Node the default prefix is already user-owned — a plain `npm install -g billion-context` works as-is. On Windows the default prefix (`%APPDATA%\npm`) is also user-writable — plain `npm install -g billion-context`. This installs the `bili` command (`bili-proxy` is kept as an alias). Hitting `EACCES` with an old root-owned prefix? Reinstall with `--prefix=~/.local` (pass the flag again on any future npm reinstall of `bili`) — that is the permanent fix; avoid `sudo`. Prefer containers? A `Dockerfile` ships at the repository root — see [Running in Docker](#running-in-docker) below. ## Quickstart Three ways to use it — pick one: - **Native plugin (most native):** `bili plugin install ` — bili becomes a plugin inside the client; start the client as usual. - **Launcher (config-free):** one `bili ` command brings up the proxy and the client together — no real config file is ever touched. - **URL change (most universal):** prefix your client's baseURL with the proxy origin + `/bili/`. Mechanism details behind these three options (plugin lifecycle, runtime-info protocol, injection priority) live in [TECHNICAL-NOTES.md](TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). Ports, briefly (#1660): `bili start` (manual) owns `8787`. Everything a lane spawns for you (native hooks, launcher lanes) lives in a separate self-managed zone starting at `18787` — collisions hop +1 and each lane remembers its drift, so zero-config installs never fight you for a port, and a deliberate `bili start` daemon is attached by default. Attach is lane-aware (#2905): a hook rides its own lane's instance first, NEVER another declared lane's — except lanes you list in `native.attachLanePriority` — and the 8787 user-zone daemon stays the LAST-resort fallback. An upgrade-restart that finds the previous build still draining on the lane's port waits for it to release (up to 5s) and rebinds the SAME port instead of drifting (#1723); only a genuinely occupied port hops +1 — and that hop is now logged loudly. ### Option 1 — Native plugin (`bili plugin install pi` / `omp` / `opencode` / `dsh` / `kimi` / `hermes` / `zcode`) The proxy lives inside the client: install once, then start the client exactly as you always do — no launcher command, no env vars, no fixed port, no URL edits. Supported today for **pi**, **omp**, **opencode** (1.x and 2.x), **dsh**, **kimi**, **hermes** and **zcode**: ```bash bili plugin install pi # registers a "billion-context" entry in pi's settings (npm form when bili itself was npm-installed) bili plugin install omp # registers an extensions entry in omp's config.yml (~/.omp/agent/config.yml) bili plugin install opencode # registers the plugin in opencode's real config + disables native auto-compaction bili plugin install dsh # runs 'dsh plugin --profile add billion-context' for every existing profile bili plugin install kimi # writes $KIMI_CODE_HOME/plugins/managed/billion-context/kimi.plugin.json (+ installed.json record); per-session routing block lands in config.toml on first start (Kimi Code >= 2.0.0) bili plugin install hermes # copies the Python plugin into ~/.hermes/plugins/billion-context/ (+ machine-owned bili.json sidecar) and enables it via `hermes plugins enable billion-context` bili plugin install zcode # writes hooks.enabled + a SessionStart hook + mcp.servers.bili into ~/.zcode/cli/config.json; per-session routing lands in the bigmodel provider store on first start bili plugin remove # undo (dsh removes through the same channel; config snapshots go to .bili-bak) ``` Where a client has its own plugin channel you can also install natively, skipping bili commands entirely: - **dsh:** `dsh plugin --profile add billion-context` is the very command `bili plugin install dsh` drives per profile (npm form only; a git checkout has no published entry — pasting a GitHub address installs source without `dist/` and the bundle never loads) — same end state either way (pnpm into the profile, bundled patch layer mounted by dsh itself); remove through the same channel. See the dsh section below. - **opencode:** add the bare npm name to your real config's plugin list — `"plugin": ["billion-context"]` (npm form only; a git checkout has no published entry). The package publishes `exports["./server"]` → `dist/agent/opencode-native.js`, so opencode loads it through its own Npm.add machinery and the plugin self-spawns exactly like the bili-installed form. Do the two things the bili installer would have done for you too: set `"compaction": { "auto": false }` in the same config (otherwise OpenCode's native auto-compaction double-compresses) and keep a manual backup of the file first. - **claude:** this repository doubles as a Claude Code plugin marketplace — `/plugin marketplace add ranxianglei/billion-context`, then `/plugin install billion-context@billion-context`, then run `/billion-context:bili-setup` (it drives `bili plugin install claude` for you and tells you to restart). Same end state as the bili installer; the plugin ships no hooks or MCP entries of its own, so nothing double-registers. For pi / omp / kimi / claude there is no client-side channel — `bili plugin install ` writes their config entries for you (kimi's declarative `kimi.plugin.json` + registry record, claude's managed settings block, …). Notes: - Native mode is **mutually exclusive** with the standalone in-process extensions (`billion-context-pi`, `opencode-acp`) — the installer swaps the entries and snapshots the original config (`.bili-bak`). - **pi:** native installs wire in built-in subagents by default (`acp_delegate` / `acp_delegate_wait` / `acp_delegate_cancel`) — how to disable them while keeping context compression: [Pi built-in subagents](#pi-built-in-subagents). - OpenCode legacy sessions, V1/V2 shapes and caveats: [OpenCode](CLIENTS.md#opencode). - `kimi` reports runtime-info at bootstrap only (static headers can't carry per-request window/model values); subagent tool calls are routed by the proxy's outbound tool-use witness ring (#1685) — no model-visible conversation id. - `hermes`'s native plugin is Python: it points hermes' httpx stack at the proxy via env vars after a health check and stamps per-request headers through an `llm_request` middleware. - `codex` is the one client a plugin install cannot make self-sufficient: codex routes model traffic via env only (no config-file routing seam for the default ChatGPT-login provider — a managed `model_providers` block would force API-key auth and drop subscription login), and an MCP server cannot inject env into its parent. `bili plugin install codex` writes a single `[mcp_servers.bili]` block into `~/.codex/config.toml` (command = node, args = dist/mcp.js) exposing the four ACP tools; at session start the shell resolves a proxy — env `BILI_MCP_PROXY` > the live-instance record (any lane's proxy or a `bili start` daemon) > the 8787 user-zone default (#1660 removed the install-time origin bake, #403) — nothing reachable → `tools/list` fails with -32003. So: start bili first (`bili start` or any client's lane proxy), export HTTPS_PROXY yourself if you also want compression, or use `bili codex` for the zero-config full posture. Mechanics: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md#codex-openai-codex-cli). - `claude` has a native posture (#964): managed settings block + `SessionStart` hook + MCP shell; the hook rides the self-managed port zone (#1660) and re-pins the managed URL to the live origin each session, so port drift self-heals. Since #1821 the MCP shell also watches the proxy mid-session (30 s tick × 3 failures) and respawns a dead lane proxy itself, so model requests recover within ~90 s instead of a new session (same semantics as the zcode lane). Opt out with `BILI_NATIVE_CLAUDE=0` (passthrough). Mechanics: [TECHNICAL-NOTES.md](TECHNICAL-NOTES.md). **Known limitation (#2290):** the Claude Desktop app's Code tab (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=claude-desktop`) sets its own `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on its embedded Claude Code, overriding the managed one — desktop sessions bypass the proxy entirely while the managed block's `DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1` still applies, so they get neither bili compression nor native auto-compaction. The hook warns loudly at session start (and records it for `bili doctor`, which also flags machines where Claude Desktop is installed alongside the native lane); terminal sessions are unaffected. **Field-tested 2026-10-06 (#2290):** putting `HTTPS_PROXY` in the settings `env` block produced zero CONNECT traffic to a live MITM-enabled proxy on Claude Desktop 2.19675.1 / embedded CC 2.1.288 (Windows 11) — the variable reaches no network stack there, matching the CLI behavior of that era — note that newer builds (CC 2.1.301+) DO honour `HTTPS_PROXY` on the CLI, which is why `bili claude` routes via the `/bili/` base-URL rewrite — the launcher gives this lane no proxy and no CA at all, and a child that brings a proxy of its own gets the loopback hosts merged into `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` so that leg stays direct regardless of its proxy behavior (#3446). As of that version there is no usable routing seam on the desktop Code tab; the lane stays tracked in [#2290](https://github.com/ranxianglei/billion-context/issues/2290) in case upstream changes behavior. Desktop-only users can restore native auto-compact with `bili plugin remove claude`. Since #5095 the managed block also installs a `SubagentStart` hook (`node /dist/claude-subagent-hook.js`) that mints a per-dispatch lane token into each subagent's context: subagents that ride the parent's session id with no agent-id headers (the VS Code extension build, #4352) key onto their own `|sub:…:t:` compression lanes, so parallel same-type dispatches stop merging (and the token disappears from later requests once the first message folds — those fall back to the fingerprint lane). Uninstall removes the hook with the managed block. - `zcode` has a native posture (#1145): managed `~/.zcode/cli/config.json` block + per-session provider `baseURL` rewrite. Full mechanics: [CLIENTS.md](CLIENTS.md). - `jcode` and `aider` have no native mode (no plugin/MCP/tool-injection seam: #962, #1048) — use `bili jcode` / `bili aider`. - `copilot`, `amp` and `goose` are launcher-only (#1049); goose cannot be cert-MITMed (rustls trusts no CA file) and rides plain-HTTP base-URL redirects instead. ### Option 2 — Launcher (`bili pi` / `bili codex` / `bili claude` / `bili omp` / `bili opencode` / `bili hermes` / `bili dsh` / `bili codebuddy` / `bili qoder` / `bili trae` / `bili jcode` / `bili kimi` / `bili gemini` / `bili iflow` / `bili qwen` / `bili antigravity` / `bili mcode` / `bili aider` / `bili copilot` / `bili amp` / `bili goose`) The launcher wraps a client in one command: it starts a proxy on an independent port (a fresh instance is always spawned — a port is never reused), then points the client at it — **certificate-based MITM** where the client honors proxy/CA env vars, or an isolated **`/bili/` config rewrite** where it doesn't. No real config file is ever edited; the client's own config is READ to discover which HTTPS upstream hosts it talks to, and those hosts are whitelisted for MITM so the proxy can TLS-terminate exactly them and blind-tunnel everything else. ```bash bili pi # launch pi through the proxy — file-free (#535): env + extension registerProvider, real ~/.pi untouched bili codex # launch codex through the proxy bili claude # launch claude through the proxy bili omp # pi-style, file-free (#535): env + extension registerProvider + compaction cancel, real ~/.omp untouched bili opencode # OpenCode (1.x & 2.x): full guide in the [OpenCode](CLIENTS.md#opencode) section below bili hermes # file-free (#535): hermes proxy env (HTTPS_PROXY + combined CA bundle via SSL_CERT_FILE) — https via CONNECT MITM, http via absolute-form forward proxy; real ~/.hermes untouched bili dsh # deepseek-harness: full native plugin injected via --patch (#941) — real dsh tools, session-bound /acp + /acp-cache (plugin mode); non-loopback upstreams ride proxy envs, loopback keeps the overlay DSH_HOME rewrite (#535); dsh auto-compaction off everywhere — host plane via the bundle patch, web-profile presets at load time (#1772/#2474/#3354) bili codebuddy # Tencent CodeBuddy Code CLI: CODEBUDDY_BASE_URL /bili/ rewrite (OpenAI chat completions wire), budget aligned via CODEBUDDY_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW; real ~/.codebuddy untouched bili qoder # qoder: model endpoint is hardcoded https (no /bili/ rewrite possible) — cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, default model hosts whitelisted (#653) bili trae # Trae CLI (ByteDance, closed Go binary, no base-URL override) — cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + SSL_CERT_FILE, model host from TRAE_CLI_API_HOST or the default enterprise gateway (#655) bili jcode # jcode (Rust agent harness) — env-only cert-MITM launch: HTTPS_PROXY + SSL_CERT_FILE, model host api.z.ai whitelisted, local loopback providers stay direct via NO_PROXY bili kimi # Kimi Code CLI (Moonshot): standard proxy envs except an unconditional loopback bypass — https via cert-MITM, http via absolute-form forward proxy; loopback endpoints inventoried with a manual /bili/ hint (#757) bili gemini # Gemini CLI (Google): GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL /bili/ rewrite to generativelanguage.googleapis.com (Google native wire), real ~/.gemini untouched bili iflow # iFlow CLI: IFLOW_BASE_URL /bili/ rewrite to apis.iflow.cn/v1 (OpenAI chat-completions wire), real ~/.iflow untouched bili qwen # Qwen Code (multi-protocol gemini-cli fork, no base-URL hook): cert-MITM via HTTPS_PROXY + NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, default DashScope/Qwen model hosts whitelisted, custom relays via --mitm-domain bili antigravity # Antigravity CLI (agy, Google): CLOUD_CODE_URL /bili/ rewrite of daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com — the real default upstream (bare cloudcode-pa 400s on /v1internal:*, #3129); undocumented language-server env override, v2.19.1 binary-verified; wire recognized as Google native by path (#2115) bili mcode # MiniMax Code CLI: same shape as kimi (proxy envs, unconditional loopback bypass, cert-MITM/absolute-form);

# dsh-plugin-reactive-resume Connect [Reactive Resume](https://rxresu.me) to [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Read, create, and edit your resumes and job applications from a Harness session. ## Install ```bash dsh plugin --profile add dsh-plugin-reactive-resume ``` This package declares `dsh.bundle`, so the profile picks it up as a layer and mounts it automatically. Until you configure a key it mounts nothing and logs a warning, so installing it never leaves a profile unbootable. ## Configure Mint an API key at `https://rxresu.me/dashboard/settings/api-keys` and export it as `RXRESUME_API_KEY` — the bundle patch reads that variable. To set it explicitly, or to change any other option, patch the row by id from your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: reactive-resume config: apiKey: !!js process.env.RXRESUME_API_KEY ``` ### Options | Key | Default | Description | | ------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `apiKey` | `''` | API key from `/dashboard/settings/api-keys`. Empty mounts nothing. | | `url` | `https://rxresu.me` | Origin of your instance. Set this if you self-host. | | `serverName` | `resume` | Tool namespace. Tools reach the model as `mcp____`. | | `toolCallTimeoutMs` | `60000` | Per-tool-call timeout. | Every tool Reactive Resume publishes is exposed. Narrowing that set is not currently possible from a plugin: Harness's `ctx.tools.restrict()` requires an agent-scoped context, which a plugin context is not. ### Self-hosted ```yaml - id: reactive-resume config: apiKey: !!js process.env.RXRESUME_API_KEY url: http://localhost:3000 ``` ## What it does Bridges Reactive Resume's MCP server into `ctx.tools`, and contributes a system-prompt section covering the things models get wrong about resume editing: reading before patching, RFC 6902 path construction against the published schema, UUID-keyed section entries, and locked resumes. You could wire the bridge yourself with a raw `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row. What you cannot do that way is contribute the prompt section — that is what this package adds. ## Harness compatibility The peer ranges list each supported DSH host line as an explicit `||` union: `^0.1.0-rc.6` (what this package already shipped against) plus `^0.2.0-rc.1` (which admits `0.2.0-rc.1` and `0.2.0-rc.2`). The union is purely additive — every version the old range admitted is still admitted. Every published DSH release is a prerelease, which makes the comparison mode matter: - The Harness host decides whether to mount a plugin with `semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })`. The upper bound is what rejected the old range there: `^0.1.0-rc.6` expands to `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0`, and `0.2.0-rc.2` sorts above `0.2.0-0` because the numeric identifier `0` precedes `rc`. - npm's default mode — the one the plugin market's checker uses — additionally requires a comparator set to pin the same `major.minor.patch` tuple with a prerelease of its own. Under that mode the bare `^0.1.0-rc.6` admits only `0.1.0-rc.6` through `0.1.0-rc.8`. Measured against all 29 published host releases, that gap is wide: `^0.1.0-rc.6` admits 22 of them under the host's mode (every `0.1.x` line, including `0.1.5-rc.2` and `0.1.7-rc.2`) but only 3 under npm's default mode. Widening the upper bound does not close it, because the default mode ignores the widened comparator: `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.3.0-0` still admits only those same 3, and `*` admits none at all. `^0.1.0-rc.6 || ^0.2.0-rc.1` admits 24 releases under the host's mode and 5 under the default one, so an explicit union member per host line is the only form both checkers agree on. Against `0.2.0-rc.2` this package needed no source change: `dsh-mcp-client@0.2.0-rc.2` keeps its `Config` union, its `apply(ctx, config)` signature, and the `mcp____` public tool name, while `dsh-system-prompt@0.2.0-rc.2` keeps `section({ name, order, text })`. What 0.2.0 adds to the bridge — MCP resource publishing and a server-instructions prompt section — is additive and scoped to `ctx.inject(["mcpResources"])` / `ctx.inject(["systemPrompt"])`, neither of which this package depends on. ## Development This package lives in the [Reactive Resume monorepo](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume) at `packages/dsh-plugin`, next to `packages/mcp` — the server it bridges. `src/tool-names.test.ts` checks every tool the prompt guide names against `@reactive-resume/mcp/tool-names`, so renaming a tool breaks this package in the same pull request. ```bash pnpm --filter dsh-plugin-reactive-resume test pnpm --filter dsh-plugin-reactive-resume build ``` ## License MIT > [!IMPORTANT] > Reactive Resume now lives at **[`reactive-resume/reactive-resume`](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume)** on GitHub. > GHCR images publish to `ghcr.io/reactive-resume/reactive-resume`. > Docker Hub stays at `amruthpillai/reactive-resume`.

Reactive Resume

Reactive Resume is a free and open-source resume builder for writing resumes and cover letters, checking your work, and tracking job applications.

Get Started · Learn More

Sponsored by

--- Create a free account, import an existing resume or start fresh, and see the finished page as you write. Download a PDF, Word, Markdown, or JSON file, or share your resume with a public link. You can also run the whole application on your own infrastructure. You own your data. The codebase is open source under the MIT license, with no tracking, no ads, and no paid tier. Optional AI features use a provider you connect; hosting and provider usage may have their own costs. ![Reactive Resume v6 editor with Write, Design, and Check modes and a live PDF preview](docs/images/getting-started/editor-overview.webp) ## Build a better resume, together [Join the Reactive Resume community on Discord](https://discord.gg/u9pAd3za9t) to exchange resume feedback, get help using or self-hosting the app, and share ideas with other users and contributors. - **Resume feedback:** post a redacted resume and one specific question, or help someone improve theirs. - **Help:** find troubleshooting discussions and ask questions in dedicated forum threads. - **Contribute:** discuss ideas, translations, and code with the people building Reactive Resume. Feedback comes from fellow community members. Remove contact details and other private information before posting. ## Features **Write, Design, and Check** - Redesigned editor with inline content editing and click-to-select on the page - Live PDF preview and browser downloads powered by Forme, rendered in a background worker - Rich text, custom sections, drag-and-drop ordering, and structured dates with consistent formatting - Autosave, local recovery of unsaved resume drafts, and up to 200 undo steps - Phone and tablet layouts, keyboard shortcuts, and a searchable command bar **Templates and Customization** - 18 templates, including the new Porygon and Smeargle, previewed with your own content - One-column, two-column, and ATS-safe template filters - Font presets, custom fonts, colors, spacing, A4 and Letter paper, and left or right sidebars - Fit overflowing content by adjusting density, margins, and text size - Custom Styles written as Semantic CSS, with an element picker on the page **Resume Checks** - Readability checks with findings pinned to the relevant lines - Job-posting keyword matching and a view of the text hiring software reads - Checks on the exported PDF, plus an optional AI writing review - A public [ATS checker](https://rxresu.me/ats-checker) that reads PDFs in your browser without an account **Documents and Cover Letters** - One searchable library for resumes and letters, with tags, sorting, and grid or list views - Standalone cover letters with their own editor, exports, and version history - Link a letter to a resume to keep its sender details and design in sync, or customize it independently - Automatic and named versions you can preview and restore - Trash with Undo and a 30-day recovery window **Job Applications** - List, Board, Insights, and Calendar views for tracking applications from Saved to Offer - Save jobs from a URL or pasted posting; optional keyword search through Firecrawl, Tavily, or Exa - Tailor a resume and draft a cover letter for a saved job - Track contacts, notes, follow-ups, application outcomes, and the documents you sent - Schedule interviews, export calendar events, and import or export applications as CSV **AI Assistant** - Assistant beside your resume or letter, with conversations tied to that document - Proposed edits show what changes and why; accept or reject each suggestion - Improve selected text, review writing, and draft letters from a resume and job posting - Connect OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, or other supported providers and compatible endpoints - Optional web search and page reading; self-hosters can configure shared AI and web-access providers **Import, Export, and Sharing** - Import Reactive Resume JSON, JSON Resume, LinkedIn data exports, PDF, and Word files - JSON, LinkedIn, and readable PDF imports work without AI; Word imports require a connected provider - Export resumes and letters as PDF, Word (DOCX), Markdown, or JSON - Share resumes through public links with optional password protection and view/download statistics - REST API and MCP server for document management, imports, exports, checks, and application workflows **Privacy and Control** - Self-host with Docker, Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, or a 1-click deploy on Hostinger - No tracking or ads; export your account data or delete your account - Passkeys, two-factor authentication, and linked sign-in providers - Multiple interface languages, light/dark/system themes, and reduced-motion support ## Templates

## Quick Start Use the [hosted app](https://rxresu.me) to start writing, or build this checkout locally with Docker and Docker Compose: ```bash # Clone the repository git clone --depth=1 https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume.git reactive-resume cd reactive-resume # Create your local configuration cp .env.example .env # Edit .env: set AUTH_SECRET and a separate ENCRYPTION_SECRET. # Generate each secret with: openssl rand -hex 32 # Build the app and start PostgreSQL, Redis, and SeaweedFS docker compose up -d --build # Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser ``` This builds the checked-out source. For a deployment using published images, follow the [Docker guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker). For source development, see the [development setup guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/development). ## Tech Stack | Category | Technology | | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | Web app | React 19 SPA, TanStack Router, and Vite | | Server | Hono on Node.js 24 or Cloudflare Workers | | Language | TypeScript | | Monorepo | pnpm and Turborepo | | Database | PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM | | API | oRPC, OpenAPI REST, and MCP | | Auth | Better Auth | | Styling | Tailwind CSS | | UI Components | Base UI + shared UI package | | State Management | Zustand + TanStack Query | | PDF rendering | Forme, with PDF.js for the viewer | | Rich text | TipTap | | Localization | Lingui | ## Documentation The full documentation lives at [docs.rxresu.me](https://docs.rxresu.me): | Guide | Description | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | [Getting started](https://docs.rxresu.me/getting-started) | First-time setup and basic usage | | [What's new in v6](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/whats-new-in-v6) | Changes and where familiar features moved | | [Checking your resume](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/checking-your-resume) | Readability, job match, and writing reviews | | [Using the assistant](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/using-the-assistant) | Ask for changes and review proposed edits | | [Resume and career agent skills](plugins/reactive-resume/README.md) | 32 skills for resume writing, specific roles and the job search | | [Writing a cover letter](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/writing-a-cover-letter) | Create a letter and link it to a resume | | [Tracking job applications](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/tracking-job-applications) | Saved jobs, stages, interviews, and insights | | [Exporting your resume](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/exporting-your-resume) | PDF, Word, Markdown, and JSON downloads | | [API](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/using-the-api) and [MCP](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/using-the-mcp-server) | Connect scripts and external assistants | | [Self-hosting](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker) | Deploy on your own infrastructure | | [Migrating from v5](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/upgrading-to-v6) | Migrations and integration changes | | [Development setup](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/development) | Local development environment | | [Project architecture](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/architecture) | Codebase structure and package boundaries | ## Self-Hosting Reactive Resume runs the same application everywhere: PostgreSQL for data, plus storage for uploads. Pick the option that fits how much you want to manage. | Option | Best for | Guide | | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [Hostinger](#hostinger) | A ready-made VPS with no setup | [Hostinger guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/hostinger) | | [Vercel](#vercel) | Serverless, with managed database and storage | [Vercel guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/vercel) | | [Cloudflare Workers](#cloudflare-workers) | Workers, R2 and your own PostgreSQL | [Cloudflare guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/cloudflare) | | [Docker and Kubernetes](#docker-and-kubernetes) | Your own server, homelab or cluster | [Docker](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker) · [Kubernetes](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/kubernetes) | > **PDF generation in v6** uses Forme in the browser and on the server. No Browserless, Chromium, or external print service is needed. Legacy `PRINTER_*` and `BROWSERLESS_*` environment variables can be removed. ### Hostinger The quickest way to get going is a 1-click deploy on Hostinger, starting at $6.49/month. Their VPS plans include a ready-made Reactive Resume template that provisions the Docker environment and brings the app up for you, with weekly backups and a Docker manager UI included — so you can skip the setup entirely. See the [Hostinger guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/hostinger) for what the template sets up and what to configure afterwards, such as email, your own domain, and turning off sign-ups. ### Vercel [![Deploy with Vercel](https://vercel.com/button)](https://vercel.com/new/clone?repository-url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Freactive-resume%2Freactive-resume&project-name=reactive-resume&repository-name=reactive-resume&env=AUTH_SECRET%2CENCRYPTION_SECRET&envDescription=Generate+two+independent+secrets+with+openssl+rand+-hex+32.+Keep+these+values+across+deployments.&envLink=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.rxresu.me%2Fself-hosting%2Fvercel&stores=%5B%7B%22type%22%3A%22integration%22%2C%22protocol%22%3A%22storage%22%2C%22integrationSlug%22%3A%22neon%22%2C%22productSlug%22%3A%22neon%22%7D%2C%7B%22type%22%3A%22integration%22%2C%22protocol%22%3A%22storage%22%2C%22integrationSlug%22%3A%22upstash%22%2C%22productSlug%22%3A%22upstash-kv%22%7D%2C%7B%22type%22%3A%22blob%22%2C%22access%22%3A%22private%22%7D%5D) Vercel provisions Neon PostgreSQL, private Blob storage, and Upstash Redis through its deployment wizard. Supply two persistent secrets and use the **Services** framework preset. Static assets run in the frontend service, and Hono serves the application routes and APIs from the backend service. See the [Vercel guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/vercel) for setup, limits, and optional SMTP/OAuth configuration. ### Cloudflare Workers Cloudflare deployment requires **Workers Paid** and uses Static Assets, private R2 storage, SQLite Durable Objects, and PostgreSQL through Hyperdrive. Supply an existing PostgreSQL database and apply migrations before deployment. See the [Cloudflare guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/cloudflare) for setup and runtime limits. ### Docker and Kubernetes The application needs: - **PostgreSQL** — Accounts, documents, applications, and assistant conversations - **Upload storage** — A persistent local directory or an S3-compatible bucket, such as SeaweedFS - **Redis** (optional) — Shared coordination across instances and resumable assistant replies - **SMTP** (optional) — Verification and password-reset emails Published releases are available from Docker Hub and GitHub Container Registry (`latest` tracks the latest stable release): ```bash # Docker Hub docker pull amruthpillai/reactive-resume:latest # GitHub Container Registry docker pull ghcr.io/reactive-resume/reactive-resume:latest ``` See the [Docker guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker) or [Kubernetes guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/kubernetes) for complete instructions. Running on a NAS? See the [Synology and UGREEN guides](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/nas). ### Configuration Every setting is listed in the [environment variables reference](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/environment-variables). Self-hosters can also configure [shared AI and job-search services](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/job-search-and-ai) and [single sign-on](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/sso). ### Upgrading from v5 Back up your database and uploads and stop all v5 instances before applying v6 migrations. evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-inner-browser-use

A Chrome that the agent owns, mirrored into the right column of DeepSeek Harness.

The agent opens pages, reads them, clicks, types and scrolls. The browser is a separate
Chrome with its own profile on disk, not the tab the product ships: the column shows a
live picture of that browser, and your own cursor keeps working on the picture.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `browser_open` | Starts the browser (or reuses the running one) and opens an address. `headless: false` shows a real window on the desktop instead. |
| `browser_view` | Returns the address, the title, every control as `1 … 120`, and the visible text. |
| `browser_read` | Reads the page the way a person does: one Markdown block of headings, paragraphs, lists and links, no controls. Far fewer tokens than a snapshot on long pages, and the links stay usable. Give it a `query` and only the sentences that answer it come back: BM25 over Readability-style blocks, then per-sentence scoring with heading, position and link-density priors, idf-weighted coverage, MMR de-duplication and a character budget — 92% fewer tokens on a long page in the bench. A question the page cannot answer returns the nearest passages and says so instead of pasting the page (79% fewer tokens in the bench). When the tab has no answer, the other tabs this chat holds are read in the same call and the answer comes back with the tab it came from — one read instead of switch-and-read-again (90% fewer characters in the bench); `across: false` stays on this tab. |
| `browser_find` | Finds words (or a regex) anywhere on the page: matching controls come back with a clickable number, matching text with its point, each saying whether it is on screen. |
| `browser_extract` | Returns the items a CSS selector matches, one compact line each with its link, instead of the whole page. |
| `browser_click` | Clicks a numbered control, or an `x`/`y` point. `double: true` double-clicks. A cookie banner or modal over the control is cleared first, then the click happens. |
| `browser_type` | Types text into the focused field, or clicks a numbered control first. Chinese goes in as one string. `submit: true` presses Enter. |
| `browser_key` | Presses one key: Enter, Tab, Escape, Backspace, Delete, Insert, arrows, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, F1-F12, the numeric keypad, letters, digits, punctuation and every shifted symbol, plus ContextMenu, CapsLock, PrintScreen and media keys. `Ctrl`/`Alt`/`Shift`/`Meta`/`Mod` modifiers, chords with `+`, and `Ctrl+C/X/V/A/Z/Y` run the real editing commands. |
| `browser_scroll` | Scrolls the wheel at the centre of the page, or at `x`/`y`. `dy: 600` is about a screen down. |
| `browser_shot` | Saves a full-size PNG into `~/.dsh-inner-browser-use/screenshots` and returns the path. |
| `browser_look` | Looks at a page that draws itself — a game, a canvas, a Flash movie — and returns it as a grid of letters, one per block of screen, the same letter for the same colour: 12×8 costs about 200 characters, so a picture costs no image tokens. A second look reports only the cells that changed. `browser_shot` is still the tool for colour, layout and anything a person should see. |
| `browser_media` | Lists the video and sound the page already fetched, with sizes, the one its own player shows first and marked `main`; `save: <row>`, `save: main` or part of the address keeps one. Ads and beacons stay out unless `all: true`; `watch: false` stops remembering the page. A stream is followed to its pieces and joined, so nothing has to be installed. |
| `browser_login` | Keeps a sign-in by name: `save` stores this window's cookies and each site's local storage, `list` shows what is kept, `use` signs that account back in and reopens the page, `import` takes a sign-in that is already in Chrome, Brave, Edge or Chromium on this Mac and keeps it under a name, `drop` forgets it. Names survive a restart and belong to the browser rather than to one chat, so two accounts on one site are two names. What sits on disk is encrypted, with the key in the system keychain. |
| `browser_state` | Reports whether the browser runs, which profile it uses, its address and title, how many columns are showing it, how much memory it holds right now and when it would close on its own if left alone. |

A site you read twice is remembered by origin in `~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/sites.json` (override with `DSH_INNER_BROWSER_STATE_DIR`). After two reads, a site whose page text or control count is big opens in `browser_view` as a `map:` of what is there, and a site whose articles are long has `browser_read` cut at 3,500 characters with a line saying so. Both come with one sentence naming the measurement, and both yield to an explicit `mode`, `query` or `max_chars` — learning changes the default, not the answer to a direct question. `scripts/check-sites.mjs` is the live proof: three views of a 300-button page and three reads of a 12,000-character document, saying where the cut fell.

`browser_read` on the same page is the words only, in Markdown (measured: 4,520
characters of an about page against 2,987 characters of snapshot — and the
snapshot spends most of its budget on controls; on a long article the gap grows
with the number of controls skipped). `browser_view` answers with one page of text:

```
https://example.com
Example Domain

1 [a] More information
7 [input] Search
```

Numbers stay valid until the next read. Anything that changes the page returns a fresh read.

## The column

The pane is a picture of the browser, sent as JPEG over the session's own stream: quality 72,
every frame, about 82 KB and 25 per second on a page at rest. The page is laid out at the size
of the column, so the picture fills the frame instead of sitting letterboxed inside it.

Two pointers live on that picture:

- **The black arrow** is the agent. It marks where its last click landed, and it moves the
  moment a new one is dispatched, without waiting for the page to repaint.
- **Your cursor** is the real one. Hovering, clicking, the wheel and keystrokes are sent to
  the browser as real mouse and keyboard input, so a site that rejects scripted clicks still
  works. Moving your mouse never moves the black arrow.

The address row above the picture is an address bar: type an address and press Enter, or use
back, forward and reload. The field follows the page except while you are editing it.

Typing arrives two ways: composed text (Chinese, emoji, anything the input method produces)
lands as one insertion, and keys arrive as themselves, so Backspace deletes one character on
the page.

The pane opens only in the session that asked for it. A tool call in another session drives
the same browser without taking the column that someone else is reading.

## Logins

The profile is a directory of its own: `~/.dsh/inner-browser-use/chrome/default`. It sits
outside the product's browser storage, which is created per process and gone on restart, so a
sign-in here is still there the next day.

- **Plugin reload.** A reload adopts the Chrome that is still running, with the page it was on.
- **Harness restart.** The same directory is opened again, so cookies, `localStorage` and
  passwords that Chrome saved all survive.
- **Shutdown.** The browser is asked to close rather than killed, which is when Chrome writes
  the last of its cookies.

## What it costs

Measured on the same machine with the same harness as Playwright MCP and Chrome
DevTools MCP: idle RSS **551 MB** (1414 / 1280), idle CPU **0.03–0.32%**
(38.1% / 36.3%), and a wake in **0.82–0.85 s** instead of a 4.6–5.1 s restart.
With six tabs open it is **876 MB**, about +2 MB per tab, still four renderer
processes and 1.36 % of a core idle. `npm run bench` and `npm run tabs`
reproduce both.

## When nobody is looking

A browser used every two seconds rests after two minutes; one used every ninety seconds waits
nine. The window is p95 of the person's own last 64 gaps, × 6 for rest and × 2 for a reversible
pause, so it is learned rather than configured. Close the column and the rest is one minute
away; leave it open and the page is frozen instead (DOM, scroll and sign-ins kept, screenshot
stream stopped). A wake is 0.3–1.1 s and lands on the same address. `npm run rest` checks the
whole chain headlessly; `docs/RESOURCES.md` has the memory ladder and how the neighbours do it.

Screenshots are the only thing written outside the profile:
`~/.dsh-inner-browser-use/screenshots/`.

## Measured

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Navigate to first frame | ~850 ms, network included |
| Frame | 1440×900 JPEG, ~82 KB |
| Stream | ~25 frames per second |
| Pointer move to arrow | 0.8–7 ms |
| Read, dense page | 444 tokens (1510 chars, 90 controls) |
| Read round trip | 1–4 ms |
| Click round trip | 2 ms |
| Key round trip | 7 ms |
| Key to next frame | 15–18 ms |
| Screenshot | 75 ms, 115 KB |

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/regrevia/dsh-inner-browser-use
dsh plugin install /path/to/dsh-inner-browser-use
```

In the app: **Plugins → Install from folder**, and pick the clone. To install the packed
tarball instead, build it from that directory and install the file:

```bash
npm pack                                  # writes dsh-inner-browser-use-0.16.0.tgz
dsh plugin install ./dsh-inner-browser-use-0.16.0.tgz
```

The plugin appears under **Plugins** as *Background browser*. It needs Google Chrome or
Chromium on the machine; see [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md).

## When it opens

Only when the person asks for it by name: "in the browser", "on the web page",
"open this site", "click it for me". A link on its own is not a request.

- A public article, one link's text, docs, a GitHub repo or PR: read it with
  `web_fetch` or Envoy. No browser, no Chrome process.
- If the page needs a login, is an empty shell to `web_fetch`, or needs a click,
  say why and ask once instead of starting a browser on your own.
- Asked for, it starts without a question and never opens a second, external
  Chrome. The picture stays in this chat's right column and stays open when the
  work is done.

One browser is shared by every chat (see [Sharing](#sharing)), so opening one is
a tab, not a second Chrome.

## Use

1. Open the chat you want the agent to browse for.
2. Ask for something on a page: *"open example.com and tell me the title"*.

The first call starts the browser and puts its mirror in this chat's right column. Nothing
opens before a call: a chat that never asked for a page keeps its column as it was.

## Sharing

Every chat uses the same background Chrome: one process, one tab per chat, and
each tab's address saved so it can be closed and reopened cheaply. Past six
chats the oldest tab nobody is watching is closed (a watched tab — the one on
someone's screen — never is). Tabs an earlier plugin load left behind are closed
on first use: one profile used for weeks otherwise keeps a renderer per chat that
ever opened it. Nothing is launched per chat, and the browser itself is closed 15
minutes after the last mirror is detached.

## Frames, downloads, network

- **Frames are read, including cross-site ones.** Controls inside an iframe are numbered like
  the page's own, whether Chrome shares the page's process or runs the frame apart; a click in
  either lands where the frame actually sits.
- **A download lands on disk.** A click that saves a file writes it into the browser's own
  profile folder, and `browser_downloads` names it, its size and when it arrived.
- **The network is visible.** `browser_network` lists what the page asked for, newest first,
  so a page that fills itself in from an address can be understood without a screenshot.
- **An overlay does not eat the action.** A cookie banner over the button is cleared the way a
  person would clear it, then the click lands — in the same call, and in every step of a
  `browser_do` batch. Anything offering to delete, pay or sign out is reported instead.

## What it does not do

- **It does not touch your Chrome.** The browser runs from a separate profile with no
  connection to the window you are using.
- **The layout viewport is the column, nothing more.** Desktop layout, no mobile emulation, no
touch emulation; a very narrow column is laid out narrow rather than zoomed out.
- **One page at a time.** A link that opens a tab is followed — the mirror lands on the new
  page and the popup closes — so there is never a second page to choose between.

## Compatibility

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Harness | 0.2.0 or newer |
| Chrome | Google Chrome, Chromium or Canary, 112 or newer |
| Runtime | Node 20 or newer |
| License | MIT |

Details in [docs/COMPATIBILITY.md](docs/COMPATIBILITY.md); how the halves connect in
[docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Development

```bash
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

The server half is zero-dependency ESM, the page half is a client module loaded at runtime.
Neither has a build step.

## License

MIT © regrevia

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# deepseek-bot — 类人社交认知 Bot

把 DeepSeek Harness（`dsh`）接入 QQ 的最小可用骨架：QQ 侧走 **OneBot v11**（NapCat / LLOneBot / Lagrange），
当前线上入口是 **Aurabot 模块 + OneBot 11**；`brain/` 是独立认知内核，
不绑定某个 QQ 框架，另有通用 OneBot 11 适配器。

```
QQ 客户端 ──▶ NapCat(QQUID 登录) ──OneBot v11 WS──▶ bridge.mjs ──ACP(stdio JSON-RPC)──▶ dsh --profile acp ──▶ 模型/工具
```

## 为什么用 ACP，而不是别的方式

| 方案 | 形态 | 适合场景 | 主要缺点 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dsh --profile headless "任务"` | 一次性子进程，stdout 出最终答案 | 定时任务、一次性问答 | 每条消息冷启动 2~5s，靠 `--session-id` 续聊，无流式 |
| **`dsh --profile acp`** | 常驻子进程 + JSON-RPC stdio，多 session | **IM 机器人（本方案）** | 需要自己实现 ACP 客户端（已完成） |
| `dsh --profile sdk` | 常驻，dsh 自家 SDK JSON-RPC | 深度嵌入、要拿到内部事件 | 协议未公开成文档，版本变动风险 |
| `dsh web` | HTTP + 浏览器 UI | 人工使用、远程共享 | 面向浏览器信任模型，不适合机器人直接调用 |

ACP 是 dsh 官方支持的标准协议（`dsh --profile acp` 的 `--help` 明确写 "Serve automation clients over Agent Client Protocol stdio"），
协议稳定、跨 agent 通用，Zed 等编辑器也用它。

## 目录

```
src/acp-client.mjs   ACP v1 客户端（NDJSON JSON-RPC，含权限请求回执、超时、子进程生命周期）
src/bridge.mjs       OneBot v11 WS 接入、@ 判定、会话映射、串行队列、并发限流、消息分片
.env.example         全部配置项
```

## 多模态与上下文

- 眼睛：`brain/plugins/vision-eye.mjs` 本地 OCR，写 `media_insights` 与情景记忆
- 四肢：`brain/plugins/limbs.mjs` + `brain/src/core/actions.mjs`，受控发文本/图片/文件/撤回/戳
- 上下文：`brain/src/context/assembler.mjs`，旧对话抽取式压缩到 `context_summaries`
- 数据：全部落在 `<projectRoot>/data/`，路径由项目配置或环境变量决定

## 快速开始

### 1. QQ 接入层：NapCat

1. 用 NapCat 登录一个 QQ 号（建议小号，注意风控）。
2. 在网络配置里开启 **WebSocket 服务端**（正向 WS），例如 `ws://0.0.0.0:3001`，按需设置 `access_token`。
3. 也可用 `LLOneBot`（LiteLoaderQQNT 插件）或 `Lagrange.OneBot`，协议同为 OneBot v11。

### 2. 跑桥接

```bash
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cp .env.example .env
# 编辑 .env：ONEBOT_WS / ONEBOT_TOKEN / ALLOWED_GROUPS / ALLOWED_USERS / 模型
npm start
```

首次启动应看到：

```
桥接启动，工作目录根: .../workspaces，最大并发: 2
OneBot 已连接 ws://127.0.0.1:3001
机器人 QQ: 123456789
```

群里 @机器人 说话（或私聊）即可；`/reset` 重开 session，`/stop` 中断当前回合。

### 3. 模型配置

ACP 的模型是一个 `config option`，值形如 `["provider","model"]`，可在会话创建后动态切换：

```bash
# 走 dsh 已登录账号（凭据在 ~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml），兼容 web 端登录态
DSH_MODEL='["deepseek-account","deepseek-flash"]'

# 走官方 API Key 路由
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-...   DSH_MODEL='["deepseek-official","deepseek-v4-flash"]'
```

可选模型由 `session/new` 返回的 `configOptions[0].options` 决定（当前：`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`、`DeepSeek-V4-Pro`，
以及 reasoning_effort：off/low/high/max）。

## 协议细节（已实测）

```
→ initialize           {"protocolVersion":1,...}      ← {"agentInfo":{"name":"deepseek-harness-acp"},...}
→ session/new          {"cwd":"...","mcpServers":[]}  ← {"sessionId":"...","configOptions":[...]}
→ session/set_config_option {"configId":"model","value":"[\"deepseek-account\",\"deepseek-flash\"]"}
→ session/prompt       {"sessionId":"...","prompt":[{"type":"text","text":"..."}]}

这是「把项目能力挂进 DSH」的第一步，不是替代 Aurabot。

- 只读：查询认知状态、上下文摘要、图片 OCR、最近决策、元认知校准
- 不发送 QQ、不改状态

## 版本

0.2.0：6 个只读工具，时间线包含决策/演化/情绪/记忆。

## 工具

- `dsh_bot_status`：插件/记忆/媒体/摘要/策略观察数
- `dsh_bot_context`：某会话摘要、最近消息、多模态观察
- `dsh_bot_why`：最近决策的候选、效用、特征、原因
- `dsh_bot_impressions`：人物印象
- `dsh_bot_timeline`：近期事件时间线
- `dsh_bot_calibration`：Brier/准确率/平均把握度
- `dsh_bot_learning`：未知缺口、学习任务、知识声明
- `dsh_bot_emotion`：当前 PAD、近期情绪事件与日终趋势
- `dsh_bot_relationships`：多维关系状态
- 项目路径从插件配置 `projectRoot` 或 `DSH_BOT_ROOT` 读取

## 本地安装（未自动执行）

```bash
# 在 DSH profile 的 package.json 里加入本地依赖
pnpm --dir "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web" add file:/workspace/workapps/dsh-bot/dsh-plugin
```

然后在 profile 的 patch 列表里挂 `dsh-bot-cognition`，或把 `cordis.patch.yml` 合并进 profile。

没有安装前，Aurabot 模块和 brain 内核照常运行。

## 安装验证

已在一个临时 profile 中真实安装、组合并导入成功；web profile 也已安装，当前运行中的 DSH 未重启，待下次重启激活。详见 [DSH-INSTALL.md](../docs/DSH-INSTALL.md)。

# deepseek-bot — 类人社交认知 Bot

把 DeepSeek Harness（`dsh`）接入 QQ 的最小可用骨架：QQ 侧走 **OneBot v11**（NapCat / LLOneBot / Lagrange），
当前线上入口是 **Aurabot 模块 + OneBot 11**；`brain/` 是独立认知内核，
不绑定某个 QQ 框架，另有通用 OneBot 11 适配器。

```
QQ 客户端 ──▶ NapCat(QQUID 登录) ──OneBot v11 WS──▶ bridge.mjs ──ACP(stdio JSON-RPC)──▶ dsh --profile acp ──▶ 模型/工具
```

## 为什么用 ACP，而不是别的方式

| 方案 | 形态 | 适合场景 | 主要缺点 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dsh --profile headless "任务"` | 一次性子进程，stdout 出最终答案 | 定时任务、一次性问答 | 每条消息冷启动 2~5s，靠 `--session-id` 续聊，无流式 |
| **`dsh --profile acp`** | 常驻子进程 + JSON-RPC stdio，多 session | **IM 机器人（本方案）** | 需要自己实现 ACP 客户端（已完成） |
| `dsh --profile sdk` | 常驻，dsh 自家 SDK JSON-RPC | 深度嵌入、要拿到内部事件 | 协议未公开成文档，版本变动风险 |
| `dsh web` | HTTP + 浏览器 UI | 人工使用、远程共享 | 面向浏览器信任模型，不适合机器人直接调用 |

ACP 是 dsh 官方支持的标准协议（`dsh --profile acp` 的 `--help` 明确写 "Serve automation clients over Agent Client Protocol stdio"），
协议稳定、跨 agent 通用，Zed 等编辑器也用它。

## 目录

```
src/acp-client.mjs   ACP v1 客户端（NDJSON JSON-RPC，含权限请求回执、超时、子进程生命周期）
src/bridge.mjs       OneBot v11 WS 接入、@ 判定、会话映射、串行队列、并发限流、消息分片
.env.example         全部配置项
```

## 多模态与上下文

- 眼睛：`brain/plugins/vision-eye.mjs` 本地 OCR，写 `media_insights` 与情景记忆
- 四肢：`brain/plugins/limbs.mjs` + `brain/src/core/actions.mjs`，受控发文本/图片/文件/撤回/戳
- 上下文：`brain/src/context/assembler.mjs`，旧对话抽取式压缩到 `context_summaries`

1. 用 NapCat 登录一个 QQ 号（建议小号，注意风控）。
2. 在网络配置里开启 **WebSocket 服务端**（正向 WS），例如 `ws://0.0.0.0:3001`，按需设置 `access_token`。
3. 也可用 `LLOneBot`（LiteLoaderQQNT 插件）或 `Lagrange.OneBot`，协议同为 OneBot v11。

### 2. 跑桥接

cp .env.example .env
# 编辑 .env：ONEBOT_WS / ONEBOT_TOKEN / ALLOWED_GROUPS / ALLOWED_USERS / 模型

OneBot 已连接 ws://127.0.0.1:3001
机器人 QQ: 123456789
