`ui-settled`, one this bridge never claimed answers `ui-unknown`, and a payload over 8 KiB answers `invalid-args` | | `ui.list` | `{}` | `{cards:[{key, sessionId, state, payload}], complete:true}` — only the cards still held; `key` is `"<sessionId>/<callId>"` and `payload` is that card's `ui.request` payload verbatim, and the read claims nothing, moves no deadline and settles nothing | `hello` is callable without a device token and reports the connection's own `auth` state. `session.snapshot` maps the harness follow stream's opening snapshot into `turns`, reports its cursor as `lastSeq` and then keeps that stream open as this connection's subscription for the session; `session.prompt` ensures the same subscription idempotently, so a client may skip the snapshot. The prompt mode is fixed to queue, `clientTimeZone` is filled server-side with the host's IANA zone, and `requestId` is an idempotency key: the same `requestId` in the same session is sent once, and a repeat answers `{accepted:true}` without sending anything again. `session.interrupt` cancels the turn; it does not drop the subscription. The two agent methods interpret nothing. `presets.list` answers the host's `agentPresets/list` body as it arrived — that endpoint takes no request, so a preset row is whatever the registry publishes, its plugin list included — and `session.create` sends the client's payload as that endpoint's single `request` argument and answers the host's own reply. The field names, the defaults and the refusal codes are the host's: a client validates a creation request against the host's own `SessionCreateRequest`, never against a copy kept here, and a rejection reaches it as the host's `code` and `msg` — an uncoded failure crosses as this bridge's `internal`, with the host's text. Both methods exist only for a client that declared `agents.v1`: without it each answers `unknown-method` and nothing is sent, and a connection that declared it and never calls them costs the host no read at all. The fork method interprets nothing either. `session.fork` sends `sessionId` and, only when the client named one, `atSeq` — the source event seq the fork includes — as that endpoint's single `request` argument, and answers the host's own `SessionForkValue`. An omitted `atSeq` stays omitted: the host reads an absent fork point as its newest finished turn, and inventing one here would move the cut silently. A cut that is not a positive integer is refused here as `invalid-args`, because no event log has such a seq; what the host refuses crosses with the host's own `code` and `msg`, and an uncoded failure as this bridge's `internal`. The method exists only for a client that declared `session.fork.v1`: without it the answer is `unknown-method` and the host is asked nothing. The command channel interprets nothing either. `session.commands` reads both host catalogs for one session and folds them into one directory: `commands/list` is the registry's effective view for that Agent — a command registered through an Agent-scoped child shadows the global one — and `skills/list` is the catalog that session's cwd and preset select, so a phone lists what the desktop composer would offer that same session. Every command comes first and every skill after, each in the host's own order, and no list is re-sorted, de-duplicated or paged. A row is `{name, description, kind, line}`, where `kind` is `command` or `skill` and `line` is the whole draft text that invokes it, separator space included — both host surfaces resolve a bare gesture only when whitespace or the end of the text follows the name, and a skill gesture is `/(^|\s)\/([a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*)(?=\s|$)/`. That last rule is also why a skill line is not a command line: a skill is never registered with the command registry, so running one through `session.command` answers `matched: false` and nothing runs. `session.command` sends the line to `commands/execute` exactly as the client wrote it, with an empty attachment list, and answers one decided fact: whether the host resolved the line at all. A line the host resolves runs and answers `matched: true`; a line it resolves to nothing — no leading slash, an unknown name, or a skill's gesture — answers `matched: false` and nothing runs. Nothing is cached and nothing is pushed: both methods read the host on every call, hold no event, and a client that never declared `commands.v1` is answered `unknown-method` with no registry read and no catalog read on its behalf. A host that exports neither endpoint answers this bridge's own `commands-unavailable` rather than a failure per call, while a call the host refuses, and a service that is merely still activating, cross with the failure's own code and text. The session-admin channel interprets nothing either, and it is two capabilities because reading and writing are two different offers. `workspace.list` answers the host registry's own synchronous projection — one row per registered workspace in registry order, never sorted here, never carrying the workspace's session account — with the archive and pin sets beside it; an archived session is a session-level fact, not an archived workspace, so nothing is filtered out of that list and an archived session keeps its slot, which is where `session.unarchive` puts it back. Pinning is a registry-global set rather than an order inside a workspace: a new pin is prepended, a repeated pin neither writes nor reorders, a pin on an archived session is refused by the host, and archiving drops the pin in the same durable write — the visible order a client shows is therefore its own derivation, exactly as the desktop derives it. Five writes then map one-to-one onto the endpoints that already own their semantics: `session.rename` reaches `session/rename`, which restores a cold session before it writes and answers the title it normalized with the seq that committed it, so a client needs no resume path of its own; `session.pin`, `session.unpin`, `session.archive` and `session.unarchive` reach `workspace/pinSession`, `workspace/unpinSession`, `workspace/archiveSession` and `workspace/unarchiveSession`. No boolean is invented and nothing is branched here: `stopActivity` crosses only when the client sent a boolean, and a session that is still running without it is refused by the host as `workspace/session-active`, which is the refusal that tells a phone to offer the confirmation. This channel pushes no event, because the host announces none of these writes as a cordis event a connection could fold into a delta — a rename appends one `session/title` record and nothing else — so a client re-reads after every write: the pin set through `workspace.list`, the roster through `session.list`, and the new name into its own copy while the title cache expires. The cost is stated rather than hidden: a pin or an archive made on the desktop reaches the phone at its next refresh. A connection that never declared `workspace.v1` or `session.admin.v1` is answered `unknown-method` for the methods behind it, with no registry read and no write on its behalf. The squads channel is the one that replaces nothing: it reads and drives the agent squads of the `dsh-agents` plugin, and it sits beside `agents.v1` rather than on top of it, so a phone written before it keeps the preset roster and session creation it was built against. Five commands stand behind `squads.v1`. `squads.state` answers `{squads, runs, presets?, host:{ownerPid?}}`; `squads.list` answers `{squads}` and `squads.runs` answers `{runs}`, the two halves of one read cut from the same answer, so a squad listing and a run history can never disagree; `squads.runMember` sends `{squadId, memberId, firstMessage?}` and `squads.runSquad` sends `{squadId, goal?}`, each answering `{run}`. A `Squad` is `{id, name, description?, workspaceId?, leadPreset?, order?, members:[Member]}` and a `Member` is `{id, name, preset?, permission?, model?, reasoningEffort?, brief?}`; a `Run` is `{id, squadId, kind:'squad'|'member', memberId?, sessionId, createdAt, status:'running'|'settled'|'failed', failure?}`, where `kind` is required on this wire and a run recorded before whole-squad runs existed — one carrying no `kind` at all — reads as the member run it is by construction. Nothing the plugin keeps for itself crosses: a definition's `createdAt`/`updatedAt`, a member's `teamId` backlink and the `goal` handed to a Lead stay on the host's side. The domain is the plugin's own, so its refusals are the plugin's own too and cross with the plugin's code and its one bounded sentence — `team-not-found`, `member-not-found`, `preset-registry-unavailable`, `preset-unknown`, `preset-unavailable`, `workspace-unavailable`, `workspace-unknown`, `model-pin-invalid`, `session-create-failed` and their neighbours — while this bridge names only the two conditions the plugin cannot: `squads-unavailable`, for a host that serves no squad domain this bridge can reach or answers a body this build cannot read, and `squads-run-unavailable`, for definitions that are readable while no run route can be reached, which is answered instead of a run that never started. A malformed row is refused rather than repaired and an empty answer is never invented, so a host without the plugin answers an error rather than an empty board. How the domain is reached is this bridge's one dependency-free rule: the plugin's own routes over this machine's loopback origin — `GET /dsh-agents/api/state`, `POST /dsh-agents/api/run`, `POST /dsh-agents/api/squad/run`, addressed at the origin `webServer` already serves and carrying that origin in the `origin` header the plugin's browser fence reads as its same-origin signal — and, when no loopback call can connect at all, the plugin's ledger at `$DSH_HOME/dsh-agents/ledger.json` read read-only under the same rules, with `host.ownerPid` then read out of the plugin's own lock beside it. An answer of any status is not a fallback: it is the plugin speaking, and only a call that never connected reaches the ledger. Nothing is called on a connection's behalf, and a client that never declared `squads.v1` is answered `unknown-method` for all five. The usage channel reads two facts that belong to the host rather than to one device, so one instance serves every connection. `usage.session` names one session and answers `{contextWindow?, composition?}`: the window is the harness's own `RequestContext.contextWindow` from the latest `request/context` event this process saw broadcast, and the composition is this bridge's estimate of what the next request is made of, split three ways — `tools` from the raw tools schema of the latest `request/header`, `system` from the latest `system/message` text, and `messages` from the text of every `user/message`, `assistant/message` and `tool/result` seen since — each component the UTF-8 byte count divided by four and floored, always carrying `estimated: true`, because a phone must never read an estimate as the host's own accounting. A key the host never broadcast is absent rather than zero, and a session that exists while neither reading does answers `{}`: existence has three witnesses — the host's own session roster (the same `session/list` the roster method serves, so a session this bridge never observed and that is not live still counts), the live session store, and the events this process folded — and a session id none of the three names is refused `unknown-session`. The roster is read only when the other two answer nothing, and its answer is reused for five seconds so a burst of opens costs one read; a bridge that cannot read a roster at all falls back to the live store and the fold alone. The fold starts when this row mounts and never reads a session log: an event broadcast before it mounted is not a reading, so a session that ran entirely before it answers `{}` rather than a composition of zeros. `usage.balance` names one provider route and answers either `{provider, currency, total, toppedUp, granted, updatedAt}` — the numbers in yuan, taken from `balance_infos[0]` — or `{provider, unsupported, reason?}` with `no-credential`, `not-deepseek-route` or `probe-failed`. The route must be an official DeepSeek id (`deepseek` or `deepseek-official`) AND its configured `baseURL` absent or on `https://api.deepseek.com`: the balance endpoint reports one origin's account, so probing it for a reseller profile that merely reused the `deepseek` id would print the official account's money under that route's name. The credential is resolved the way the harness's own usage plugin resolves it — the pi-ai record `llm-pi-ai/<provider>`, then the profile's `apiKeyEnv`, then the DeepSeek adapter's own reference (default `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) — and an OAuth grant is not a credential here, because the official endpoint accepts an API key only. One reading is cached for 60 seconds per provider and credential, concurrent calls merge into one upstream request, and 401, a timeout or an unrecognized body all answer `probe-failed` instead of a previous reading presented as current. A client that never declared `usage.v1` is answered `unknown-method` for both methods, with no event folded and no upstream request made on its behalf. `usage.stats` reads the ledger another plugin keeps, so it is its own capability behind `usage.stats.v1` and its own read path: one `GET /api/dsh-usage/overview` and, only when the requested window reaches deeper than the 30 days that document already carries, one `GET /api/dsh-usage/day?date=YYYY-MM-DD` per day that ledger actually recorded. Days the ledger holds nothing for cross as real zeros — the host answers those dates as zeroed days itself — while a route that is absent (`no-usage-plugin`), unreachable, shaped differently or too slow answers `probe-failed` with a short reason and never a previous reading. One `days` window is cached for 30 seconds on this side and concurrent calls merge into it, so two phones asking at once cost the host one read. `usage.session` gained one optional key beside the window: when the host has broadcast no `request/context` window, the answer may carry `modelContextWindow`, taken from `GET {baseURL}/models` of the session's current route — the first available of `context_length`, `context_window` and `max_input_tokens` for that exact model id, cached for ten minutes per route, and sent with that route's own credential. The two numbers are never mixed: `contextWindow` is always the host's measurement, `modelContextWindow` is always the model's declaration, and the second never appears beside the first. `hello` also carries the client's capabilities, and a capability is an announcement rather than a negotiation: the handshake answers the same frame whatever `cap` holds, an unknown name is ignored, and the frame cap is one constant in both directions — the 10 MiB that bounds a received frame is the same budget that fits a snapshot and that drops an oversized outbound event. This bridge serves twenty-three capabilities and advertises them in `hello`'s `capabilities`: `session.snapshot.trim.v1`, `session.snapshot.page.v1`, `questions.v1`, `questions.list.v1`, `subagent.thread.v1`, `jobs.v1`, `agents.v1`, `delta.v1`, `session.list.omit-archived.v1`, `session.deep-history.v1`, `frame.deflate.v1`, `session.list.compact.v1`, `session.snapshot.since.v1`, `session.fork.v1`, `commands.v1`, `workspace.v1`, `session.admin.v1`, `squads.v1`, `push.v1`, `usage.v1`, `usage.stats.v1`, `ui.v1` and `ui.list.v1` — a capability a mounted plugin adds is not on that list, because the bridge is not its author. `ui.v1` is the one name here that a bridge can only advertise when it really serves the other half: behind it a page arrives as `ui.request` and the user's action returns with `ui.event`, and a host whose bridge predates the channel sends nothing. `ui.list.v1` is its reconciliation read, the same announcement shape as `questions.list.v1`: only an answer marked `complete` may retire a card a phone carries. Nor is `approvals.v1`, which a client declares and this bridge deliberately never advertises: it gates a replay rather than the channel, so the handshake stays the same frame for every client (see the approval channel below). `questions.list.v1` is the one name here that announces a method rather than changing a channel: `question.list` answers the questions this bridge is still holding, and only an answer marked `complete` may retire a card a phone carries. The first is the trimmed baseline. A client that does not declare it — including every client written before it existed — is served exactly the baseline protocol v1 always served. A client that does declare it is sent a trimmed baseline: inside every turn, only the entries it renders (`user/message`, `assistant/message`, `tool/call`, `tool/result`, `subagent/catalog`) survive, and the harness's own bookkeeping records (`system/message`, `request/header` and the like) are dropped before the frame is measured. Nothing else about the snapshot changes: which turns are kept, their order, and each turn's `seq`, `endSeq`, `reason` and `time` are the projection's own values, a turn whose entries are all bookkeeping stays as a turn with an empty `entries` array, and `lastSeq` is still the harness cursor. The frame budget applies afterwards — entries are trimmed first, then whole oldest turns are dropped, and only then does a snapshot that still does not fit answer `snapshot-too-large`. A second capability bounds the opening screen itself: `session.snapshot.page.v1`. Without it a snapshot stays the whole opening window, byte for byte, exactly as before. With it, `session.snapshot` answers with the newest page only, measured against `maxBytes` (default 524288 = 512 KiB, and refused rather than clamped when it is not a usable budget), cut by the very same entry-level slice `session.history` uses: a turn's entries may split between this page and the next one while that turn keeps its own fields, an entry larger than the whole budget is a page of its own, and `snapshot-too-large` can no longer answer such a connection. The budget is measured on the whole encoded answer and never per turn, so what it bounds is the page rather than an entry: a page is inside `maxBytes` unless the newest entry alone is past it, and then the page is exactly as large as that entry — a 2.2 MB newest message answers a 2.2 MB page against the 512 KiB default, while a window of ordinary entries answers 513794 bytes. That is the one cost a paged snapshot can still carry. The page carries `lastSeq` and `hasMore`, and the cursor for the next, older page is the `seq` of its own oldest entry — the same value `session.history` takes as `before`, which is why no `nextBefore` field restates it. Opening a session then costs one page, and `session.history` walks the rest of the window back in the same 512 KiB pages. The capability that makes a reconnect cheap is `session.snapshot.since.v1`, and it takes two declarations to change anything: the capability in the handshake AND a `sinceSeq` in the request. A request missing either is answered byte for byte what protocol v1 answered before it existed, with no field added, so a client can adopt the name before it relies on any of it. Behind both, the client names the durable `lastSeq` of a snapshot it already holds — the harness cursor, never the connection's own event seq — and the bridge proves continuity against the current follow window: only when that window's oldest entry sits at or below `sinceSeq + 1`, or the window is empty, is the answer the increment `{turns:[...], lastSeq, mode:"since", reset:false}` carrying nothing but the entries above that watermark, each turn keeping its own `seq`, `endSeq`, `reason` and `time` exactly as the baseline presented it. An entry the client never renders still counts as an entry the window holds, so the proof is read off the untrimmed window and can only be conservative. A window that has scrolled past the watermark cannot prove the chain is unbroken, so there — and when the increment would not fit one 10 MiB fra

# dsh-remote-web-ui · Mobile & Cross-Device Remote Web Control for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) English | [中文](README.zh.md) > **Deprecation notice**: `@linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui` is deprecated in favor of [@linxin666/dsh-remote-bridge](../dsh-remote-bridge/README.md). It has been retired from the `@linxin666/dsh-web-all` aggregate bundle (where legacy profile rows mount silently as no-ops via tombstone exports and the `retiredPlugins` registry) and will be removed in the next release. Standalone installation (`dsh plugin --profile add @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui`) remains functional during this transitional period. Browser-based remote control has been replaced by the native phone app (@linxin666/dsh-remote-bridge), and this package no longer provides remote access capabilities. > > - **Capabilities migrated to `@linxin666/dsh-remote-bridge`**: Ingress stack (relay registry identity, lease control claim/release, quick and named tunnel connectors, Durable Object relay bridge connector, cloudflared lifecycle management and orphan process reaping, Cloudflare named tunnel ingress sync, LAN forwarder, host bind capability probe, and host firewall management). > - **Capabilities retired with this package**: Browser-facing remote web control (pairing cookie gate, `/api/pair` endpoints, `/remote` proxy channel, and the mobile browser touch adaptation layer). > - **Known coexistence risk**: if installed in the same profile alongside `@linxin666/dsh-remote-bridge`, do not enable relay on both plugins simultaneously (both share the same on-disk relay identity per profile; running both causes Durable Object connection contention, and mounting the bridge with `relay=false` withdraws the shared registration row and releases the lease).

   

Mobile & Cross-Device Remote Web Control for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
Instant QR Pairing · Cross-Device PC Access · Mobile Touch Gestures · Cloudflare Tunnels · Secure Device Session

> Seamless remote access for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI and desktop client sharing the **exact same interface**: pair an iPhone, Android smartphone, tablet, or another computer from the QR code next to settings. Both ends run the authentic official Web GUI — phones receive an injected portrait touch layer while remote computers enjoy the complete desktop workbench. Access is guarded by expiring pairing tokens and revocable sessions. Built-in LAN binding and optional Cloudflare quick tunnels enable effortless external access with persistent hostnames. This package is an official external plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), structured as a cordis bundle: the host half manages pairing tokens, device sessions, `/api/pair` routes, the gated `/remote` channel, and LAN binding; the browser half renders the remote access trigger, QR pairing modal, live device roster, settings card, and mobile portrait touch adaptation. ## What it does - **Entry**: a phone icon beside the settings button in both the expanded sidebar and the narrow rail; its tooltip and accessible label say "Remote access". - **Panel**: "Remote access" title, a "Pair a device" card with the status area ("Waiting for a device" + status badge), a large QR code, the pairing link with its copy button, Stop / Refresh QR actions, and the authorized-device roster (a saved device name that falls back to the User-Agent-derived label, online/offline, last active time, per-device rename and unpair, and a merge action for rows sharing one User-Agent). Credential-bearing device ids and raw User-Agent values are never rendered. Both the phone and the PC use the same time-limited link: until it expires or the QR is refreshed, that link can pair several devices, each with its own device session. - **Phone side**: scanning the QR binds the phone with a time-limited token and reloads into the **official Web GUI** — there is no second interface to drift from. While the phone is in portrait, the plugin injects a touch-adaptation layer over the running UI (see "The mobile adaptation layer" below). The accept chain is cookieless (`/pair-accept` → `/pair-app`): the plugin itself serves the official shell, so the phone needs no harness browser-auth cookie at all. A reopen service worker (https origins) then owns later navigations to `/` from history, bookmarks, or tab restore, so the phone reopens straight into the app instead of a 401 dead end (see Security model). - **PC side**: the same link opens the full desktop Web GUI on another computer over the gated `/remote` channel; unpaired PCs see a guided blocking page (with a manual pair-token input) and no workspace data behind it. - **Security**: one active token at a time (a refresh invalidates the old link; the link stays re-usable within its expiry window so a scan handed between browsers can complete pairing; it expires). 停止 revokes every paired device and the current token — the `/remote` channel cuts them off on their next request. Pairing is this plugin's access control for the `/remote` channel; the web server keeps its loopback bind, so a LAN browser reaches the app through this plugin's gated `/remote` gateway (the client moves its transport there) rather than the native `/api`, which the harness Host fence answers with 403 for a LAN authority (see Security model). Loopback (127.0.0.1) keeps using `/api` directly, and so does a page an application on this machine delivered — the desktop shell's `dsh-app://app/` or a `file:` page — because a pairing link is reachable only over the network. A paired device is a **full-control credential** (see Security model). - **LAN access toggle (runtime forwarder)**: the settings card starts a forwarder instead of touching any file. The web server keeps its loopback bind, and the forwarder listens on this machine's LAN IPv4 address at the same port, re-issuing every request — HTTP and WebSocket upgrades alike — to `127.0.0.1:`. `--host`/`--port` keep their ordinary meaning, so an explicit `dsh web --host ` still works and the forwarder then yields the port. The toggle applies while the process runs: no restart, no profile edit. When this machine has no LAN IPv4 address the forwarder stays off and the card says so. It maintains the matching host firewall rule (Windows Defender via netsh; Linux firewalld/ufw/iptables; other platforms report the firewall as unmanaged) and shows the live bind, the reachable LAN URLs, the forwarder state (`forward { listening, host, port, reason, error }`) beside the host's own `localBindHost`, and the firewall state. - **Live status**: the desktop badge flips to 已连接 in real time; an `/api` posture probe reports any host whose `/api` fence the SDK leaves open, and the auto-tunnel state appears on the panel while the tunnel is starting. - **Self-update lives next door**: the one-click family update is its own plugin (`dsh-update`, the same sidebar foot seat), so turning remote access off — or disabling this plugin — never removes the update trigger. - **Desktop foot row**: on the wide sidebar the footer-action occupants share the official Settings trigger's line instead of stacking above it, so no single control owns a full-width row; any other foot block (the usage glance card, another plugin's) keeps a full row above them, and the 56px rail keeps the shell's stacked foot. ## The mobile adaptation layer The official desktop layout already auto-collapses the sidebar below 1024px. On top of that, while the viewport is portrait + coarse pointer + narrower than 1100px the plugin injects: - a CSS sheet keyed on CSS-Modules **semantic suffixes** (`[class$="_composerSeat"]`) so the selectors survive official rebuilds that only change hashes: 44px touch targets on the collapsed rail, 16px inputs (prevents iOS focus zoom), safe-area padding for the composer, compact type for the message list and sidebar, a column layout for the settings modal, and a full-width PlanReview card; - a **draggable whale button** as the entry to the collapsed sidebar (position persisted; wired to the official `ctx.layout.toggleSidebar()`), hidden while the sidebar is expanded; - **gestures**: left-swipe collapses the sidebar, right-swipe in the conversation opens it; long-pressing a session row opens the same action menu as the desktop ellipsis; tapping a session row or anywhere outside the sidebar collapses it again; - **input behavior for touch**: Enter only inserts a newline (send goes through the send button), programmatic composer focus is suppressed (no spurious keyboards), and official tooltip bubbles are hidden because taps leave them stuck; - **mobile plugin scope**: while the layer is active, the right-hand details column and the desktop-oriented tool surfaces (SSH terminal, skill explorer, task board, git graph, pet, usage) are hidden - keyed on the L2 semantic roots (`data-dsh-plugin`), so ownership stays with the declaring plugin and class churn cannot resurrect them. These are render suppressions; the client bundles still load. Activation also closes the details panel through the official `ctx.layout.closeDetails()`. - a **manual opt-out**: `sessionStorage.dsh-remote-force-desktop = 1` disables the whole layer; landscape, desktop, and wide viewports are never touched. The paired remote desktop also runs in **host mode**: on this harness line the "configuration plane is local" behavior is a client-side branch on `connection.isLoopback`, and the channel boot script installs the transport hook (`__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost = true`) before any boot entry. Host mode is **server-granted**: the hook is installed only when the device-gated app landing (`/pair-app`) published the grant marker ahead of the boot patch, so a shell served to an unpaired browser — a fence-open deployment — never poses as the machine owner. Settings, credentials, agent presets, and deliverables therefore work on the phone exactly as on the desktop — every call still rides the gated `/remote` channel. Three control planes stay physically local: `/api/pair/*`, `/api/update/*`, and `/api/plugin-manager/*`. ## Requirements - A DSH installation whose `dsh` CLI supports profiles (`dsh --profile`, `dsh plugin`) — the profile/bundle mechanism this package rides on. - For LAN use, either flip the **局域网访问** toggle in the settings card — it listens at once on this machine's current LAN IPv4 address at the web server's port, so after a network change flip it off and on again — or start with `dsh web --host `. A wildcard `--host 0.0.0.0` works only on a host that still accepts it; DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 and later refuses it outright. With the default `127.0.0.1` bind the panel shows an explicit explanation instead of a dead QR code — unless a public base URL is configured (see "Remote access over the internet" below), which makes the QR reachable from anywhere without rebinding, after which a phone on the same network is moved off the tunnel onto the LAN origin by the landing page. The panel's mint/stop endpoints are loopback-only by design: a desktop browser opened at the LAN URL sees a "配对面板仅限本机使用" banner. - For the one-click public tunnel (`autoTunnel`), the `cloudflared` platform binary ships with the package (its postinstall downloads it; a runtime download covers installers that skip postinstall scripts). No user-side tooling, account, or domain is needed. - The same binary also powers the fixed-hostname named-tunnel mode (`tunnelToken`): the public hostname never changes, so a paired phone keeps its bookmark and its pairing cookie across restarts and never re-pairs. ## Install Install the family aggregate package `@linxin666/dsh-web-all` (all plugins and skins in one) or this plugin alone: ```sh # Recommended: install directly from npm dsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui@latest # Or from the repository (development loop) git clone https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web.git cd dsh-web pnpm install && pnpm -r build dsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)/packages/dsh-remote-web-ui ``` Restart the profile (`dsh web`), then open the phone icon in the sidebar foot. The plugin's `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the single plugin row that mounts both halves. > `github:/` installs work for a standalone repo whose package sits at the root (the `prepare` script builds `lib/` during install; pnpm ≥10 blocks that until you copy the printed key into the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `allowBuilds` and re-run). Monorepo subpackages use the `link:` form above. ## Use 1. Open the settings card (设置 → Web 插件 → 远程访问) and flip **局域网访问** on; the card shows the live bind, the forwarder state beside the host's own `localBindHost`, the firewall state, and the reachable LAN URLs, and it says why the LAN entry is off when this machine has no LAN address. The forwarder starts and stops at once, with no restart: after a network change, flip the toggle off and on again so it follows the machine's new address. 2. Start `dsh web`, click the phone icon, and the panel mints a fresh time-limited QR. 3. Scan with the phone (or open the copied link): the device pairs and boots the **official Web GUI** served cookieless by the plugin (`/pair-accept` → `/pair-app`), which reloads into `/`. When the link names the public base, the landing page also probes the advertised LAN origins (one short no-cors request to `/pair-ping` per candidate) and moves the phone to the first one that answers, remembering the decision for the session: the public page it was served from stays usable throughout, so the probe never blocks pairing, and a phone that is not on that network simply stays where it is. On a phone, the portrait adaptation layer is already active — same layout as the desktop, same live state. Later reopens from history or a bookmark go straight back into the app (https origins; see Security model). 4. **To pair a PC instead**: copy the same link and open it in a browser on the other computer. After the same round trip the full Web GUI runs there over the gated `/remote` channel; unpaired PCs see the guided blocking page and no data. One active token pairs one device; mint a fresh QR for the next device. 5. The desktop badge flips to 已连接 in real time; the device roster lists the paired devices with per-device 取消配对, and 停止 revokes everything. 6. Configure pairing lifetime, device limits, the LAN fence policy (`requirePairingForLan`), the public base URL, the auto tunnel, the stable-hostname relay, and the named-tunnel token in the same settings card. Which network the pair traverses needs no choice: the QR link names the public base and the landing page moves a same-network phone to a LAN origin by itself. If that probe ever misjudges, pin it with the patch-only `pairingSource` key (`auto` | `public` | `lan`); the card carries no control for it, so a save from the card leaves it alone. ## Remote access over the internet (tunnels) A tunnel process restart — most often a mobile network dropping and reconnecting — used to drop the public host from the pairing fence the moment the tunnel left `running`, so the address still printed in the QR code answered 403, including on the deliberately public `/api/pair/status` (issue #1547). A named tunnel's fixed hostname and a registered relay origin never change, so both now stay trusted throughout the reconnect; a quick tunnel's previous host stays trusted for a 60 s grace window, because the edge may still be delivering a connection the phone already opened, and is dropped only if the tunnel has not come back by then. ### One-click public tunnel (recommended) Set **自动公网隧道** (autoTunnel) in the settings card. The plugin runs its own Cloudflare quick tunnel (`cloudflared` ships with the package), feeds the minted public URL into the QR base and the pairing fence dynamically, and keeps the posture probe informed — a phone anywhere can pair at any time. The manual public address and the named-tunnel token below are ignored while this is on. The minted hostname is ephemeral and changes on every `dsh web` restart — the stable-hostname relay below keeps the phone's origin fixed across those restarts. A host that dies without tearing its tunnel down leaves the `cloudflared` child running, so each start reaps the child it recorded (pid plus an exactly matching command line) and never a process it did not start itself. ### Stable-hostname relay (default on; pair once across restarts) While the quick tunnel runs, the plugin additionally registers its current tunnel URL with the dsh-market relay registry and rebuilds the QR on a fixed origin — `https://.dsh-market.com` — minted once per profile and stored under `$DSH_HOME/remote-web-ui-registry/`. The hostname never changes, so the phone's bookmark and its pairing cookie keep working across `dsh web` restarts with no Cloudflare account, no dashboard, and no domain of your own. - Registration is secret-authenticated: the plugin mints a 256-bit secret next to the identity and re-syncs the mapping on every tunnel start (crash restarts included) with capped backoff. If the registry is unreachable, the QR falls back to the raw quick URL for that session and the panel says so. - A phone opening the stable origin while the instance is offline sees an explicit "instance offline — refresh in a moment, no re-pairing needed" page instead of a dead link. - Turn **固定域名中继** (relay) off in the settings card to keep the deployment entirely on the ephemeral origin; the registry row is removed at once. Trust note: relayed traffic transits the dsh-market edge (a Cloudflare Worker operated by the package author) — see Security model. - The relay control plane is additive: whenever the relay is on and the web server port is bound, the plugin claims a named-tunnel lease from `https://dsh-market.com/api/relay/claim` — the worker finds or creates the tunnel named `dsh-relay-`, writes its ingress (catch-all rule included) and an exact proxied CNAME, and hands back that instance's own tunnel token. A lease an operator flipped to the bridge transport converges nothing in the account: that claim creates no tunnel, no ingress and no CNAME, sends no Cloudflare API call at all, keeps only the hostname and the bridge grant, and answers no `tunnel` block — the bridge's data plane is the instance's own Durable Object, so there is nothing to build and nothing to count against the account's 1 000-tunnel quota. The plugin then runs a named connector on the same hostname beside the quick connector; the `mode` the control plane answers names the one the phone is served from, so neither the switch nor its rollback needs a plugin restart. A failed claim is not fatal: the quick tunnel and the origin the registry already gave the phone keep serving, and the claim retries with capped backoff (`502` carries `retryAfterMs`). Turning the toggle off only `release`s the lease (the tunnel and the DNS record stay, so re-enabling is instant); only an explicit `retire` or the 90-day idle cron recovers the source. - The bridge transport rides the same lease: the plugin dials `wss://dsh-market.com/api/relay/bridge?id=` with the lease secret in the `Authorization` header and serves every bridged request and phone WebSocket from that one socket, forwarding the public origin as `Host` and never the loopback authority it dials. It idles while the control plane answers `mode=quick`; with no connector attached the Worker falls back to the quick path inside the same request and marks the answer `x-relay-fallback: no-connector`. Because the claim is the only answer that carries the bridge grant, it does not wait for a quick tunnel: an instance served over the bridge reaches its object with `autoTunnel` off. The connector keeps its state in `$DSH_HOME/remote-web-ui-relay-bridge.json` — state, instance, endpoint, local upstream and the last dial error — so a connector that never attached is readable without the host log. ### Fixed-hostname named tunnel (bring your own domain) The relay above already fixes the phone's origin on a shared dsh-market subdomain. A Cloudflare named tunnel is the alternative for deployments that want a hostname on **their own** domain: its public hostname is permanent, so the phone's bookmark and its pairing cookie keep working across `dsh web` restarts — pair once, never again (until the session idles past `idleExpireMs`). 1. In the Cloudflare dashboard create a Tunnel and map a public hostname — e.g. `dsh.example.com` — to `http://127.0.0.1:3080` (the port `dsh web` listens on). 2. Copy the tunnel's token and paste it into **固定域名隧道令牌** (tunnelToken) in the settings card. 3. Set the same hostname as **公网地址** (publicBaseUrl). The token does not carry the hostname, so without this step the tunnel stays off and a warning names the missing piece. The plugin then runs `cloudflared tunnel run --token` with the same lifecycle management as the quick tunnel: the binary ships with the package, unexpected exits restart with backoff, a running tunnel's public URL is probed every 60 s and two consecutive failures mint a fresh tunnel through that same restart path, and the posture probe audits the `/api` fence for the fixed host. The token is stored as a settings secret and read back redacted. The auto quick tunnel takes precedence while it is on. A `running` tunnel is not a terminal state: a connector that lost its Cloudflare edge registration keeps its process and its metrics port alive while the minted hostname stops resolving, so the plugin used to report `running` indefinitely and the relay kept forwarding the phone to the dead address (Cloudflare 530 / Error 1016) instead of the relay's offline page (issue #1723). The readiness watchdog now treats a public URL that stops answering — DNS failure, refused connection, or a Cloudflare 5xx such as 530 — as a dead tunnel after two consecutive probes, and the ordinary backoff restart mints a new URL and re-registers the relay. An unauthenticated `401`/`403` answer still counts as alive, because that is a healthy round trip to a harness that has not been paired yet. #### Keeping the ingress port in sync (optional, update-only) A named tunnel's hostname is permanent, but its ingress rule names a fixed local port (`http://127.0.0.1:3080` above). When `dsh web` later listens on another port — an operator `--port`, another profile, a second instance on the old one — the hostname still resolves and answers 502 while everything in this plugin still believes the address is published. Turn on **Cloudflare config sync** (`ingressSync`) with an account-level API token (`cfApiToken`), the `cfAccountId` and the `cfTunnelId`, and the plugin keeps that one number following the port it actually bound: - one read on start; the document is written only when the matched rule's service has drifted from the bound port; - only the `service` of the rule whose hostname exactly equals `publicBaseUrl`'s host is touched — one full-document PUT, because the API has no single-rule patch, with every other rule and every top-level key proven identical first; - a document it cannot prove that about is reported and never written: a missing or duplicated hostname, a wildcard anywhere, an `ingress` that is not an array, a missing catch-all, a service that is not an http(s) origin, or a service hosted anywhere but on this machine — only loopback literals (127.0.0.0/8, `::1`, `localhost`) and this host's own LAN addresses are retargeted, so a neighbour's address or a DNS name is never touched. No rule is added and no catch-all is invented; - the write is read back once. A disagreement is a conflict and stops there: one tunnel document has one writer, so a deployment whose dashboard or another sync owns it is reconciled by hand; - the bound port is the target: before the listener binds nothing is requested (the same settle re-plan that starts the quick tunnel delivers it), and the tunnel token's own format is never parsed. The state frame reports `off`/`waiting`/`applied`/`failed`/`conflict` with the hostname, the port, the two service strings and the reason, and the settings card renders it beside the switch. The quick tunnel takes precedence: with `autoTunnel` on there is no named tunnel to update and the sync reads as off. ### Manual tunnels (bring your own) Expose the local port with any tunnel and set **公网地址** (publicBaseUrl), e.g.: ```sh # 1. Expose the local port (whatever dsh web is listening on): cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:3080 # prints something like: https://xxxx-xxxx-xxxx.trycloudflare.com # 2. Start dsh web as usual. Do not add --trusted-host for the tunnel # domain unless you intentionally want the SDK to trust that host for # /api. Keep the LAN bind off if only tunnel access is wanted. ``` Then set the printed URL as 公网地址. The QR link is built from it, and the plugin's pairing fence accepts the tunneled authority. The posture probe keeps auditing which `/api` authorities the SDK fence leaves open. ## Development Work from this repository (no sibling checkout needed): ```sh cd dsh-web export NPM_TOKEN='' # only if private @deepseek-ai auth is still required pnpm install pnpm --filter @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui run build pnpm --filter @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui test pnpm --filter @linxin666/dsh-remote-web-ui run typecheck ``` The peer APIs come from the official NPM SDK: every `@deepseek-ai/*` package used here is declared in devDependencies (0.2.1-rc.3 cohort), and TypeScript/Vitest resolve types straight from node_modules — no DSH source checkout is required. The consumer-side `prepare` build (`tsdown.prepare.config.ts`) transpiles without type checking, so git installs work without any harness checkout either. ## Checks ```sh pnpm run typecheck pnpm test pnpm run build ``` ## Harness contract dependencies Pinned to the 0.2.1-rc.3 line; the seams this build relies on: - **`sidebar.footer.action` foot seat** (the 0.1.7 shell composition): the sidebar declares and renders the seat the remote entry occupies. - **`ctx.layout.toggleSidebar()`** (packages/client/ui-layout): the whale button expands the collapsed sidebar through the official panel-action face. - **`ctx.connection.authenticatedUrl()`** (packages/client/connection): the sanctioned launch-token seam the proxy redeems once for its inner credential (`src/inner-auth.ts`), so re-issued `/api` calls satisfy the harness browser-auth check. - **`__DSH_FILE_UPLOAD__`** (file-upload client hooks): the optional pre-Cordis transport the upload service reads once at construction. The remote boot patch publishes it so background uploads stay on the rewritten main-thread fetch instead of a Web Worker that escapes the channel (issue #1580). - **`__DSH_TRANSPORT__.ownsHost`** (client-connection transport hooks): the host-mode flip for paired remote desktops. It is installed only when the device-gated app landing published the `__DSH_REMOTE_HOST_GRANT__` marker ahead of the boot patch, so the flip is server-granted rather than asserted from the origin. There is no host-side per-method privilege pin on this line — the configuration plane branches on `connection.isLoopback` in the client — and no `api/gate` waterfall either (the gate listener stays mounted for deployments that gain the seam; pairing enforcement lives on this plugin's own `/remote` channel). - **Web server bind ownership**: the profile's `- id: webserver` row belongs to the official bundle and this plugin never writes it — same-id patch rows replace a row's config wholesale, and the user patch layer cannot evaluate `webStartup`-dependent `!!js` expressions reliably, so the row keeps `host: !!js ctx.webStartup.host ?? '127.0.0.1'` and `--host`/`--port` reach it. LAN reachability is runtime state instead: the forwarder in `src/lan-forward.ts` listens on the LAN interface at the web server's actual port and re-issues to `127.0.0.1` on the same port. The fence helpers (`isTrustedApiRequest` / `isLoopbackHostname`) are reimplemented locally in `src/gate.ts` / `src/routes.ts`: the connection plugin stopped exporting them, so the pairing routes carry their own copy scoped to the literals the QR links advertise. The loopback question is split in two there: `isLoopbackUpstream` (loopback socket and Host, forwarding headers ignored) only decides whether a Host can be answered at all, while `isLoopbackClient` (no forwarding header) decides who receives a credential or the desktop payload. The shared copy in `shared/host/loopback.ts` keeps `isLoopbackRequest` refusing every forwarded request and adds `isForwardedLoopbackRequest` for the narrower shape a route family may admit behind its own default-off switch. ## Manual E2E: LAN pairing round trip The unit/component specs cover the route family, the gate, the channel, the LAN forwarder with its status frame, and the adaptation layer, but the pairing loop involves a real browser on a non-loopback origin. Repeat this after any change to the wire contract or the connection loop: 1. Start an isolated instance: `DSH_HOME=/tmp/dsh-qa dsh --profile web --no-open --port 3191`; open the card at `http://127.0.0.1:3191`, flip **局域网访问** on, and confirm the card reports the forwarder listening on the machine's LAN IPv4 at 3191. 2. Open the **loopback** URL (`http://127.0.0.1:3191`) in a browser: the phone icon sits in the sidebar foot; the panel mints a QR whose link is `/pair-accept?pair=`. With a public base configured the link names that origin instead — reachable from anywhere — and the landing does the network choice described under **Use**. 3. In a sec

# dsh-session-archive · Full-Text Session Search, Batch Archiving & Lifecycle Manager for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) English | [中文](README.zh.md)

   

Full-Text Session Search, Batch Archiving & Lifecycle Manager for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
Centralized Session View · Faceted Search & Filtering · Batch Archive & Cascade Delete · Automated Retention Rules

A comprehensive session lifecycle and archive management plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI and official desktop client: centralized session inventory, batch archive/unarchive, and verifiable cascade physical deletion pipelines with disk space reclamation. Optional automated policies automatically archive inactive sessions and prune expired archives based on retention schedules. ## What it does - **Complete inventory**: every session the host can see — active, archived, blank, sub-agent, workspace-less, and historical sessions with incomplete metadata — with title, session ID, workspace, last activity, status, archive time (or an explicit "unknown"), size, and child-session counts. - **Filter, search, sort**: by status (all / unarchived / archived), workspace (including no workspace), title or ID search, last-activity / archive-time / creation-time / title / size sorting, and a "sessions with issues" quick filter. The result count is always shown. - **True multi-select**: per-row checkboxes, per-workspace select/deselect, and select-all that covers the complete filtered result set — not just rendered rows. Selection is kept across filter changes with an explicit note when selected items fall outside the current filter. - **Batch operations**: archive, unarchive, and physical delete over the selected set, executed as bounded server-side chunks with live progress, per-session results (success / skipped with reason / failed with reason), and a retry-failed-only action. The current session, running sessions, and sessions with running descendants are always protected and skipped with an explanation. - **Physical delete with cascade semantics**: deleting a session also removes its storage (jsonl.zstd directory or session-rdb rows), workspace accounting, archive-set entries, projection cache, and the plugin's archive ledger. Deleting a parent pulls in all descendants; a family containing any protected member is skipped whole — never half-deleted. Deletion requires an explicit confirmation that states the direct count, the cascade count, the final total, the skipped protected count, and the estimated freed space; large deletes require an extra acknowledgement. - **Optional automatic maintenance (off by default)**: auto-archive sessions inactive beyond a threshold (by last-activity time, never creation time) and auto-delete archived sessions past their retention (by the recorded archive time, never file times). Manual and automatic archiving both support bare UUID and `session-`-prefixed IDs, while the archive ledger uses canonical IDs. Both are independent switches with pre-enable previews, run-now buttons, and persisted last-run/next-check status. Sessions archived before this plugin existed have no reliable archive time, are shown as "unknown", and are never auto-deleted unless the optional backfill below is enabled. - **Safe by construction**: all routes are loopback-fenced (tunnels and LAN clients get 403), deletion never follows symlinks outside the sessions root, and operations serialize so two batches can never interleave. ## Install ```sh pnpm add @linxin666/dsh-session-archive ``` The family bundle (`dsh-web-all`) includes this plugin. For a standalone profile mount: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-web/packages/dsh-session-archive ``` Restart `dsh web`. The plugin adds its own Archived sessions Settings entry: it seats the plugin's own `settings.section` id (`dsh-session-archive`) at nav order (25), carrying this plugin's management surface. The section opens on the archived view. The section id is deliberately this plugin's own namespace rather than the official `archived-sessions` id. The settings shell renders one nav row per registration and never merges same-id sections, and its registry refuses a second registration of the same `id` at the same `priority` (default 0) while `order` only sorts the rows. Two archive plugins claiming the same section id therefore collide whatever order they pick: one registration throws, or one of the two entries silently disappears. With its own id the entry coexists with the official Archived sessions page and with any third-party archive plugin, one entry each. A standalone install, or an install with no other archive plugin enabled, shows this single entry. ## Configuration The settings section exposes: - `enabled` — turn the whole management surface off. - `autoArchiveEnabled` + `autoArchiveDays` (1–3650, default 7) — auto-archive threshold by last activity. - `autoDeleteEnabled` + `autoDeleteDays` (1–3650, default 7) — archive retention before physical deletion. - `recordManualArchive` (default off) — backfill an archive time for sessions archived outside this plugin; see below. - `checkIntervalMin` (15–1440, default 60) — scheduler cadence for the automatic checks. Invalid or out-of-range values are never saved; the form shows a validation message. ## Semantics you should know - **Archiving never deletes data.** An archived session only disappears from grouping surfaces; unarchiving restores it with its workspace slot intact. - **Physical delete is unrecoverable.** It removes the session history, metadata, workspace association, archive records, projection cache, and other session-owned data. Shared, content-addressed attachments are left alone (they may be referenced by other sessions); orphaned attachment objects are not garbage-collected by this plugin. - **Archive times are recorded by this plugin.** The archive ledger (`$DSH_HOME/dsh-session-archive/archive-ledger.json`) stays the only archive-time fact source; no file timestamp is ever used. Sessions archived before installation — including sessions archived from the official sidebar, which never reaches this plugin — show "archive time unknown" and stay outside auto-delete until a human deletes them, they are unarchived and re-archived (which restarts the retention clock), or the backfill below records a time for them. - **`recordManualArchive` is a backfill, off by default.** When enabled, the first time this plugin observes a session that is already archived with no ledger entry, it records one `observed` entry stamped with the observation moment, so the retention countdown starts from there and the session can later be auto-deleted. The observation moment is a lower bound, not the real archive moment, and the list marks it "(backfilled)" to keep the two distinguishable. The backfill never deletes in the same cycle that records a time: the existing rule that ignores archive times at or after the run start keeps the row out of that cycle. With the switch off, nothing is written to the ledger and behaviour is exactly as before. - **Auto-starting the clock is a deliberate trade.** A session archived long ago gets a countdown that starts now, not its real age; the backfill can therefore never delete something that was archived more recently than the retention window. - **Protected sessions are never deleted, manually or automatically**: running sessions, the session you are currently viewing, sessions with running children, and sessions already inside another archive operation. Forced stops never happen. ## Security model All HTTP routes (`/api/dsh-session-archive/*`) are fenced to loopback sockets with a loopback Host header and browser same-origin markers; `X-Forwarded-For` is never trusted. Deletion resolves storage paths only through the plugin's own sessions-root index, re-validates realpaths before removal, and rejects anything outside `$DSH_HOME/sessions`. Clients send session IDs only — never file paths. The session-rdb store (SQLite) is fingerprint-checked before any row deletion. ## Known limitations - Remote-browser users (LAN or `dsh-remote-web-ui` tunnels) cannot operate this section; every route is loopback-only by design, because it can destroy local session data. - Sessions missing from the host feed and the projection cache are flagged "incomplete metadata" and excluded from automatic flows. - Attachments under `$DSH_HOME/attachments` are shared and content-addressed; this plugin does not reclaim orphaned ones. # dsh-web · DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI 插件与主题全家桶 中文 | [English](README.en.md) dsh-web 是面向 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）Web GUI、DeepSeek 网页版与官方桌面客户端（DeepSeek Desktop）的模块化插件生态与 AI 智能体开发工作台。全面支持 DeepSeek-V3 与 DeepSeek-R1 等前沿推理模型，为开发者与重度用户提供自主任务自动化看板（Cron 定时后台执行）、手机 App 远程访问、Web SSH 终端与 Linux 集群运维、Git 可视化提交图谱与多 Agent Worktree 隔离开发、全量会话检索与归档管理、Token 用量与成本监控（含 Token 银行），以及一站式主题皮肤与桌面宠物工坊。用户既可以通过官方 profile 机制将插件全家桶一键挂载至已有的 `dsh web` 实例，也可以直接在官方 DeepSeek Harness 桌面客户端中开箱即用。

事务账本为权威持久化核心，真正实现了长程任务从拆解、分发、团队协作、对抗质检到外部成果闭环的全流程自动化： - **宿主权威后台驱动与 7x24 小时离线无人值守**：区别于传统仅在前端网页轮询的脆弱看板，所有卡片流转、调度触发与执行监控完全由 DSH 后端 Host - **对抗式双盲质量验收门禁（No False Completion）**：彻底终结 AI 编程中“自述已完成、实则未改动或改崩溃”的虚假交付顽疾。以 goal 形式执行的任务在 Agent 试图调用 `update_goal(complete)` 宣告完工的瞬间被 Host 强制拦截，必须由独立的裁判模型（可自选模型与思考档位）进行真实验收。验收机制沿用严苛的 Coding 质量判据、0.65 绝对通过阈值，每项判据双轮交换 A/B 位置打分消偏，并严格结合会话执行轨迹与宿主工作区真实磁盘文件的 Diff 行级变更审查。首轮未达标精准下发具象结构化问题引导 Agent 自我修复，两次仍不通过才判负，杜绝敷衍糊弄。 - **全自动 GitHub Issue-to-PR 闭环研发流**：搭配官方扩展（`dsh-client-ui-task-board-github`），实现任务看板与 GitHub Issues / PR 状态的实时双向深度同步。远端 Issue 自动进入看板流水线驱动 Agent 读取需求、定位代码、修复 Bug 并运行测试，验收交付后全自动创建 GitHub Pull Request 并绑定 Issue 关联，PR 合并后自动关闭 Issue，打造全天候无人值守的开源与企业 Issue 自动化修复交付管线。 - **长程目标驱动、会话持久化与冻结交接包（Freeze Handover）**：任务支持武装内置 `/goal` 引擎进行多轮自主续跑；周期性任务可开启会话复用，保留完整上下文记忆；支持通过 `<< Agent 预设”中选用。梁神模式（`dsh-liangshen`）是专为追求**极致推理效率、超低静态上下文开销与严苛工程执行纪律**而深度重构的杀手级预设与运行时插件。针对主流大模型在长程编程任务中容易出现的系统提示词冗长膨胀、工具 Schema 挤占上下文、思维链无效空转（如“流水账推理”）以及多轮遗忘退化等痛点，梁神模式通过原生极简提示词、程序化代码工具调用（PTC）、MCP 温和分页与关键事实局部就近投射，提供纯粹而强悍的编程作战体验： - **极简 Persona 与严苛行动导向纪律（Zero Prompt Waste）**：彻底剥离官方 Standard 预设中冗长繁琐的系统级条文，将提示词极致收敛为单行 Persona 与经过实战千锤百炼的高效工程纪律。内置反思熔断（同一假设推演不超过两轮，缺少事实立即闭合思考并调用原生工具探测，杜绝凭空揣测）、行动导向（思考过程仅用于决定下一步具体操作，严禁在思考中预演完整代码）、并发探索（单轮内并发派发多个独立检测或搜索工具）、YAGNI 与 PDCA 循环（单步验证单一假设，不写冗余注水注释）、以及有界收敛纪律（前置检查最多 2-3 轮即刻收敛，迅速转入实际作答或编辑）。大幅降低静态 Token 占用，让模型注意力百分之百倾注于业务与代码本身。 - **程序化工具调用传输（PTC · Programmatic Tool Calling）**：彻底终结在每次请求中平铺上百个 JSON Schema 工具参数的低效模式。默认将网络线协议（wire）极致收拢为唯一的 `run_code`（运行 TypeScript 脚本），其余所有工具均通过自动生成的强类型 SDK 在独立的沙箱线程中以代码形式调用。无论系统注册了多少复杂工具，静态传输面始终保持极小体积；模型可原生利用 `Promise.all` 编写并发工具调用，并在程序内预先过滤、聚合、提取关键数据，只将精炼结论回传至对话上下文，从根本上解决大文本输出打爆 Token 的问题。对于习惯原生工具面的场景，亦可在插件设置中一键无缝切换为组装好的原生工具清单（Native）。 - **MCP 工具温和分页与 LRU 动态激活（Gentle Tool Paging）**：针对海量 MCP 工具或第三方插件扩展，出厂默认启用温和分页（默认匹配 `mcp__*`）。外部工具在初始状态下仅以命名空间摘要形式登记在目录消息中，既不占 wire 协议也不进 SDK 声明；当大模型判定需要使用对应工具时，可自主调用 `tool_activate({ namespace })` 按需挂载。内置 LRU 策略（上限 3 个活跃命名空间），自动淘汰最久未用的命名空间，激活状态在会话压缩与恢复后完整重建，兼具海量工具接入能力与极致小巧的静态 Schema 面。 - **关键事实登记簿与就近状态投射（Fact Register & Working Context）**：长程多轮对话中大模型极易遗忘早期的关键业务约束或踩过的坑。插件向模型提供专属 `fact_register` 工具，可将用户硬性约束、已确认的架构决策或失败路径登记为单行事实（每条不超过 160 字符，最多保留 12 条）。关键事实随 `[Working Context: ...]` 状态行在每一轮交互中就近投射至最新消息尾部的局部注意力窗口内，从物理机制上彻底解决长上下文“中间遗忘”与重复踩坑顽疾。 - **原生调度者架构与敏捷访谈纪律（Dispatcher Identity & Triage）**：预设出厂深度集成调度者（Dispatcher）架构规范，赋能模型以团队指挥官身份统领工程任务。内置复杂度分诊机制（L0/L1 单点任务直接敏捷执行，L2 复杂任务严格遵循“澄清访谈 -> 架构规划 -> 并发子代理派发 -> 双层严格验收”标准流）；设定严格的提问预算控制（单轮最多 4 问、总计最多 3 轮、影响面排序、假设先行），杜绝无效拉扯；任务状态权威沉淀于 `todo_write`，杜绝浮躁的敷衍式交付。 - **新建会话老虎机拨杆与炫酷中奖特效（Composer Slot Lever）**：在新建会话输入框工具行、模型选择器左侧，精心打造了一台复古老虎机拨杆控件。下拉拨杆（支持鼠标拖拽、单击或键盘快捷操作）即可一键为当前新建会话装配梁神模式，拉下命中即触发绚丽的中奖粒子特效（闪光、冲击环、火花粒子与专属彩蛋横幅）；上推即可平滑切回默认模式。拨杆自适应全局主题色彩，且在会话开始后自动隐藏，丝滑灵动，极具极客趣味。 详细机制、评测数据与高级配置参数见 [dsh-liangshen README](packages/dsh-liangshen/README.zh.md)。 ### 手机 App 远程访问（Mobile Remote · 原生手机 App 接入） 在 profile 中安装 `@linxin666/dsh-remote-bridge` 插件并重启服务后，点击侧边栏底部的二维码图标（aria-label 为「配对手机（协议 v1）」）打开配对面板。使用手机 App 扫码即可直接开始使用。 配对面板具备本地安全保护，令牌路由（`/remote-bridge/pair/token`）带有回环门控，仅允许在本机浏览器中访问（非本机访问返回 403）。面板生成的配对码为一次性凭据，有效期为 30 秒，点击「重新取码」将作废上一张配对码。二维码编码包含服务地址与令牌的文档（URL 形如 `wss:///ios/v1?token=...`），手机 App 扫码后即可同时获取服务地址与鉴权令牌。 网络接入协议面仅暴露 `/ios/v1` 一个 WebSocket 端点，隧道与局域网转发均指向仅放行该路径的入站闸门，公网无法直接访问 Web GUI 路由。服务地址按实时状态（中继租约或运行中的隧道）、环境变量 `DSH_REMOTE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` 以及局域网转发器实际监听地址的顺序解析。默认配置下公网可用（中继默认开启、隧道默认关闭、局域网转发默认关闭）；若需在局域网内直连，需在插件配置中开启局域网转发。原浏览器远程控制插件 `dsh-remote-web-ui` 已退役，接入栈能力已迁入本包。 ### 远程连接（SSH Ops · Web 终端、SFTP 传输与集群运维） 通过侧边栏“SSH”入口打开远程运维面板。支持密钥与密码认证，可一键导入本地 `~/.ssh/config` 主机列表；配置数据安全保存在 `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json` 中。面板提供以下操作能力： - **Web 终端**：基于 xterm.js 的完整远程交互终端，支持实时输出与窗口自适应； - **文件传输**：集成 SFTP 上传与下载功能，提供进度提示并支持可视化浏览远程目录； - **端口转发**：支持建立本地到远程内部服务的加密隧道（如内网数据库、后端 API），默认仅监听 127.0.0.1 安全地址； - **集群并发执行**：支持多主机批量命令执行，并可通过别名、运行环境或标签进行过滤； - **Agent 直连调用**：智能体与面板共享主机配置，在会话中发出指令即可委派 Agent 执行远程巡检与运维命令。 ### 使用统计（Usage Statistics · Token 消耗追踪、余额预警与 Token 银行） 在“设置 > 使用统计”中集中查看 token 消耗数据、供应商余额以及编程套餐额度，支持自动定时刷新与手动即时查询。 - **用量明细**：查看每日输入、输出与缓存用量，按不同供应商与模型细分展示，并提供最近 30 天消费趋势；支持的供应商提供账户余额查询，针对 DeepSeek 官方路由还提供峰谷分时计费与账单估算。 - **个人套餐追踪**：实时展示 Kimi、GLM、MiniMax、OpenCode Go、Codex / ChatGPT 等平台编程套餐的使用比例与重置周期。 - **Token 银行**：所有 provider 每消耗 100 万 tokens 铸造 1 鲸元，以“鲸元券”形式展示台账周期内的累计 token 与调用指标，支持保存票券卡片与系统级分享。 - **桌面宠物联动**：安装宠物插件后，可通过桌面悬浮挂件的气泡提示直接查看当前会话供应商的额度、余额或今日消耗。 统计自插件首次启用起计，不回填历史数据；鲸元券统计台账窗口内所有 provider 的 tokens（消费行仍只来自 DeepSeek 官方余额观测）。支持的供应商列表与配置细节见 [dsh-usage README](packages/dsh-usage/README.zh.md)。 ![DeepSeek Token 用量统计与 Token 银行 — API 消耗追踪与账单估算](docs/screenshots/35-usage-token-bank.webp) ### Git 图谱（Git Graph · 分支可视化与 Worktree 会话隔离） 在对话输入框上方集成 Git **安全批量操作**：支持跨筛选结果的多选批量归档、批量恢复以及级联物理删除。执行物理删除时系统将明确提示受影响的后代会话数与预计释放空间，大批量删除需二次确认；当前处于运行中或带有运行中子代理的会话受到严格保护，防止误删； - **自动化生命周期策略**：提供两个默认关闭的自动化策略：根据最后活跃时间自动归档、根据归档时间自动清理超期数据，支持在启用前进行结果预览与单次手动执行。 删除操作不可逆，所有管理路由严格限制本机回环访问。详细机制见 [dsh-session-archive README](packages/dsh-session-archive/README.zh.md)。 ### 更多插件（More Plugins） - **Skill 中心**（`dsh-client-ui-skill-explorer`）：按来源集中查看与管理已加载的 agent `dsh web` 可正常启动。 - npm 安装方式无需额外环境；若从源码仓库构建，需要 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm 环境。 ### 三步上手（npm 安装，推荐） - **DSH Web CLI（现有浏览器服务）**： 1. 先完成三项构建脚本审批（见“安装排障”），再安装聚合包：`dsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-web-all@latest` 2. 重启 `dsh web` 服务，侧边栏将自动呈现各插件入口 3. 打开“设置 > 插件配置”按需开关插件，或在皮肤面板选用主题 - **官方桌面客户端（DeepSeek Harness Desktop）**： 1. 打开官方桌面客户端，进入“设置 → 插件”页面 2. 在插件安装框中输入 `@linxin666/dsh-web-all` 并确认安装 3. 重启客户端，即可在侧边栏与“设置”中使用各插件功能 > 若仅需要皮肤功能，可单独安装 `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-skin-center`。若因包管理器门禁安装到旧版本，请参阅后文“安装排障”。 ### 从 GitHub 仓库直接安装 仓库根目录声明了标准 `dsh.bundle` npm 安装聚合包效果等价，二者择其一即可。请勿同时通过两种方式安装，以免出现 entry id 冲突。 ### 从仓库安装（开发调试） 如需二次开发或调试插件，可按以下步骤从源码构建（要求 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm）： ```sh # 1. 克隆源码仓库 git clone https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web.git cd dsh web 服务 dsh web ``` > 提示：profile 目录未配置为 pnpm workspace，聚合包内部的 `workspace:*` 依赖在解析时会尝试回退拉取 npm 线上版本。若线上包存在版本差异，请先运行 `node scripts/link-profile.mjs` 确保全部子包均指向本地构建产物。 ### 单独安装某个插件 展开查看常见安装与构建排障方案
> **pnpm 严格依赖隔离导致模块找不到**：pnpm 的 isolated 模式默认仅将聚合包放置在顶层，部分子包可能被嵌套收敛，导致 `dsh web` 启动时报错 `Cannot find package '@linxin666/dsh-...'`。若遇到此情况，可在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中添加配置 `nodeLinker: hoisted`（或 `public-hoist-pattern: ['@linxin666/*']`）后重新安装。 > **构建脚本被拦截 (ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS)**：这三项审批必须在首次 add 之前就位。正确顺序是重置 profile（官方 `--from-default-profile web`）或换新 profile，在 `/pnpm-workspace.yaml` 里把三项写成映射，再执行 add： > > ```yaml > allowBuilds: > cloudflared: true > cpu-features: true > ssh2: true > ``` > > 必须写成上面的映射形式：

# dsh-session-id · Instant Session ID Copy & Navigation Helper for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) English | [中文](README.zh.md)

   

Instant Session ID Copy & Navigation Helper for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)
Sidebar Footer Trigger · Real-Time Session ID List · One-Click Clipboard Copy · Instant Local Filter

A browser-only extension for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI and desktop client: provides a quick trigger at the bottom of the sidebar to view full session IDs and copy them with one click. Mounts into `sidebar.footer.action` without modifying DSH source code and incurs zero host overhead. ## What it does - Adds a "Session ID" trigger beside the sidebar settings row: an icon-only button in both the 56px rail and the wide sidebar (the label stays as the accessible name and hover tooltip). - In the rail it stacks vertically with the update/remote actions on the rail centerline; in the wide sidebar it sits inline with them. - Opens a centered panel listing every session: display title, full session id (monospace), and a per-row "Copy" button. The current session is marked. - A search box filters the list locally by title or id substring (read-only, no host query), so finding a session among hundreds stays fast. - Sessions are read from the official `ctx.sessions.list` feed, so the panel stays live as sessions start, finish, or get archived — no refresh needed. - Clicking "Copy" writes the id through the official clipboard helper (`writeClipboard`); the button briefly shows "Copied". ## Install ### From npm (recommended) ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-session-id@latest ``` Restart `dsh web` (or wait for the hot-reload) and click the Session ID entry at the bottom of the sidebar. ### From the repository (development) ```sh git clone https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web.git cd dsh-web pnpm install pnpm -r build dsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)/packages/dsh-session-id ``` ## Security model - A session id is a **locator / automation identifier**, not a credential: it never grants access to the session, its files, or its host. The panel only displays and copies ids; it never writes them to the session log, the agent prompt, or any persistent storage, and it never copies automatically. - Copying is always user-gesture driven; a failed clipboard write shows an actionable "Copy failed, retry" state with no permission request and no background retry. - Sharing a session id can still **expose workflow associations** (titles, run times, and the session's place in the workspace), so copy ids only when you actually need to reference a session elsewhere. ## Known limitations - Requires a DSH shell that declares `sidebar.footer.action` (0.1.0-rc.8 and newer shells). On older shells the entry does not render. - Read-only viewer: it shows and copies ids, it does not open or manage sessions. ## Telemetry The browser half sends one anonymous install heartbeat per UTC day to dsh-market.com: a random localStorage id plus this package's name, nothing else. The server stores only a salted hash of that id, never IP addresses, and exposes aggregate counts only. See [docs/telemetry.md](../../docs/telemetry.md) for the full contract. ## License BSD-3-Clause. # dsh-web · DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI 插件与主题全家桶 中文 | [English](README.en.md) dsh-web 是面向 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）Web GUI、DeepSeek 网页版与官方桌面客户端（DeepSeek Desktop）的模块化插件生态与 AI 智能体开发工作台。全面支持 DeepSeek-V3 与 DeepSeek-R1 等前沿推理模型，为开发者与重度用户提供自主任务自动化看板（Cron 定时后台执行）、手机 App 远程访问、Web SSH 终端与 Linux 集群运维、Git 可视化提交图谱与多 Agent Worktree 隔离开发、全量会话检索与归档管理、Token 用量与成本监控（含 Token 银行），以及一站式主题皮肤与桌面宠物工坊。用户既可以通过官方 profile 机制将插件全家桶一键挂载至已有的 `dsh web` 实例，也可以直接在官方 DeepSeek Harness 桌面客户端中开箱即用。

               

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）Web 插件生态 · 模块化智能体工作台
全功能 Web UI · 任务自动化看板 · 手机 App 远程访问 · Web SSH 运维 · Git 图谱与 Worktree · Token 成本统计 · 视觉工坊

## 是什么 原生 DeepSeek Harness Web 提供了核心的对话交互与工具调用能力，但在多任务并发调度、长程后台执行、移动端协同以及工程化开发运维方面仍有扩展空间。 dsh-web 通过官方 profile 机制挂载到 `dsh web`，零修改侵入官方源码，为用户提供完整的模块化扩展体系： - **工程运维与协同插件**：涵盖长程自动化任务看板（多 Agent 级联/Teams 编排、对抗验收质检与定时调度）、梁神模式（极简 Persona、PTC 代码运行传输与敏捷调度纪律）、手机 App 远程访问、SSH 终端传输、Git 图谱与 worktree 隔离、全量会话归档管理以及模型能力声明编辑器； - **视觉主题与资产解耦**：功能插件与样式资产完全分离。皮肤插件负责底层渲染，多样化的主题皮肤（含样式、贴图与动态特效）以及桌面宠物可通过 [DSH 创意工坊](#创意工坊dsh-marketcom)自由安装； - **全家桶聚合与按需组合**：既支持通过 `@linxin666/dsh-web-all` 聚合包一键安装完整功能，也支持按需单独安装特定插件。聚合包预集成家族全部功能插件，详见[插件全家桶使用指南](packages/dsh-web-all/README.zh.md)。 ![DeepSeek Harness Web GUI 配合 [插件安装快速上手](#快速上手) | ## 官方桌面客户端 对于希望直接使用独立桌面应用的用户，推荐下载并使用官方发布的 DeepSeek Harness 桌面客户端（DeepSeek Harness Desktop）。 官方桌面客户端与 `dsh web` 共用 `~/.dsh` 数据目录，其 profile 为 `desktop`。由于官方桌面客户端对 `desktop` profile 实行应用内专管（外部 CLI 会限制对 `desktop` profile 的修改），安装本插件全家桶时请直接在桌面客户端内进行： 1. 打开官方桌面客户端，进入“设置”中的“插件”页面（或左侧导航栏的插件入口）； 2. 在插件管理界面的安装输入框中，输入插件全家桶包名 `@linxin666/dsh-web-all`（或 `@linxin666/dsh-web-all@latest`），点击安装； 3. 安装完成后重启客户端，即可在客户端中使用任务看板、主题皮肤、远程控制等全套插件能力。 ## 创意工坊（dsh-market.com） [创意工坊](https://dsh-market.com) 是 DSH 生态的一站式资产分发平台，统一提供主题皮肤、桌面宠物、功能插件与社区 Agent 预设。所有项目按照真实设备点赞热度排序，皮肤支持即时试穿预览，插件提供一键安装命令。经典的 Blue Fantasy 蓝色幻想随皮肤插件内置，其余主题皮肤与宠物资产均可在工坊浏览、查看源代码并按需安装。在 Web GUI 的“创意工坊”设置卡中可直接浏览线上清单，皮肤与宠物可一键下载至 DSH 主目录并在对应设置页选用；社区预设下载至本地预设库，启用后即可在“设置 → Agent 预设”中用于新建会话。 ![DeepSeek Harness 创意工坊 dsh-market.com — 主题皮肤、桌面宠物与社区插件市场](docs/screenshots/31-market-home.png) 创意工坊站点为本仓库的组成部分：前端为纯静态构建，由构建脚本 `scripts/market-build` 依据 `skin.json`、`pet.json` 与 `community.json` 等数据源自动生成；点赞等动态能力由 Cloudflare Workers 边缘函数与 D1 数据库提供支持（遵循单设备单票限制），代码合入 `main` 分支后自动触发持续集成部署。 创意工坊旨在建立开放透明的社区生态，方便开发者分享作品并让用户自由选择所需扩展。 ## 功能插件 ### 任务看板（Task Board · 企业级后台长程执行引擎与多 Agent 自动化流水线） 通过侧边栏“任务看板”进入。任务看板不仅仅是一个可视化卡片界面，更是 DeepSeek Harness 官方 Web GUI 与桌面客户端中的**宿主权威后台长程执行与多 Agent 自动化调度引擎**。任务按“待规划、待办、进行中、已完成、已失败”五列进行全生命周期管理，以 Schema v6 事务账本为权威持久化核心，真正实现了长程任务从拆解、分发、团队协作、对抗质检到外部成果闭环的全流程自动化： - **宿主权威后台驱动与 7x24 小时离线无人值守**：区别于传统仅在前端网页轮询的脆弱看板，所有卡片流转、调度触发与执行监控完全由 DSH 后端 Host 进程作为唯一权威驱动。浏览器仅为异步视图，关闭网页标签页、熄灭屏幕或断开网络，后台智能体会话照常并发执行与原子落盘结算。内置跨平台防休眠电源管理（macOS `caffeinate`、Windows `ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED`、带有 systemd-logind 的 Linux `systemd-inhibit`），允许显示器正常关闭的同时阻止整机因闲置休眠，确保夜间无人值守巡检与流水线准时打卡。 - **多 Agent 树状级联并发与原生 Agent Teams 团队编排**：复杂工程目标可自由拆解为多层树状子任务（支持 1~3 层深度，内置环路与深度护栏）。**级联执行模式**通过受控准入队列（runLaunchWidth）并发派生多个独立智能体会话，自动跳过已在完成列的子任务，任一子任务失败自适应收拢整树状态；**原生 Agent Teams 模式**深度对接官方团队服务，启动专属 Team Lead 会话并在其内部为每个子任务动态孵化专属 Teammate，协同工具跨智能体联动，实现真正意义上的多智能体团队协同作战。 - **对抗式双盲质量验收门禁（No False Completion）**：彻底终结 AI 编程中“自述已完成、实则未改动或改崩溃”的虚假交付顽疾。以 goal 形式执行的任务在 Agent 试图调用 `update_goal(complete)` 宣告完工的瞬间被 Host 强制拦截，必须由独立的裁判模型（可自选模型与思考档位）进行真实验收。验收机制沿用严苛的 Coding 质量判据、0.65 绝对通过阈值，每项判据双轮交换 A/B 位置打分消偏，并严格结合会话执行轨迹与宿主工作区真实磁盘文件的 Diff 行级变更审查。首轮未达标精准下发具象结构化问题引导 Agent 自我修复，两次仍不通过才判负，杜绝敷衍糊弄。 - **全自动 GitHub Issue-to-PR 闭环研发流**：搭配官方扩展（`dsh-client-ui-task-board-github`），实现任务看板与 GitHub Issues / PR 状态的实时双向深度同步。远端 Issue 自动进入看板流水线驱动 Agent 读取需求、定位代码、修复 Bug 并运行测试，验收交付后全自动创建 GitHub Pull Request 并绑定 Issue 关联，PR 合并后自动关闭 Issue，打造全天候无人值守的开源与企业 Issue 自动化修复交付管线。 - **长程目标驱动、会话持久化与冻结交接包（Freeze Handover）**：任务支持武装内置 `/goal` 引擎进行多轮自主续跑；周期性任务可开启会话复用，保留完整上下文记忆；支持通过 `<< Agent 预设”中选用。梁神模式（`dsh-liangshen`）是专为追求**极致推理效率、超低静态上下文开销与严苛工程执行纪律**而深度重构的杀手级预设与运行时插件。针对主流大模型在长程编程任务中容易出现的系统提示词冗长膨胀、工具 Schema 挤占上下文、思维链无效空转（如“流水账推理”）以及多轮遗忘退化等痛点，梁神模式通过原生极简提示词、程序化代码工具调用（PTC）、MCP 温和分页与关键事实局部就近投射，提供纯粹而强悍的编程作战体验： - **极简 Persona 与严苛行动导向纪律（Zero Prompt Waste）**：彻底剥离官方 Standard 预设中冗长繁琐的系统级条文，将提示词极致收敛为单行 Persona 与经过实战千锤百炼的高效工程纪律。内置反思熔断（同一假设推演不超过两轮，缺少事实立即闭合思考并调用原生工具探测，杜绝凭空揣测）、行动导向（思考过程仅用于决定下一步具体操作，严禁在思考中预演完整代码）、并发探索（单轮内并发派发多个独立检测或搜索工具）、YAGNI 与 PDCA 循环（单步验证单一假设，不写冗余注水注释）、以及有界收敛纪律（前置检查最多 2-3 轮即刻收敛，迅速转入实际作答或编辑）。大幅降低静态 Token 占用，让模型注意力百分之百倾注于业务与代码本身。 - **程序化工具调用传输（PTC · Programmatic Tool Calling）**：彻底终结在每次请求中平铺上百个 JSON Schema 工具参数的低效模式。默认将网络线协议（wire）极致收拢为唯一的 `run_code`（运行 TypeScript 脚本），其余所有工具均通过自动生成的强类型 SDK 在独立的沙箱线程中以代码形式调用。无论系统注册了多少复杂工具，静态传输面始终保持极小体积；模型可原生利用 `Promise.all` 编写并发工具调用，并在程序内预先过滤、聚合、提取关键数据，只将精炼结论回传至对话上下文，从根本上解决大文本输出打爆 Token 的问题。对于习惯原生工具面的场景，亦可在插件设置中一键无缝切换为组装好的原生工具清单（Native）。 - **MCP 工具温和分页与 LRU 动态激活（Gentle Tool Paging）**：针对海量 MCP 工具或第三方插件扩展，出厂默认启用温和分页（默认匹配 `mcp__*`）。外部工具在初始状态下仅以命名空间摘要形式登记在目录消息中，既不占 wire 协议也不进 SDK 声明；当大模型判定需要使用对应工具时，可自主调用 `tool_activate({ namespace })` 按需挂载。内置 LRU 策略（上限 3 个活跃命名空间），自动淘汰最久未用的命名空间，激活状态在会话压缩与恢复后完整重建，兼具海量工具接入能力与极致小巧的静态 Schema 面。 - **关键事实登记簿与就近状态投射（Fact Register & Working Context）**：长程多轮对话中大模型极易遗忘早期的关键业务约束或踩过的坑。插件向模型提供专属 `fact_register` 工具，可将用户硬性约束、已确认的架构决策或失败路径登记为单行事实（每条不超过 160 字符，最多保留 12 条）。关键事实随 `[Working Context: ...]` 状态行在每一轮交互中就近投射至最新消息尾部的局部注意力窗口内，从物理机制上彻底解决长上下文“中间遗忘”与重复踩坑顽疾。 - **原生调度者架构与敏捷访谈纪律（Dispatcher Identity & Triage）**：预设出厂深度集成调度者（Dispatcher）架构规范，赋能模型以团队指挥官身份统领工程任务。内置复杂度分诊机制（L0/L1 单点任务直接敏捷执行，L2 复杂任务严格遵循“澄清访谈 -> 架构规划 -> 并发子代理派发 -> 双层严格验收”标准流）；设定严格的提问预算控制（单轮最多 4 问、总计最多 3 轮、影响面排序、假设先行），杜绝无效拉扯；任务状态权威沉淀于 `todo_write`，杜绝浮躁的敷衍式交付。 - **新建会话老虎机拨杆与炫酷中奖特效（Composer Slot Lever）**：在新建会话输入框工具行、模型选择器左侧，精心打造了一台复古老虎机拨杆控件。下拉拨杆（支持鼠标拖拽、单击或键盘快捷操作）即可一键为当前新建会话装配梁神模式，拉下命中即触发绚丽的中奖粒子特效（闪光、冲击环、火花粒子与专属彩蛋横幅）；上推即可平滑切回默认模式。拨杆自适应全局主题色彩，且在会话开始后自动隐藏，丝滑灵动，极具极客趣味。 详细机制、评测数据与高级配置参数见 [dsh-liangshen README](packages/dsh-liangshen/README.zh.md)。 ### 手机 App 远程访问（Mobile Remote · 原生手机 App 接入） 在 profile 中安装 `@linxin666/dsh-remote-bridge` 插件并重启服务后，点击侧边栏底部的二维码图标（aria-label 为「配对手机（协议 ### 验证与卸载 安装后重启 `dsh web` 服务，侧边栏出现对应功能图标即代表加载成功；亦可通过执行 `dsh --profile web --dump-config` 检查配置层挂载状态。若侧边栏未刷新出入口，请确认服务进程已彻底重启。 卸载聚合包：`dsh plugin --profile web remove @linxin666/dsh-web-all`，完成后重启 `dsh web` 即可恢复纯净状态。 技术实现细节与挂载原理解析见 [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md)。 ### 安装排障
展开查看常见安装与构建排障方案
> **pnpm 严格依赖隔离导致模块找不到**：pnpm 的 isolated 模式默认仅将聚合包放置在顶层，部分子包可能被嵌套收敛，导致 `dsh web` 启动时报错 `Cannot find package '@linxin666/dsh-...'`。若遇到此情况，可在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中添加配置 `nodeLinker: hoisted`（或 `public-hoist-pattern: ['@linxin666/*']`）后重新安装。 > **构建脚本被拦截 (ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS)**：这三项审批必须在首次 add 之前就位。正确顺序是重置 profile（官方 `--from-default-profile web`）或换新 profile，在 `/pnpm-workspace.yaml` 里把三项写成映射，再执行 add： > > ```yaml > allowBuilds: > cloudflared: true > cpu-features: true > ssh2: true > ``` > > 必须写成上面的映射形式：列表形式会被 pnpm 改写成 `'0': cloudflared` 之类的占位条目，重跑时还会回退已解析的包（`Packages: -10`）。装失败后补审批重跑会 exit 0，但 `dsh.profile.bundles` 仍无该行：静默半挂载，重跑修不回来，需要先 remove 再 add。已带审批的存量 profile 升级不受影响。 > **pnpm 11 发布时间门禁问题**：在包版本发布后的短时间内，pnpm 11 的默认安全策略（`minimumReleaseAge`）可能会尝试回退拉取旧版本。建议在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中排除相关命名空间以确保获取最新版本： > > ```yaml > minimumReleaseAgeExclude: > - '@linxin666/*' > ```
## 兼容性与运行环境 dsh-web 针对主流操作系统、现代化浏览器及网络拓扑进行了深度工程调优与兼容性保障： | 维度 | 支持范围与技术规格 | | --- | --- | | 宿主运行环境 | DeepSeek Harness CLI (`dsh web`)、官方桌面客户端（DeepSeek Harness Desktop） | | 操作系统 | macOS (Apple Silicon M 系列 & Intel 芯片)、Windows 10/11 (含 WSL2)、Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch, CentOS 等) | | 浏览器与设备 | 桌面浏览器 (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox)；移动端现代浏览器 (iOS Safari, Android Chrome 等) | | 网络连接架构 | 本机环回访问 (127.0.0.1)、局域网多设备互联 (LAN)、公网隧道安全穿透 (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale, FRP, Nginx 反向代理) | | 模型供应商覆盖 | DeepSeek 官方通道与满血模型、OpenAI (GPT-4o 等)、Anthropic Claude、Google Gemini、Kimi (Moonshot)、GLM (智谱)、MiniMax、Ollama 本地大模型、SiliconFlow 等 | | 运行时依赖 | npm 方式安装无特殊环境依赖；源码编译需 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm >= 9 | ## 常见问题
安装重启后，侧边栏未显示插件入口？ 请首先检查插件是否正确安装至 `web` profile（命令需包含 `--profile web`），并通过 `dsh --profile web --dump-config` 验证配置层是否已成功挂载。注意仅刷新网页无法加载新模块，必须彻底重启 `dsh web` 后端服务进程。
定时任务为何未能按时触发执行？ 任务调度完全由 `dsh web` 后端宿主进程驱动，无需保持前端浏览器页面打开。若宿主进程退出、系统关机或整机进入深度睡眠，错过的触发时间点将遵循跳过策略处理，不执行回填补跑；若任务到达触发点时上一轮仍在运行，会自动顺延至下一个周期。若需要允许息屏但防止主机自动睡眠，可开启任务看板自带的电源保护选项。
手机 App 配对后为何没有收到流式推送？ 手机 App 通过协议 v1 的 WebSocket 通道与宿主通信。隧道或中继中断期间流式更新暂停，网络恢复后连接会自动重连；更新节奏的差异主要来自广域网往返延迟。
试穿主题皮肤不满意如何还原？ 皮肤面板提供免落盘试穿功能：点击试穿即刻在当前界面生效预览，离开面板或关闭预览会自动恢复初始外观；只有显式点击“应用”按钮才会将主题配置写入磁盘，可放心预览各类主题。
是否可以仅使用主题皮肤或某个单一插件？ 完全支持。若仅需要视觉定制，直接安装 `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-skin-center` 即可；若仅需特定功能，参考“单独安装某个插件”章节直接安装对应 npm 包即可。
已安装全家桶的前提下，能否额外独立安装某个子插件？ 可以。聚合包内部的插件注册标识均统一带有 `web-ui-` 前缀（例如 `web-ui-usage`），与独立包的原生标识（如 `usage`）相互独立，不会产生 loader entry 重复冲突。宿主服务对同类插件会自动去重。通常情况下安装全家桶即可满足完整需求，无需重复安装单个子包。
如何通过手机 App 远程访问 DeepSeek Harness？是否必须在同一 Wi-Fi 下？ 手机远程访问由协议 v1 支撑，不要求必须处于同一 Wi-Fi。默认配置下插件已开启公网中继服务，在电脑端点击侧栏底部的二维码图标打开配对面板后，使用手机 App 扫码即可直接通过公网连接；亦可配置 Cloudflare 隧道。若希望在同一局域网内直连访问，需在插件配置中开启局域网转发并扫码配对。
关闭浏览器或电脑休眠后，DeepSeek 的定时任务还会继续运行吗？ 任务调度完全由 `dsh web` 后端宿主进程驱动，关闭浏览器标签页不影响定时任务的触发与执行。但如果整机进入深度睡眠或关机，宿主进程将暂停运行，离线期间错过的触发点会遵循跳过策略处理。若希望保持无人值守后台自动化，可在任务看板设置中开启“电源保护”选项，该选项会阻止系统因空闲进入休眠（允许显示器正常熄灭），确保定时任务准时触发。
如何查看和监控 DeepSeek 及其他模型 API 的 Token 消耗与账户余额？ 安装使用统计插件后，在“设置 > 使用统计”面板中可查看按日汇总的输入、输出与缓存 Token 数量，支持按模型细分查看 30 天消费趋势。针对 DeepSeek 官方路由还提供峰谷分时计费估算；若配置了支持查询余额的供应商 API，插件可定时拉取当前账户剩余额度与重置周期。
多个 AI 智能体（Agent）并发编码时，如何避免 Git 分支和代码冲突？ 直接在单一 Git 工作区并发运行多个智能体容易导致代码互相覆盖。使用全家桶内置的 Git 图谱插件，可以在新建会话时自动或手动创建独立的 Git Worktree。每个智能体会话在各自专属的分支和物理目录中独立运行、提交修改，彻底隔绝主工作区文件，开发完成后可在图谱面板中清晰比对并合并分支。
## 已知限制 - 任务看板由后端 Host 进程统一调度，关闭前端标签页不影响任务执行；但若宿主进程停止或操作系统关机睡眠，处于离线期间的触发点将直接跳过不补跑。可选的电源保护仅阻止系统闲置睡眠，无法阻止用户主动合盖、手动休眠或电源切断，技术细节见 [dsh-task-board README](packages/dsh-task-board/README.zh.md)。 - SSH 凭据（密码与私钥口令）保存在本地 `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json` 文件中（文件权限为 0600）；在网络中断重连时可能重新发送非幂等命令，终端输出保持原样返回不执行脱敏，安全规范见 [dsh-ssh README](packages/dsh-ssh/README.zh.md)。 - 手机 App 流式交互经隧道或中继转发，广域网往返延迟叠加在每次更新上；固定域名中继比裸快速隧道多一跳，两者均可使用。 - 从源码构建全仓需要 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm 工具链，直接从 npm 安装不受此限制。 ## 社区 欢迎加入社区交流群，与开发者及其他用户探讨使用技巧、反馈使用问题或提出新功能建议。 扫描下方二维码加入“DSH Web 交流群”： 也可以通过 [Discord 社区](https://discord.gg/6v4gm9u4S) 进行交流，或前往 [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web/issues) 提交缺陷报告与功能需求。 ### 关键词索引（Keywords & Topics） `DeepSeek` · `DeepSeek Harness` · `DSH` · `DeepSeek Web` · `DeepSeek Web UI` · `DeepSeek 网页版` · `DeepSeek 桌面客户端` · `DeepSeek Desktop` · `DeepSeek-V3` · `DeepSeek-R1` · `DeepSeek 插件` · `DeepSeek 扩展` · `DeepSeek 任务看板` · `DeepSeek 定时任务` · `DeepSeek Cron 自动化` · `DeepSeek 手机版` · `DeepSeek 远程控制` · `DeepSeek 手机 App` · `DeepSeek SSH 终端` · `DeepSeek 服务器运维` · `DeepSeek Token 统计` · `DeepSeek 余额查询` · `DeepSeek API 费用` · `Token 银行` · `DeepSeek 主题` · `DeepSeek 皮肤` · `DeepSeek 动态壁纸` · `Wallpaper Engine` · `DeepSeek 桌面宠物` · `DeepSeek Git 图谱` · `DeepSeek Worktree 隔离` · `DeepSeek 会话归档` · `多智能体协作` · `AI Agent 工作台` · `AI 编程助手` · `开源智能体` ### 友情链接 - [LINUX DO](https://linux.do) —— 有理想的新社区。 - [dshfind](https://dshfind.com) —— 面向 DeepSeek Harness 的学习与分享社区，聚合论文精读、插件超市与用户排名。 ## 商务合作 欢迎各类技术交流、生态集成、定制开发与商业合作。如有合作意向，欢迎通过邮件联系我们：[chunlinzhu666@gmail.com](mailto:chunlinzhu666@gmail.com)。 ## 参与贡献 - 提交代码前请查阅 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)；涉及用户界面的修改请附带测试用例或验证截图； - 提交信息严格遵循 Conventional Commits 规范（例如 `fix(task-board): 修复状态同步问题`），代码、文档与 commit 信息全程杜绝使用 emoji； - 新建插件请使用标准脚手架生成：`node scripts/dsh-plugin-new `；新建皮肤请在 [dsh
